blocks.text: The competition challenges teams of university students to conceive, design, fabricate, develop and compete with small formula style race cars.

rules.display_text: The competition challenges teams of university students to conceive, design, fabricate, develop and compete with small formula style race cars.

blocks.text: The competition is split into the following classes:
Internal Combustion Engine Vehicle (CV) including Combustion Hybrid Vehicle (HY)
Electric Vehicle (EV)

rules.display_text:
The competition is split into the following classes:
▪ Internal Combustion Engine Vehicle (CV) including Combustion Hybrid Vehicle (HY)
▪ Electric Vehicle (EV)

blocks.text: All vehicles must meet the requirements defined in chapters T and either EV or CV , depending on their drivetrain type.

rules.display_text: All vehicles must meet the requirements defined in chapters T and either EV or CV , depending on their drivetrain type.

blocks.text: The competition starts with Technical Inspection, described in chapter IN , to check the vehicle for safety and compliance with the rules.

rules.display_text: The competition starts with Technical Inspection, described in chapter IN , to check the vehicle for safety and compliance with the rules.

blocks.text: The competition is divided into a series of static and dynamic disciplines described in chapters S and D .

rules.display_text: The competition is divided into a series of static and dynamic disciplines described in chapters S and D .

blocks.text: The achievable points in each class are listed in Table 1.

rules.display_text: The achievable points in each class are listed in Table 1.

blocks.text: Vehicles of both classes can take part in an additional Driverless Cup (DC).

rules.display_text: Vehicles of both classes can take part in an additional Driverless Cup (DC).

blocks.text: The maximum achievable points for the DC are listed in Table 1.

rules.display_text: The maximum achievable points for the DC are listed in Table 1.

blocks.text: Each discipline’s points and the overall points are bounded by 0 ≤𝑃team ≤𝑃max, where 𝑃team is the points achieved by the team including penalties and 𝑃max is the maximum achievable points for the respective discipline or overall.

rules.display_text:
Each discipline’s points and the overall points are bounded by 0 ≤𝑃team ≤𝑃max, where 𝑃team is the points achieved by the team including penalties and 𝑃max is the maximum achievable points for the respective discipline or overall.

changelog: Added explicit bounds for points

blocks.text: The team with the most overall points wins the competition for its class or the DC, respectively.

rules.display_text: The team with the most overall points wins the competition for its class or the DC, respectively.

blocks.text: The official language of the competition is English.

rules.display_text: The official language of the competition is English.

blocks.text: Every organizer of an event based on this document bears the sole responsibility.

rules.display_text: Every organizer of an event based on this document bears the sole responsibility.

blocks.text: The event specific rules and information are defined in the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: The event specific rules and information are defined in the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: Vehicles entered into the competition must be conceived, designed and maintained by the student team members without direct involvement from external professional engineers, racers, machinists or related professionals.

rules.display_text: Vehicles entered into the competition must be conceived, designed and maintained by the student team members without direct involvement from external professional engineers, racers, machinists or related professionals.

blocks.text: The student team may use any information from professionals or from academics as long as the information is given as a discussion of alternatives with their pros and cons.

rules.display_text: The student team may use any information from professionals or from academics as long as the information is given as a discussion of alternatives with their pros and cons.

blocks.text: Professionals must not make design decisions or drawings.

rules.display_text: Professionals must not make design decisions or drawings.

blocks.text: Students should perform fabrication tasks wherever possible.

rules.display_text: Students should perform fabrication tasks wherever possible.

blocks.text: A vehicle may only be used for one year, counting from the first day on site of its first event.

rules.display_text: A vehicle may only be used for one year, counting from the first day on site of its first event.

blocks.text: To be classified as new, a vehicle must have a newly manufactured chassis.

rules.display_text: To be classified as new, a vehicle must have a newly manufactured chassis.

blocks.text: In the following cases, the existing chassis may be used for one more consecutive year:
Changing the powertrain from CV → EV or CV → HY or HY → EV
Initial implementation of an Autonomous System, see T 14
The team must inform the officials ahead of time if they intend to use this exception.

rules.display_text:
In the following cases, the existing chassis may be used for one more consecutive year:
▪ Changing the powertrain from CV → EV or CV → HY or HY → EV
▪ Initial implementation of an Autonomous System, see T 14
The team must inform the officials ahead of time if they intend to use this exception.

blocks.text: The officials reserve the right to revise the schedule of the event and/or interpret or modify the event or competition rules at any time and in any manner that is, in their sole judgment, required for safe and efficient operation.

rules.display_text: The officials reserve the right to revise the schedule of the event and/or interpret or modify the event or competition rules at any time and in any manner that is, in their sole judgment, required for safe and efficient operation.

blocks.text: All team members are required to cooperate with, and follow all instructions from the officials.

rules.display_text: All team members are required to cooperate with, and follow all instructions from the officials.

blocks.text: Official announcements are considered part of these rules.

rules.display_text: Official announcements are considered part of these rules.

blocks.text: All guidelines and clarifications posted in the “Rules and Important Documents” sections on the competition website for the current season including the Event Handbook are considered part of these rules.

rules.display_text: All guidelines and clarifications posted in the “Rules and Important Documents” sections on the competition website for the current season including the Event Handbook are considered part of these rules.

blocks.text: Failure of a team member to follow an instruction or command directed specifically to that team or team member results in 25 penalty points being deducted from the team’s overall score.

rules.display_text: Failure of a team member to follow an instruction or command directed specifically to that team or team member results in 25 penalty points being deducted from the team’s overall score.

blocks.text: Argument with, or disobedience to, any official results in penalty points for the team up to the team being disqualified from the event.

rules.display_text: Argument with, or disobedience to, any official results in penalty points for the team up to the team being disqualified from the event.
changelog: Clarified rule

blocks.text: In the event of unsportsmanlike conduct, 25 penalty points are deducted from the team’s overall score. A second violation results in the team’s disqualification from the event and its immediate expulsion from the event site.

rules.display_text: In the event of unsportsmanlike conduct, 25 penalty points are deducted from the team’s overall score. A second violation results in the team’s disqualification from the event and its immediate expulsion from the event site.
changelog: Unified wording for disqualification

blocks.text: Violation of the intent of a rule is considered a violation of the rule itself.

rules.display_text: Violation of the intent of a rule is considered a violation of the rule itself.

blocks.text: Any part, device or software fragment designed with the intent to violate a rule is considered a violation.

rules.display_text: Any part, device or software fragment designed with the intent to violate a rule is considered a violation.

blocks.text: Violations according to A 3.5.2 result in a minimum of 100 penalty points being deducted from the team’s overall score up to disqualification from the event.

rules.display_text: Violations according to A 3.5.2 result in a minimum of 100 penalty points being deducted from the team’s overall score up to disqualification from the event.
changelog: Added explicit penalty for intent-violation

blocks.text: Questions about the rules may be asked to the officials.

rules.display_text: Questions about the rules may be asked to the officials.

blocks.text: The frequently asked questions (FAQ) section on the competition website must be checked before submitting a question.

rules.display_text: The frequently asked questions (FAQ) section on the competition website must be checked before submitting a question.

blocks.text: The officials only answer questions that are not already answered in the rules or FAQs or that require new or novel interpretation.

rules.display_text: The officials only answer questions that are not already answered in the rules or FAQs or that require new or novel interpretation.

blocks.text: Refer to the competition website for specific directions how to submit a rules question.

rules.display_text: Refer to the competition website for specific directions how to submit a rules question.

blocks.text: A team may protest any rule interpretation, score or official action which they feel has caused some actual, non-trivial, harm to their team, or has had a substantive effect on their score.

rules.display_text: A team may protest any rule interpretation, score or official action which they feel has caused some actual, non-trivial, harm to their team, or has had a substantive effect on their score.

blocks.text: All protests must be submitted in writing as defined in the Event Handbook by the team captain within the announced protest period. In order to have a protest considered, a team must post a protest bond of 25 points which is forfeited if their protest is rejected.

rules.display_text: All protests must be submitted in writing as defined in the Event Handbook by the team captain within the announced protest period. In order to have a protest considered, a team must post a protest bond of 25 points which is forfeited if their protest is rejected.

blocks.text: The decision of the officials regarding any protest is in a written form and is final.

rules.display_text: The decision of the officials regarding any protest is in a written form and is final.

blocks.text: Rule violations result in at least 20 penalty points, unless explicitly defined otherwise. The penalty points are deducted from the team’s overall score.

rules.display_text: Rule violations result in at least 20 penalty points, unless explicitly defined otherwise. The penalty points are deducted from the team’s overall score.

blocks.text: Overall penalties apply to CV, EV and DC score, except for penalties concerning disciplines which are not part of the respective class or cup.

rules.display_text: Overall penalties apply to CV, EV and DC score, except for penalties concerning disciplines which are not part of the respective class or cup.

rules.title: Code of Conduct
changelog: Added Code of Conduct

blocks.text: A Code of Conduct is published in the “Rules and Important Documents” section of the competition website. It forms part of these rules, see A 3.1.4.

rules.display_text: A Code of Conduct is published in the “Rules and Important Documents” section of the competition website. It forms part of these rules, see A 3.1.4.

blocks.text: The Code of Conduct applies to every person present at the event in any capacity, for the whole duration of the event and in every setting connected with it, including accommodation and campsites, transfers, social and evening activities, and official online channels.

rules.display_text: The Code of Conduct applies to every person present at the event in any capacity, for the whole duration of the event and in every setting connected with it, including accommodation and campsites, transfers, social and evening activities, and official online channels.

blocks.text: Acceptance of the Code of Conduct is a condition of team registration and of individual accreditation.

rules.display_text: Acceptance of the Code of Conduct is a condition of team registration and of individual accreditation.

blocks.text: Alleged breaches of the Code of Conduct are dealt with under the procedure set out in that document. The protest procedure, see A 3.7.2, does not apply to them, and no protest bond is required. The objection procedure of the Code of Conduct applies instead.

rules.display_text: Alleged breaches of the Code of Conduct are dealt with under the procedure set out in that document. The protest procedure, see A 3.7.2, does not apply to them, and no protest bond is required. The objection procedure of the Code of Conduct applies instead.

blocks.text: Team captains must ensure that every team member has read the Code of Conduct before arriving at the event. Dealing with a breach inside the team instead of reporting it is itself a breach.

rules.display_text: Team captains must ensure that every team member has read the Code of Conduct before arriving at the event. Dealing with a breach inside the team instead of reporting it is itself a breach.

blocks.text: Organizers reserve the right to ban an individual, or take action against a team, in case of a serious breach of the Code of Conduct that occurs outside the event, especially if the safety of participants or the reputation of the competition, sponsors or other teams is compromised.

rules.display_text: Organizers reserve the right to ban an individual, or take action against a team, in case of a serious breach of the Code of Conduct that occurs outside the event, especially if the safety of participants or the reputation of the competition, sponsors or other teams is compromised.

blocks.text: A university can register one CV team and one EV team which both can take part in the DC.

rules.display_text: A university can register one CV team and one EV team which both can take part in the DC.

blocks.text: For the purposes of registering and competing, a university’s CV team and EV team are considered to be separate and independent entities.

rules.display_text: For the purposes of registering and competing, a university’s CV team and EV team are considered to be separate and independent entities.

blocks.text: Teams which are formed with members from two or more universities are treated as a single team.

rules.display_text: Teams which are formed with members from two or more universities are treated as a single team.

blocks.text: Each participant must provide proof of valid private liability & individual health insurance for the event.

rules.display_text: Each participant must provide proof of valid private liability & individual health insurance for the event.

blocks.text: All on-site participants must sign a liability waiver upon registering on site which can be found on the competition website.

rules.display_text: All on-site participants must sign a liability waiver upon registering on site which can be found on the competition website.

blocks.text: A team member may only be part of one team, work on one vehicle and take part in static and dynamic disciplines for only one team.

rules.display_text: A team member may only be part of one team, work on one vehicle and take part in static and dynamic disciplines for only one team.

blocks.text: Each team must have one team member identified as the team captain. The team captain is the main contact person for the officials during the registration process and the event.

rules.display_text: Each team must have one team member identified as the team captain. The team captain is the main contact person for the officials during the registration process and the event.

blocks.text: Persons who have previously attended any official event of any competition as a judge are not allowed to participate as team members.

rules.display_text: Persons who have previously attended any official event of any competition as a judge are not allowed to participate as team members.

blocks.text: Team members must be enrolled as degree seeking undergraduate or graduate students in any university. Team members who have graduated within the seven month period before the event remain eligible to participate.

rules.display_text: Team members must be enrolled as degree seeking undergraduate or graduate students in any university. Team members who have graduated within the seven month period before the event remain eligible to participate.

blocks.text: Students seeking a PhD degree/PhD students or equivalent are not allowed to participate.

rules.display_text: Students seeking a PhD degree/PhD students or equivalent are not allowed to participate.

blocks.text: Counting from the year of their first event, team members can only participate for four additional full years. First event is defined as the first registration of a team member for an event by the team captain, irrespective if the team or the team member actually physically participated.

rules.display_text: Counting from the year of their first event, team members can only participate for four additional full years. First event is defined as the first registration of a team member for an event by the team captain, irrespective if the team or the team member actually physically participated.

blocks.text: Team members must be at least 18 years of age.

rules.display_text: Team members must be at least 18 years of age.

blocks.text: Team members who drive a competition vehicle at any time during an event must present a valid, government issued driver’s license for passenger cars, containing a photograph.

rules.display_text: Team members who drive a competition vehicle at any time during an event must present a valid, government issued driver’s license for passenger cars, containing a photograph.

blocks.text: Every participating team has to appoint one to four ESOs for the event.

rules.display_text: Every participating team has to appoint one to four ESOs for the event.

blocks.text: The ESOs are responsible for all electrical work carried out on the vehicle during the event.

rules.display_text: The ESOs are responsible for all electrical work carried out on the vehicle during the event.

blocks.text: The ESOs are the only persons in the team who may declare the vehicle electrically safe, in order for work to be performed on any system of the vehicle by the team.

rules.display_text: The ESOs are the only persons in the team who may declare the vehicle electrically safe, in order for work to be performed on any system of the vehicle by the team.

blocks.text: The ESOs must be valid team members, i.e. they must have student status, see A 4.2.6.

rules.display_text: The ESOs must be valid team members, i.e. they must have student status, see A 4.2.6.

blocks.text: The ESOs must be contactable by phone at all times during the event.

rules.display_text: The ESOs must be contactable by phone at all times during the event.

blocks.text: An ESO must accompany the vehicle whenever it is operated or moved around at the event site.

rules.display_text: An ESO must accompany the vehicle whenever it is operated or moved around at the event site.

blocks.text: If only one ESO is named by the team, this ESO must not be a driver.

rules.display_text: If only one ESO is named by the team, this ESO must not be a driver.

blocks.text: An appropriate Electrical System Officer Qualification (ESOQ) requires the proof of a practical and theoretical training for working on the TS. Regarding content, the training should be on the basis of DGUV 209-093 stage 2E/3E1 and held by an external expert.

rules.display_text: An appropriate Electrical System Officer Qualification (ESOQ) requires the proof of a practical and theoretical training for working on the TS. Regarding content, the training should be on the basis of DGUV 209-093 stage 2E/3E1 and held by an external expert.

blocks.text: To operate the AS, the participating team must appoint at least one ASR for the event. This person is responsible for all autonomous operations of the vehicle during the event which includes any work on the AS as well as racing and testing.

rules.display_text: To operate the AS, the participating team must appoint at least one ASR for the event. This person is responsible for all autonomous operations of the vehicle during the event which includes any work on the AS as well as racing and testing.

blocks.text: For vehicles with an electric drivetrain the ASR must fulfill A 4.3 and therefore replaces the ESO. The team may register additional ESOs for Accumulator Inspection and work on TS only. The sum of registered ASRs and ESOs must not exceed four persons.

rules.display_text: For vehicles with an electric drivetrain the ASR must fulfill A 4.3 and therefore replaces the ESO. The team may register additional ESOs for Accumulator Inspection and work on TS only. The sum of registered ASRs and ESOs must not exceed four persons.

blocks.text: The ASR is the only person in the team who is allowed to declare the AS safe, so that the vehicle may be operated in manual or autonomous mode.

rules.display_text: The ASR is the only person in the team who is allowed to declare the AS safe, so that the vehicle may be operated in manual or autonomous mode.

blocks.text: The ASR must be a valid team member, i.e. they must have student status, see A 4.2.6.

rules.display_text: The ASR must be a valid team member, i.e. they must have student status, see A 4.2.6.

blocks.text: The ASR must accompany the vehicle whenever it is operated or moved around at the event site.

rules.display_text: The ASR must accompany the vehicle whenever it is operated or moved around at the event site.

blocks.text: If only one ASR is named by the team, this ASR must not be a driver.

rules.display_text: If only one ASR is named by the team, this ASR must not be a driver.

blocks.text: The ASR must be properly qualified to handle the AS and to understand and deal with problems and failures. As ASR Qualification (ASRQ), a bachelor degree in computer science, electrical engineering, mechatronics, automation engineering, robotics or similar, i.e. comparable study content or progress, is a sufficient qualification. The qualification certificate needs to be an official university document and contain information on completed courses.

rules.display_text: The ASR must be properly qualified to handle the AS and to understand and deal with problems and failures. As ASR Qualification (ASRQ), a bachelor degree in computer science, electrical engineering, mechatronics, automation engineering, robotics or similar, i.e. comparable study content or progress, is a sufficient qualification. The qualification certificate needs to be an official university document and contain information on completed courses.

blocks.text: Several documents and forms must be submitted by the action deadlines defined in the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: Several documents and forms must be submitted by the action deadlines defined in the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: Submitted documents may only be viewed by members of the submitting team, authorized judges and officials.
Footnote: 1https://fsg.one/4i5SP

rules.display_text:
Submitted documents may only be viewed by members of the submitting team, authorized judges and officials.
Footnote: 1https://fsg.one/4i5SP

blocks.text: By submitting documents via the competition website, the team agrees that they may be reproduced and distributed by the officials, in both complete and edited versions, for educational purpose.

rules.display_text: By submitting documents via the competition website, the team agrees that they may be reproduced and distributed by the officials, in both complete and edited versions, for educational purpose.

blocks.text: Documents or videos that are largely incomplete or not readable/viewable are considered as not submitted.

rules.display_text: Documents or videos that are largely incomplete or not readable/viewable are considered as not submitted.

blocks.text: If the officials request a correction for a document, the corrected version has to be submitted within 168 hours (7 days) following the request.

rules.display_text: If the officials request a correction for a document, the corrected version has to be submitted within 168 hours (7 days) following the request.

blocks.text: Corrections requested before the initial deadline are treated as if they were requested at the initial deadline.

rules.display_text: Corrections requested before the initial deadline are treated as if they were requested at the initial deadline.

blocks.text: Separate requests for different parts within one document or form are treated independently.

rules.display_text: Separate requests for different parts within one document or form are treated independently.

blocks.text: If the corrected version of the document does not completely contain all requested corrections, the team is de-registered from the event.

rules.display_text: If the corrected version of the document does not completely contain all requested corrections, the team is de-registered from the event.

blocks.text: For each submission later than the respective deadline 10 penalty points are deducted from the team’s overall score.

rules.display_text: For each submission later than the respective deadline 10 penalty points are deducted from the team’s overall score.

blocks.text: Teams that do not submit documents until 24 hours (1 day) after the respective deadline are de-registered from the event.

rules.display_text: Teams that do not submit documents until 24 hours (1 day) after the respective deadline are de-registered from the event.

blocks.text: A team which is de-registered from the event has a single chance to apply for a place on the waiting list.

rules.display_text: A team which is de-registered from the event has a single chance to apply for a place on the waiting list.

blocks.text: To apply, the team must complete the following within 24 hours after the de-registration notification
Submit an informal application to the officials
Correct the reason for de-registration (e.g. submission of a document)

rules.display_text:
To apply, the team must complete the following within 24 hours after the de-registration notification
▪ Submit an informal application to the officials
▪ Correct the reason for de-registration (e.g. submission of a document)

blocks.text: If the application is positively confirmed by the officials, the team:
is placed at the end of the waiting list.
receives 20 penalty points.

rules.display_text:
If the application is positively confirmed by the officials, the team:
▪ is placed at the end of the waiting list.
▪ receives 20 penalty points.

blocks.text: Applications are declined if the rework is inadequate or de-registration was caused by misbehavior of the team.

rules.display_text: Applications are declined if the rework is inadequate or de-registration was caused by misbehavior of the team.

blocks.text: All teams must submit a video showing the vehicle driving in manual mode before the event. The video must be submitted before the deadline specified in the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: All teams must submit a video showing the vehicle driving in manual mode before the event. The video must be submitted before the deadline specified in the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: [DC ONLY] The vehicle must instead drive in autonomous mode. No manual mode VSV is necessary.

rules.display_text: [DC ONLY] The vehicle must instead drive in autonomous mode. No manual mode VSV is necessary.

blocks.text: The video must show the following sequences in the described order:
Standing still
360° video around the vehicle (close up, may overlap with the following two bullet points)
[CV ONLY] Start engine / [EV ONLY] Activate TS
Straight driving, minimum distance is 30 m, minimum speed is 10 km/h for manual mode
Full stop (not needed for autonomous mode VSV)
180° cornering
Straight driving back to start point, minimum speed is 10 km/h for manual mode
[DC ONLY] At the end of the VSV, the vehicle must be stopped by an emergency brake maneuver, see T 15.
Standing still, [CV ONLY] engine off / [EV ONLY] TS deactivated

rules.display_text:
The video must show the following sequences in the described order:
▪ Standing still
▪ 360° video around the vehicle (close up, may overlap with the following two bullet points)
▪ [CV ONLY] Start engine / [EV ONLY] Activate TS
▪ Straight driving, minimum distance is 30 m, minimum speed is 10 km/h for manual mode
▪ Full stop (not needed for autonomous mode VSV)
▪ 180° cornering
▪ Straight driving back to start point, minimum speed is 10 km/h for manual mode
▪ [DC ONLY] At the end of the VSV, the vehicle must be stopped by an emergency brake maneuver, see T 15.

blocks.text: The following listed requirements are considered the minimum for a testing/operating environment to qualify as safe. Following these guidelines does not guarantee safety under all circumstances:

blocks.text: For activities on the inactive TS, the following procedure must be carried out:
The vehicle must be barred from anyone not involved in the work, by using barrier tape.
The Tractive System Master Switch (TSMS) must be switched off.
It must be assured that the TS cannot be activated by, at a minimum, using the lockout/ tagout of the TSMS.
A check for zero-potential must be carried out.

A sign that declares the vehicle is electrically safe must be installed. The name of the ESO who is supervising the activities must be noted on the sign. This ESO is the only person who may remove the sign and the barrier.

rules.display_text:
For activities on the inactive TS, the following procedure must be carried out:
▪ The vehicle must be barred from anyone not involved in the work, by using barrier tape.
▪ The Tractive System Master Switch (TSMS) must be switched off.
▪ It must be assured that the TS cannot be activated by, at a minimum, using the lockout/ tagout of the TSMS.
▪ A check for zero-potential must be carried out.
▪ A sign that declares the vehicle is electrically safe must be installed. The name of the ESO who is supervising the activities must be noted on the sign. This ESO is the only person who may remove the sign and the barrier.

rules.section_title: [EV ONLY] Working on the Tractive System

blocks.text: In case of measurements on the active TS or an activation of the TS in the pit for testing purposes, the following steps must be followed:
The vehicle must be barred from anyone not involved in the work, by using barrier tape.
The vehicle must be jacked up and the driven wheels removed.
One team member must be prepared to push a shutdown button at any time.
The TS must only be activated for as long as necessary.
Appropriate insulated tools and equipment must be used.
Safety glasses with side shields and compliant safety gloves must be worn by all participating team members when parts of the TS are exposed.
No other work on the vehicle is allowed when the TS is active.

rules.display_text:

blocks.text: Chassis — the fabricated structural assembly that supports all functional vehicle systems. This assembly may be a single welded structure, multiple welded structures or a combination of composite and welded structures.

blocks.text: Cockpit — the volume which accommodates the driver which is defined by the top of the vehicle, the floor closeout, the inner side of the bodywork, the front bulkhead and the firewall.

blocks.text: Chassis member — a minimum representative single piece of uncut, continuous tubing or equivalent structure.

blocks.text: Main hoop — a roll bar located alongside or just behind the driver’s torso.

rules.display_text: Monocoque — a chassis made of composite material.

blocks.text: Rollover protection envelope — the union of
the primary structure and any additional structures fixed to the primary structure which meet the minimum specification defined in T 3.2 or equivalent
the plane from the top of the main hoop to the top of the front hoop
the plane from the top of the main hoop to the rearmost structure according to T 3.2 or equivalent
additional planes covering concave sections of structures according to T 3.2, e.g. to accommodate suspension or other components

blocks.text: Fire Retardant — a material meeting one of the following standards:
UL94 V-0 for the minimum used material thickness
UL94 HF-1 for foams; UL94 VTM-0 for materials that are not suitable for testing according to UL94 V-0 due to their thickness or flexibility.

Equivalent standards are only accepted, if the team shows equivalence and this is approved by the officials before the event. Compliance of alternative materials to above standards can be shown through testing with appropriate documentation in the SES/ASES and/or at Technical Inspection.

rules.display_text:
Fire Retardant — a material meeting one of the following standards:
▪ UL94 V-0 for the minimum used material thickness
▪ FAR 25.853(a)(1)(i)
▪ UL94 HF-1 for foams; UL94 VTM-0 for materials that are not suitable for testing according to UL94 V-0 due to their thickness or flexibility.
Equivalent standards are only accepted, if the team shows equivalence and this is approved by the officials before the event. Compliance of alternative materials to above standards can be shown through testing with appropriate documentation in the SES/ASES and/or at Technical Inspection.
changelog: Allowed UL94 VTM-0 for thin materials in addition to foams

blocks.text: Coolant — a substance used for heat transfer by convection.

rules.display_text: Coolant — a substance used for heat transfer by convection.

blocks.text: Direct Connection — two devices or circuits are directly connected if the connection is not routed through any common PCB and does not include any devices or functionality other than overcurrent protection or connectors.

rules.display_text: Direct Connection — two devices or circuits are directly connected if the connection is not routed through any common PCB and does not include any devices or functionality other than overcurrent protection or connectors.

blocks.text: Manual Mode — a vehicle is in manual mode when driven by a human driver. In this case the ASMS must be off (AS deactivated).

rules.display_text: Manual Mode — a vehicle is in manual mode when driven by a human driver. In this case the ASMS must be off (AS deactivated).

blocks.text: Autonomous Mode — a vehicle is in autonomous mode when the AS is activated. When a vehicle is in autonomous mode, there must be no person inside the vehicle.

rules.display_text: Autonomous Mode — a vehicle is in autonomous mode when the AS is activated. When a vehicle is in autonomous mode, there must be no person inside the vehicle.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be designed and fabricated in accordance with good engineering practices.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must be designed and fabricated in accordance with good engineering practices.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be open-wheeled, single seat and open cockpit (a formula style body) with four wheels that are not in a straight line.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must be open-wheeled, single seat and open cockpit (a formula style body) with four wheels that are not in a straight line.

blocks.text: Open wheel vehicles must satisfy the following, see also Figure 4:
The wheel/tire assembly must be unobstructed when viewed from the side.

No part of the vehicle may enter a keep-out-zone defined by two lines extending vertically from positions 75 mm in front of and 75 mm behind the outer diameter of the front and rear tires in the side view of the vehicle, with steering system straight ahead. This keep-out zone extends laterally outward from the inboard plane of the wheel/tire assembly indefinitely. The keep-out-zone at the rear tires extends up to 700 mm above the ground.

An additional keep-out-zone extends from the top of the rear tire to 700 mm above the ground and 150 mm inboard from the inboard plane of the rear tire. It is bounded longitudinally by the 75 mm keep-out-zone of the rear tire.

rules.display_text:
Open wheel vehicles must satisfy the following, see also Figure 4:
▪ The wheel/tire assembly must be unobstructed when viewed from the side.
▪ No part of the vehicle may enter a keep-out-zone defined by two lines extending vertically from positions 75 mm in front of and 75 mm behind the outer diameter of the front and rear tires in the side view of the vehicle, with steering system straight ahead. This keep-out zone extends laterally outward from the inboard plane of the wheel/tire assembly indefinitely. The keep-out-zone at the rear tires extends up to 700 mm above the ground.
▪ An additional keep-out-zone extends from the top of the rear tire to 700 mm above the ground and 150 mm inboard from the inboard plane of the rear tire. It is bounded longitudinally by the 75 mm keep-out-zone of the rear tire.
[Figure 4: Keep-out-zones for the definition of an open-wheeled vehicle — see figure on page 21]
changelog: Added new wording for rear tire keep-out-zone

blocks.text: No part of the vehicle forward of the vertical plane through the leading edge of the front tires must enter the variable keep-out zone, see Figure 5. It is defined by two independent, non-intersecting, cuboids of 75 mm × 250 mm × infinite length. One infinite-length face must rest on the ground, and the infinite-length edges must be parallel to the vehicle longitudinal axis. The cuboids must not extend outboard of the front tires.

rules.display_text:
No part of the vehicle forward of the vertical plane through the leading edge of the front tires must enter the variable keep-out zone, see Figure 5. It is defined by two independent, non-intersecting, cuboids of 75 mm × 250 mm × infinite length. One infinite-length face must rest on the ground, and the infinite-length edges must be parallel to the vehicle longitudinal axis. The cuboids must not extend outboard of the front tires.
[Figure 5: Variable keep-out-zone in front of the front tires — see figure on page 21]
changelog: Added variable keep-out-zone

blocks.text: The minimum static ground clearance of any portion of the vehicle, other than the tires, including a driver, must be 30 mm. If an active suspension system is installed, the static ground clearance is measured in the lowest adjustable position.

rules.display_text: The minimum static ground clearance of any portion of the vehicle, other than the tires, including a driver, must be 30 mm. If an active suspension system is installed, the static ground clearance is measured in the lowest adjustable position.

blocks.text: Sliding skirts or other aerodynamic devices that by design, fabrication or as a consequence of moving, contact the track surface are prohibited.

rules.display_text: Sliding skirts or other aerodynamic devices that by design, fabrication or as a consequence of moving, contact the track surface are prohibited.

blocks.text: There must be no openings through the bodywork into the cockpit other than that required for the cockpit opening. Minimal openings around the front suspension and steering system components are allowed.

rules.display_text: There must be no openings through the bodywork into the cockpit other than that required for the cockpit opening. Minimal openings around the front suspension and steering system components are allowed.

blocks.text: In any side section view in front of the cockpit opening and outside the area defined in T 8.2 all parts of the bodywork must have no external concave radii of curvatures. Any gaps between bodywork and other parts must be reduced to a minimum.

rules.display_text: In any side section view in front of the cockpit opening and outside the area defined in T 8.2 all parts of the bodywork must have no external concave radii of curvatures. Any gaps between bodywork and other parts must be reduced to a minimum.

blocks.text: Enclosed chassis structures and structures between the chassis and the ground must have two venting holes of at least 25 mm diameter in the lowest part of the structure to prevent accumulation of liquids. Additional holes are required when multiple local lowest parts exist in the structure.

rules.display_text: Enclosed chassis structures and structures between the chassis and the ground must have two venting holes of at least 25 mm diameter in the lowest part of the structure to prevent accumulation of liquids. Additional holes are required when multiple local lowest parts exist in the structure.

blocks.text: The bodywork in front of the front wheels with the tangent of surface above 45° relative to the forward direction must have a radius of at least 38 mm along the top, sides and bottom of all affected edges.

rules.display_text: The bodywork in front of the front wheels with the tangent of surface above 45° relative to the forward direction must have a radius of at least 38 mm along the top, sides and bottom of all affected edges.

rules.title: Minimum Edge Radii of Bodywork and Aerodynamic Devices
rules.section_title: Minimum Edge Radii of Bodywork and Aerodynamic Devices
Minimum Edge Radii of Bodywork and Aerodynamic Devices

blocks.text: For all edges that could come into contact with any standing pedestrian without reaching to the vehicle, the minimum radius of the bodywork and aerodynamic devices is 3 mm for all forward facing edges and 1 mm for all other edges.

rules.display_text: For all edges that could come into contact with any standing pedestrian without reaching to the vehicle, the minimum radius of the bodywork and aerodynamic devices is 3 mm for all forward facing edges and 1 mm for all other edges.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be equipped with fully operational front and rear suspension systems including shock absorbers and a usable wheel travel of at least 50 mm and a minimum jounce of 25 mm with driver seated.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must be equipped with fully operational front and rear suspension systems including shock absorbers and a usable wheel travel of at least 50 mm and a minimum jounce of 25 mm with driver seated.

blocks.text: All suspension mounting points must be visible at Technical Inspection, either by direct view or by removing any covers.

rules.display_text: All suspension mounting points must be visible at Technical Inspection, either by direct view or by removing any covers.

blocks.text: Any wheel mounting system that uses a single retaining nut must incorporate a device to prevent loosening of the nut and the wheel. A second nut (“jam nut”) does not meet these requirements.

rules.display_text: Any wheel mounting system that uses a single retaining nut must incorporate a device to prevent loosening of the nut and the wheel. A second nut (“jam nut”) does not meet these requirements.

blocks.text: Wheel lug bolts, drive pegs and studs must be made of steel or titanium. The team must be able to show good engineering practice and providing adequate strength by calculations. Wheel lug bolts, drive pegs and studs must not be hollow.

rules.display_text: Wheel lug bolts, drive pegs and studs must be made of steel or titanium. The team must be able to show good engineering practice and providing adequate strength by calculations. Wheel lug bolts, drive pegs and studs must not be hollow.

blocks.text: Aluminium wheel nuts may be used, but they must be hard anodized and in pristine condition.

rules.display_text: Aluminium wheel nuts may be used, but they must be hard anodized and in pristine condition.

blocks.text: The radial clearance between any non-rotating part and the rim must be at least 5 mm in static condition at any steering angle and any ride height.

rules.display_text: The radial clearance between any non-rotating part and the rim must be at least 5 mm in static condition at any steering angle and any ride height.
changelog: Clarified rule about rim clearance

blocks.text: Vehicles must have two types of tires as follows:
Dry tires - The tires on the vehicle when it is presented for Technical Inspection are defined as its “dry tires”.
Wet tires - Wet tires may be any size or type of treaded or grooved tire provided:

The tread pattern or grooves were molded in by the tire manufacturer or were cut by the tire manufacturer or their appointed agent. Any grooves that have been cut must have documentary proof that it was done in accordance with these rules.
There is a minimum tread depth of 2.4 mm.

rules.display_text:
Vehicles must have two types of tires as follows:
▪ Dry tires - The tires on the vehicle when it is presented for Technical Inspection are defined as its “dry tires”.
▪ Wet tires - Wet tires may be any size or type of treaded or grooved tire provided:
  ▪ The tread pattern or grooves were molded in by the tire manufacturer or were cut by the tire manufacturer or their appointed agent. Any grooves that have been cut must have documentary proof that it was done in accordance with these rules.
  ▪ There is a minimum tread depth of 2.4 mm.

blocks.text: Tires on the same axle must have the same manufacturer, size and compound.

rules.display_text: Tires on the same axle must have the same manufacturer, size and compound.

blocks.text: Tire warmers are not allowed.

rules.display_text: Tire warmers are not allowed.

blocks.text: Special agents that increase traction must not be added to the tires or track surface.

rules.display_text: Special agents that increase traction must not be added to the tires or track surface.

blocks.text: Steering systems using cables or belts for actuation are prohibited. This does not apply for autonomous steering actuators.

rules.display_text: Steering systems using cables or belts for actuation are prohibited. This does not apply for autonomous steering actuators.

blocks.text: The steering wheel must directly mechanically actuate the front wheels.

rules.display_text: The steering wheel must directly mechanically actuate the front wheels.

blocks.text: The steering system must have positive steering stops that prevent the steering linkages from locking up. The stops must be placed on the rack and must prevent the tires and rims from contacting any other parts. Steering actuation must be possible during standstill.

rules.display_text: The steering system must have positive steering stops that prevent the steering linkages from locking up. The stops must be placed on the rack and must prevent the tires and rims from contacting any other parts. Steering actuation must be possible during standstill.

blocks.text: Allowable steering system free play is limited to a total of 7° measured at the steering wheel. The steering system must not exhibit excessive deformation under driver-applied loads. This may be checked by an official seated normally in the vehicle while applying normal steering force with the vehicle stationary.

rules.display_text: Allowable steering system free play is limited to a total of 7° measured at the steering wheel. The steering system must not exhibit excessive deformation under driver-applied loads. This may be checked by an official seated normally in the vehicle while applying normal steering force with the vehicle stationary.
changelog: Added steering deformation limit and inspection method

blocks.text: The steering wheel must be attached to the column with a quick disconnect. The driver must be able to operate the quick disconnect while in the normal driving position with gloves on.

rules.display_text: The steering wheel must be attached to the column with a quick disconnect. The driver must be able to operate the quick disconnect while in the normal driving position with gloves on.

blocks.text: The steering wheel must be no more than 250 mm rearward of the front hoop. This distance is measured horizontally, on the vehicle centerline, from the rear surface of the front hoop to the forward most surface of the steering wheel with the steering system in any position.

rules.display_text: The steering wheel must be no more than 250 mm rearward of the front hoop. This distance is measured horizontally, on the vehicle centerline, from the rear surface of the front hoop to the forward most surface of the steering wheel with the steering system in any position.

blocks.text: The steering wheel must have a continuous perimeter that is near circular or near oval. The outer perimeter profile may have some straight sections, but no concave sections.

rules.display_text: The steering wheel must have a continuous perimeter that is near circular or near oval. The outer perimeter profile may have some straight sections, but no concave sections.

blocks.text: In any angular position, the top of the steering wheel must be no higher than the top-most surface of the front hoop.

rules.display_text: In any angular position, the top of the steering wheel must be no higher than the top-most surface of the front hoop.

blocks.text: The steering rack must be mechanically attached to the primary structure and all stationary parts of the steering system must be within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16.

rules.display_text: The steering rack must be mechanically attached to the primary structure and all stationary parts of the steering system must be within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16.
changelog: Clarified rule

blocks.text: Joints between all components attaching the steering wheel to the steering rack must be mechanical and visible at Technical Inspection. Bonded joints are allowed in accordance with T 3.2.8.

rules.display_text: Joints between all components attaching the steering wheel to the steering rack must be mechanical and visible at Technical Inspection. Bonded joints are allowed in accordance with T 3.2.8.

blocks.text: Rear wheel steering, which can be electrically actuated, is allowed if mechanical stops limit the range of angular movement of the rear wheels to a maximum of 6°. This must be demonstrated with a driver in the vehicle and the team must provide the equipment for the steering angle range to be verified at Technical Inspection.

rules.display_text: Rear wheel steering, which can be electrically actuated, is allowed if mechanical stops limit the range of angular movement of the rear wheels to a maximum of 6°. This must be demonstrated with a driver in the vehicle and the team must provide the equipment for the steering angle range to be verified at Technical Inspection.

blocks.text: The vehicle must have a wheelbase of at least 1525 mm.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must have a wheelbase of at least 1525 mm.

blocks.text: The smaller track of the vehicle (front or rear) must be no less than 75 % of the larger track.

rules.display_text: The smaller track of the vehicle (front or rear) must be no less than 75 % of the larger track.

blocks.text: The track and center of gravity of the vehicle must combine to provide adequate rollover stability. This is tested by the Tilt Test IN 7.

rules.display_text: The track and center of gravity of the vehicle must combine to provide adequate rollover stability. This is tested by the Tilt Test IN 7.

blocks.text: Among other requirements, the vehicle’s structure must include:
Two roll hoops that are braced
A front bulkhead with support system and IA
Side impact structures

rules.display_text:
Among other requirements, the vehicle’s structure must include:
▪ Two roll hoops that are braced
▪ A front bulkhead with support system and IA
▪ Side impact structures

blocks.text: Table 2 shows the minimum requirements for the members of the primary structure if made from steel tubing.

rules.display_text:
Table 2 shows the minimum requirements for the members of the primary structure if made from steel tubing.
[Table 2: Minimum Material Requirements — see table on page 24]
  Item or application | Minimum wall thickness | Minimum cross sectional area | Minimum area moment of inertia
  Main and front hoops, shoulder harness mounting bar | 2.0 mm | 173 mm2 | 11 320 mm4
  Impact structures, front bulkhead, roll hoop bracing, driver’s restraint harness attachment (except as noted above) | 1.2 mm | 119 mm2 | 8509 mm4
  Front bulkhead support, main hoop bracing supports | 1.2 mm | 91 mm2 | 6695 mm4

blocks.text: Steel tubing has to be made from unalloyed carbon steel with a maximum content of 0.3 % carbon, 1.7 % manganese and 0.6 % of any other element. All other steel grades are considered alternative materials and require additional testing and documentation, see T 3.4.

rules.display_text: Steel tubing has to be made from unalloyed carbon steel with a maximum content of 0.3 % carbon, 1.7 % manganese and 0.6 % of any other element. All other steel grades are considered alternative materials and require additional testing and documentation, see T 3.4.

blocks.text: Except for inspection holes, any holes drilled in any part which is a member of the primary structure must be considered in the SES.

rules.display_text: Except for inspection holes, any holes drilled in any part which is a member of the primary structure must be considered in the SES.

blocks.text: The steel properties used for the calculations in the SES must be the following, or what is written in the material property documentation, whichever is lower:
Non-welded strength for continuous material calculations:
Young’s Modulus (E) = 200 GPa
Yield Strength (Sy) = 305 MPa
Ultimate Strength (Su) = 365 MPa
Welded strength for discontinuous material such as joint calculations:
Yield Strength (Sy) = 180 MPa
Ultimate Strength (Su) = 300 MPa

rules.display_text:
The steel properties used for the calculations in the SES must be the following, or what is written in the material property documentation, whichever is lower:
Non-welded strength for continuous material calculations:
▪ Young’s Modulus (E) = 200 GPa
▪ Yield Strength (Sy) = 305 MPa
▪ Ultimate Strength (Su) = 365 MPa
Welded strength for discontinuous material such as joint calculations:
▪ Yield Strength (Sy) = 180 MPa
▪ Ultimate Strength (Su) = 300 MPa

blocks.text: Any tubing with a wall thickness less than 1.2 mm or a minimum area moment of inertia less than 6695 mm4 is considered non-structural and is ignored when assessing compliance to any rule regarding the vehicle structure.

rules.display_text: Any tubing with a wall thickness less than 1.2 mm or a minimum area moment of inertia less than 6695 mm4 is considered non-structural and is ignored when assessing compliance to any rule regarding the vehicle structure.

blocks.text: If a member of the primary structure (except for the roll hoops) is a bent tube or made from multiple tubes an additional tube must support it. This support tube must:
have its attachment point at the position along the bend tube where it deviates farthest from a straight line connecting both ends.
be of the same dimension as the supported tube(s).
terminate at a node of the primary structure.
be angled no more than 30° from the plane of the supported tube(s).

rules.display_text:
If a member of the primary structure (except for the roll hoops) is a bent tube or made from multiple tubes an additional tube must support it. This support tube must:
▪ have its attachment point at the position along the bend tube where it deviates farthest from a straight line connecting both ends.
▪ be of the same dimension as the supported tube(s).
▪ terminate at a node of the primary structure.
▪ be angled no more than 30° from the plane of the supported tube(s).

blocks.text: Any welded seams shape must not be mechanically altered in any way.

rules.display_text: Any welded seams shape must not be mechanically altered in any way.

blocks.text: Where bonded joints are applicable and governed by the rules, a 50 % reduction must be applied to all nominal and tested adhesive values. Bonded joints in the primary structure must be documented in the SES.

rules.display_text: Where bonded joints are applicable and governed by the rules, a 50 % reduction must be applied to all nominal and tested adhesive values. Bonded joints in the primary structure must be documented in the SES.

blocks.text: Components, see T 9.3.5, CV 5.2.1 and EV 5.5.8, themselves and their mountings must be able to withstand the following accelerations:
40 g in the longitudinal direction (forward/aft)
40 g in the lateral direction (left/right)
20 g in the vertical direction (up/down)

rules.display_text:
Components, see T 9.3.5, CV 5.2.1 and EV 5.5.8, themselves and their mountings must be able to withstand the following accelerations:
▪ 40 g in the longitudinal direction (forward/aft)
▪ 40 g in the lateral direction (left/right)
▪ 20 g in the vertical direction (up/down)

blocks.text: Alternative materials may be used for all parts of the primary structure and the TSAC with the following exceptions:
The main hoop and the main hoop bracing must be steel
The front hoop must be metal
Any welded structures of the primary structure must be steel
However, the front hoop may be an aluminium welded structure

rules.display_text:
Alternative materials may be used for all parts of the primary structure and the TSAC with the following exceptions:
▪ The main hoop and the main hoop bracing must be steel
▪ The front hoop must be metal
▪ Any welded structures of the primary structure must be steel
▪ However, the front hoop may be an aluminium welded structure

blocks.text: If any other materials than steel tubing are used in the primary structure or the TSAC, physical testing is required to show equivalency to the minimum material properties for steel in T 3.2.

rules.display_text: If any other materials than steel tubing are used in the primary structure or the TSAC, physical testing is required to show equivalency to the minimum material properties for steel in T 3.2.

blocks.text: If alloyed steel as defined by T 3.2.2 is used, the team has to include tests and documentation in the SES to show structural equivalency. This may include, but is not limited to:
Receipts and datasheets of the used tubing materials
Documentation about welding processes and filler materials
Documentation about heat treatments
Tests showing adequate strength and elongation at break in the welded condition

rules.display_text:
If alloyed steel as defined by T 3.2.2 is used, the team has to include tests and documentation in the SES to show structural equivalency. This may include, but is not limited to:
▪ Receipts and datasheets of the used tubing materials
▪ Documentation about welding processes and filler materials
▪ Documentation about heat treatments
▪ Tests showing adequate strength and elongation at break in the welded condition

blocks.text: Parts of the steering, brake and suspension system must not be manufactured using additive processes that produce anisotropic strength properties (e.g. consumer-grade FDM). Additively manufactured parts are permitted only if proven to have equivalent strength in all load directions.

rules.display_text: Parts of the steering, brake and suspension system must not be manufactured using additive processes that produce anisotropic strength properties (e.g. consumer-grade FDM). Additively manufactured parts are permitted only if proven to have equivalent strength in all load directions.

blocks.text: If composite structures are used in the primary structure and/or the TSAC:
The Flexural Rigidity (EI) of that structure must be calculated with the tools and formulas in the SES and/or ASES.
The EI must be calculated as the EI of a flat panel about its neutral axis.
The structure used for flat panel calculations must have the same composition as the structure used in the primary structure or the TSAC.
The actual geometry and curvature of the panel may only be considered if the flat panel EI equivalency exceeds 60 % of the minimum requirements (T 3.2)
Actual geometry calculations are not permitted for the side impact structure, front bulkhead and TSAC.

rules.display_text:
If composite structures are used in the primary structure and/or the TSAC:
▪ The Flexural Rigidity (EI) of that structure must be calculated with the tools and formulas in the SES and/or ASES.
▪ The EI must be calculated as the EI of a flat panel about its neutral axis.
▪ The structure used for flat panel calculations must have the same composition as the structure used in the primary structure or the TSAC.
▪ The actual geometry and curvature of the panel may only be considered if the flat panel EI equivalency exceeds 60 % of the minimum requirements (T 3.2)
▪ Actual geometry calculations are not permitted for the side impact structure, front bulkhead and TSAC.

blocks.text: If composite materials are used in the primary structure or the TSAC, the SES and/or ASES must include:
Material type(s)
Cloth weights
Resin type
Fiber orientation
Number of layers
Core material
Lay-up technique
Adhesive film type(s)
3-point-bend test and shear test data (the AIP is exempt from these tests, but must comply with T 3.17.4)

rules.display_text:
If composite materials are used in the primary structure or the TSAC, the SES and/or ASES must include:
▪ Material type(s)
▪ Cloth weights
▪ Resin type
▪ Fiber orientation
▪ Number of layers
▪ Core material
▪ Lay-up technique
▪ Adhesive film type(s)
▪ 3-point-bend test and shear test data (the AIP is exempt from these tests, but must comply with T 3.17.4)

blocks.text: For any laminate in the primary structure and/or the TSAC, the maximum weight content of parallel fibers, relative to the weight of all fibers in the laminate, is 50 %. All fibers whose orientation falls within any 20° window ±10° are considered as parallel.

rules.display_text: For any laminate in the primary structure and/or the TSAC, the maximum weight content of parallel fibers, relative to the weight of all fibers in the laminate, is 50 %. All fibers whose orientation falls within any 20° window ±10° are considered as parallel.

blocks.text: If an asymmetrical lay-up is used in the primary structure, the thinner skin must have a thickness of at least 40 % of the thicker skin or 1 mm whichever is lower.

rules.display_text: If an asymmetrical lay-up is used in the primary structure, the thinner skin must have a thickness of at least 40 % of the thicker skin or 1 mm whichever is lower.

blocks.text: When critical fasteners as defined in T 10.1.1 are used to attach components to a sandwich structure, crushing of the sandwich core is not permitted.

rules.display_text: When critical fasteners as defined in T 10.1.1 are used to attach components to a sandwich structure, crushing of the sandwich core is not permitted.
changelog: Clarified and expanded rule application and moved from T 3.16.1 to T 3.5

blocks.text: Wherever backing plates are required, they must be fully supported by the structure they are attached to.

rules.display_text: Wherever backing plates are required, they must be fully supported by the structure they are attached to.

blocks.text: Backing plates must have a continuous near-circular or near-oval perimeter without concave sections or cut-outs other than bolt holes.

rules.display_text: Backing plates must have a continuous near-circular or near-oval perimeter without concave sections or cut-outs other than bolt holes.
changelog: Shortened rule without losing definition

blocks.text: Unidirectional fibers are not allowed in the outermost structural layers of a laminate used in the primary structure.

rules.display_text: Unidirectional fibers are not allowed in the outermost structural layers of a laminate used in the primary structure.

blocks.text: If composite materials are used for any part of the primary structure (except for the AIP) or the TSAC the team must:

build a representative test panel which must measure exactly 275 mm × 500 mm that has the same design, laminate and fabrication method as used for the respective part of the primary structure represented as a flat panel. The sides of the test panel must not be laminated (core material must be visible).
perform a 3-point bending test on this panel.

The data from these tests and pictures of the test samples and test setup must be included in the SES. In the pictures, the following must be identifiable: distance between the two supports, dimensions of the load applicator and test sample marking as per T 3.6.6. The test results must be used to derive strength and stiffness properties used in the SES formula for all laminate panels. Representative test panels for parts of the TSAC may use smaller dimensions, provided that the panel core thickness is 5 mm or smaller. This representative test panel must then measure 150 mm × 275 mm. In this case, the distance between the two test panel supports must be at least 200 mm and the load applicator must have a radius of at least 5 mm. T 3.6.7 and T 3.6.8 do not apply.

rules.display_text:
If composite materials are used for any part of the primary structure (except for the AIP) or the TSAC the team must:
▪ build a representative test panel which must measure exactly 275 mm × 500 mm that has the same design, laminate and fabrication method as used for the respective part of the primary structure represented as a flat panel. The sides of the test panel must not be laminated (core material must be visible).
▪ perform a 3-point bending test on this panel.
The data from these tests and pictures of the test samples and test setup must be included in the SES. In the pictures, the following must be identifiable: distance between the two supports, dimensions of the load applicator and test sample marking as per T 3.6.6. The test results must be used to derive strength and stiffness properties used in the SES formula for all laminate panels. Representative test panels for parts of the TSAC may use smaller dimensions, provided that the panel core thickness is 5 mm or smaller. This representative test panel must then measure 150 mm × 275 mm. In this case, the distance between the two test panel supports must be at least 200 mm and the load applicator must have a radius of at least 5 mm. T 3.6.7 and T 3.6.8 do not apply.

blocks.text: If a panel represents side impact structure it must be proven that it has at least the same properties as two steel tubes meeting the requirements for side impact structure tubes for buckling modulus, yield strength and absorbed energy.

rules.display_text: If a panel represents side impact structure it must be proven that it has at least the same properties as two steel tubes meeting the requirements for side impact structure tubes for buckling modulus, yield strength and absorbed energy.

blocks.text: A baseline 3-point bending test, performed with steel tube(s), must demonstrate a minimum rig compliance of 85 % and be documented in the SES.

rules.display_text: A baseline 3-point bending test, performed with steel tube(s), must demonstrate a minimum rig compliance of 85 % and be documented in the SES.

blocks.text: Composite structures with different core thicknesses but otherwise identical construction may use material properties derived from a single test panel, except for the front bulkhead and side impact structure. The panel with the thicker core must be tested and the structure using derived material properties must not use a core thickness of less than 66 % of the tested panel.

rules.display_text: Composite structures with different core thicknesses but otherwise identical construction may use material properties derived from a single test panel, except for the front bulkhead and side impact structure. The panel with the thicker core must be tested and the structure using derived material properties must not use a core thickness of less than 66 % of the tested panel.

blocks.text: When a laminate is not quasi-isotropic, i.e. has equal strength and stiffness in the 0°, 90° and ± 45° direction, the results from the 3 point bending test are assigned to the 0° lay-up direction. To show equivalence in the SES, the 0° lay-up direction must be used and oriented accordingly in the chassis.

rules.display_text: When a laminate is not quasi-isotropic, i.e. has equal strength and stiffness in the 0°, 90° and ± 45° direction, the results from the 3 point bending test are assigned to the 0° lay-up direction. To show equivalence in the SES, the 0° lay-up direction must be used and oriented accordingly in the chassis.

blocks.text: The test samples must be presented at Technical Inspection. All samples must be marked with the following non-removable (e.g.: permanent marker or engraving, but no sticker) information: laminated structure acronym and date of testing.

rules.display_text: The test samples must be presented at Technical Inspection. All samples must be marked with the following non-removable (e.g.: permanent marker or engraving, but no sticker) information: laminated structure acronym and date of testing.

blocks.text: The distance between the two test panel supports must be at least 400 mm.

rules.display_text: The distance between the two test panel supports must be at least 400 mm.

blocks.text: The load applicator used to test any panel or tube must be metallic and have a radius of 50 mm.

rules.display_text: The load applicator used to test any panel or tube must be metallic and have a radius of 50 mm.

blocks.text: The load applicator must overhang the test piece to prevent edge loading.

rules.display_text: The load applicator must overhang the test piece to prevent edge loading.

blocks.text: There must be no material between the load applicator and the test piece.

rules.display_text: There must be no material between the load applicator and the test piece.

blocks.text: Perimeter shear tests must be completed which measure the force required to push or pull a 25 mm diameter flat punch through a flat laminate sample. The sample must be at least 100 mm × 100 mm. Core and skin thicknesses must be identical to those used in the actual primary structure and be manufactured using the same materials and processes. If an asymmetrical lay-up is used, the thinner skin must face the punch.

rules.display_text: Perimeter shear tests must be completed which measure the force required to push or pull a 25 mm diameter flat punch through a flat laminate sample. The sample must be at least 100 mm × 100 mm. Core and skin thicknesses must be identical to those used in the actual primary structure and be manufactured using the same materials and processes. If an asymmetrical lay-up is used, the thinner skin must face the punch.

blocks.text: The test fixture must support the entire sample, except for a 32 mm hole aligned co-axially with the punch. The sample must not be clamped to the fixture.

rules.display_text: The test fixture must support the entire sample, except for a 32 mm hole aligned co-axially with the punch. The sample must not be clamped to the fixture.

blocks.text: All teams must submit a Structural Equivalency Spreadsheet (SES), Structural Equivalency 3D Model (SE3D) and [EV ONLY] Accumulator Structural Equivalency Spreadsheet (ASES).

rules.display_text: All teams must submit a Structural Equivalency Spreadsheet (SES), Structural Equivalency 3D Model (SE3D) and [EV ONLY] Accumulator Structural Equivalency Spreadsheet (ASES).

provisions.text: All teams must submit a Structural Equivalency Spreadsheet (SES), Structural Equivalency 3D Model (SE3D) and [EV ONLY] Accumulator Structural Equivalency Spreadsheet (ASES).

blocks.text: The SES and [EV ONLY] ASES can be downloaded from the competition website.

rules.display_text: The SES and [EV ONLY] ASES can be downloaded from the competition website.

provisions.text: The SES and [EV ONLY] ASES can be downloaded from the competition website.

blocks.text: The SE3D must contain a three dimensional CAD model of the chassis including all members of the primary structure and their mechanical attachment details.
[Monocoque only] The SE3D must include the inner, outer skin and core thicknesses.
[Monocoque only] If the actual EI of a structure is used in the SES, this must be highlighted and included as a measurable instance.
[EV ONLY] The TSACs and their attachment must be included.
[CV ONLY] The air intake system, the fuel tank and filler neck must be included.

rules.display_text:
The SE3D must contain a three dimensional CAD model of the chassis including all members of the primary structure and their mechanical attachment details.
▪ [Monocoque only] The SE3D must include the inner, outer skin and core thicknesses.
▪ [Monocoque only] If the actual EI of a structure is used in the SES, this must be highlighted and included as a measurable instance.
▪ [EV ONLY] The TSACs and their attachment must be included.
▪ [CV ONLY] The air intake system, the fuel tank and filler neck must be included.

provisions.text: [EV ONLY] The TSACs and their attachment must be included.
[CV ONLY] The air intake system, the fuel tank and filler neck must be included.

applicability.label: All vehicles; contains CV-only and EV-only provisions

blocks.text: Vehicles must be fabricated in accordance with the materials and processes described in the SES.

rules.display_text: Vehicles must be fabricated in accordance with the materials and processes described in the SES.

blocks.text: Teams must bring a copy of the approved SES to Technical Inspection.

rules.display_text: Teams must bring a copy of the approved SES to Technical Inspection.

blocks.text: Both roll hoops must be integrated into the primary structure using node-to-node triangulation or equivalent joining methods.

rules.display_text: Both roll hoops must be integrated into the primary structure using node-to-node triangulation or equivalent joining methods.

blocks.text: The minimum radius of any bend, measured at the tube centerline, must be at least three times the tube outside diameter. Bends must be smooth and continuous with no evidence of crimping or wall failure. The minimum area moment of inertia, see T 3.2, must be maintained in all areas, including the bends of the manufactured tubes.

rules.display_text: The minimum radius of any bend, measured at the tube centerline, must be at least three times the tube outside diameter. Bends must be smooth and continuous with no evidence of crimping or wall failure. The minimum area moment of inertia, see T 3.2, must be maintained in all areas, including the bends of the manufactured tubes.

blocks.text: In a plane perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle and through the lower endpoints of the roll hoop, no part of the primary structure may lie below 30 mm of the endpoints of the roll hoop.

rules.display_text: In a plane perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle and through the lower endpoints of the roll hoop, no part of the primary structure may lie below 30 mm of the endpoints of the roll hoop.

blocks.text: Roll hoops attached to a composite primary structure must be mechanically attached at the top and bottom of both sides of that structure and at intermediate locations if needed to show equivalency. The lower roll hoop tubing attachment points must be within 50 mm of the endpoints of the roll hoop.

rules.display_text: Roll hoops attached to a composite primary structure must be mechanically attached at the top and bottom of both sides of that structure and at intermediate locations if needed to show equivalency. The lower roll hoop tubing attachment points must be within 50 mm of the endpoints of the roll hoop.

blocks.text: Mounting plates welded to the roll hoops must be at least 2 mm thick steel or 3 mm thick aluminium, dependent of the roll hoop material.

rules.display_text: Mounting plates welded to the roll hoops must be at least 2 mm thick steel or 3 mm thick aluminium, dependent of the roll hoop material.

blocks.text: Both roll hoops must have one 4.5 mm inspection hole in a non-critical straight location. The outer surface of the tube must be unobstructed for at least 180° to allow measurement of the outer tube dimensions.

rules.display_text: Both roll hoops must have one 4.5 mm inspection hole in a non-critical straight location. The outer surface of the tube must be unobstructed for at least 180° to allow measurement of the outer tube dimensions.
changelog: Clarified inspection requirement to ensure accessibility of tube dimensions

blocks.text: If any item which extends outside of the rollover protection envelope is attached to the main hoop and/or main hoop braces, additional bracing is required to prevent bending loads in a rollover situation.

rules.display_text: If any item which extends outside of the rollover protection envelope is attached to the main hoop and/or main hoop braces, additional bracing is required to prevent bending loads in a rollover situation.
changelog: Expanded scope of the additional bracing requirement to items attached to main hoop and main hoop braces, rule moved to roll hoops section

blocks.text: The main hoop must be constructed of a single piece of uncut, continuous, closed section steel tubing.

rules.display_text: The main hoop must be constructed of a single piece of uncut, continuous, closed section steel tubing.

blocks.text: In side view the portion of the main hoop which is above its upper attachment point to the side impact structure must be inclined less than 10° from vertical.

rules.display_text: In side view the portion of the main hoop which is above its upper attachment point to the side impact structure must be inclined less than 10° from vertical.

blocks.text: In side view any bends in the main hoop above its upper attachment point to the primary structure must be braced to a node of the main hoop bracing support structure with tubing meeting the requirements of main hoop bracing.

rules.display_text: In side view any bends in the main hoop above its upper attachment point to the primary structure must be braced to a node of the main hoop bracing support structure with tubing meeting the requirements of main hoop bracing.

blocks.text: In side view any portion lower than the upper attachment point to the side impact structure must be inclined either forward or not more than 10° rearward.

rules.display_text: In side view any portion lower than the upper attachment point to the side impact structure must be inclined either forward or not more than 10° rearward.

blocks.text: The front hoop must be constructed of a continuous and closed section.

rules.display_text: The front hoop must be constructed of a continuous and closed section.

blocks.text: If the front hoop is made from more than one piece it must be supported by node-to-node triangulation or an equivalent construction.

rules.display_text: If the front hoop is made from more than one piece it must be supported by node-to-node triangulation or an equivalent construction.

blocks.text: In side view, no part of the front hoop can be inclined more than 20° from vertical.

rules.display_text: In side view, no part of the front hoop can be inclined more than 20° from vertical.
