blocks.text: If the front hoop is a welded construction made from multiple aluminium profiles, the equivalent yield strength must be considered in the as-welded condition unless the team demonstrates and shows proof that it has been properly solution heat treated and artificially aged. The team must supply sufficient documentation proving the appropriate heat treatment process was performed.

rules.display_text: If the front hoop is a welded construction made from multiple aluminium profiles, the equivalent yield strength must be considered in the as-welded condition unless the team demonstrates and shows proof that it has been properly solution heat treated and artificially aged. The team must supply sufficient documentation proving the appropriate heat treatment process was performed.

blocks.text: The front hoop requires six attachment points, two on each side connecting to the front bulkhead support structures and two connecting to the front hoop bracing, and must therefore show equivalency to 180 kN, as follows from T 3.16.1 and T 3.12.5.

rules.display_text: The front hoop requires six attachment points, two on each side connecting to the front bulkhead support structures and two connecting to the front hoop bracing, and must therefore show equivalency to 180 kN, as follows from T 3.16.1 and T 3.12.5.

blocks.text: Fully laminating the front hoop to the monocoque is acceptable. Fully laminating means that the hoop has to be encapsulated with laminate around its whole circumference, see Figure 6. Equivalence to T 3.8.4 must be shown in the SES. The laminate encapsulating the front hoop must overlap by at least 25 mm on each side. It must have the same lay-up as the laminate that it is connecting to.

rules.display_text:
Fully laminating the front hoop to the monocoque is acceptable. Fully laminating means that the hoop has to be encapsulated with laminate around its whole circumference, see Figure 6. Equivalence to T 3.8.4 must be shown in the SES. The laminate encapsulating the front hoop must overlap by at least 25 mm on each side. It must have the same lay-up as the laminate that it is connecting to.
[Figure 6: Front hoop laminating requirements — see figure on page 29]

blocks.text: The main hoop must be supported to the front or the rear by bracing tubes on each side of the main hoop.

rules.display_text: The main hoop must be supported to the front or the rear by bracing tubes on each side of the main hoop.

blocks.text: In side view the main hoop and the main hoop braces must not lie on the same side of a vertical line coincident with the top of the main hoop.

rules.display_text: In side view the main hoop and the main hoop braces must not lie on the same side of a vertical line coincident with the top of the main hoop.

blocks.text: The main hoop braces must be attached to the main hoop no lower than 160 mm below the top-most surface of the main hoop. The included angle formed by the main hoop and the main hoop braces must be at least 30°.

rules.display_text: The main hoop braces must be attached to the main hoop no lower than 160 mm below the top-most surface of the main hoop. The included angle formed by the main hoop and the main hoop braces must be at least 30°.

blocks.text: The main hoop braces must be straight.

rules.display_text: The main hoop braces must be straight.

blocks.text: The lower ends of the main hoop braces must be supported back to the upper attachment point of the main hoop to the side impact structure and to the lower attachment point of the main hoop to the side impact structure by a node-to-node triangulated structure or equivalent composite structure.

rules.display_text: The lower ends of the main hoop braces must be supported back to the upper attachment point of the main hoop to the side impact structure and to the lower attachment point of the main hoop to the side impact structure by a node-to-node triangulated structure or equivalent composite structure.

blocks.text: The front hoop bracing attaches on each side of the front hoop as well as the structure forward of the driver’s feet. A minimum of two tubes without any bends must be straight on a line in side view of the frame and must have a minimum distance of 100 mm between each other at the front hoop.

rules.display_text: The front hoop bracing attaches on each side of the front hoop as well as the structure forward of the driver’s feet. A minimum of two tubes without any bends must be straight on a line in side view of the frame and must have a minimum distance of 100 mm between each other at the front hoop.

blocks.text: The front hoop bracing structure must be attached no lower than 50 mm below the top-most surface of the front hoop, see Figure 7.

rules.display_text: The front hoop bracing structure must be attached no lower than 50 mm below the top-most surface of the front hoop, see Figure 7.

blocks.text: In side view, any transition into a recessed section of a composite front hoop bracing structure with a depth greater than 50 mm must have a minimum inclination of 30° from vertical.

rules.display_text: In side view, any transition into a recessed section of a composite front hoop bracing structure with a depth greater than 50 mm must have a minimum inclination of 30° from vertical.
changelog: Added minimum inclination requirement for recessed front hoop bracing load paths (e.g. damper recession) in monocoques

blocks.text: If the front hoop is inclined more than 10° to the rear, additional braces extending rearwards are required.

rules.display_text: If the front hoop is inclined more than 10° to the rear, additional braces extending rearwards are required.

blocks.text: Composite front hoop bracing structures and their attachments cannot be counted towards the front bulkhead support structures and vice-versa for the structural equivalency documentation.

rules.display_text: Composite front hoop bracing structures and their attachments cannot be counted towards the front bulkhead support structures and vice-versa for the structural equivalency documentation.

blocks.text: Openings or reductions in effective panel height within a composite front hoop bracing or a composite front bulkhead support must not exceed a total area of 625 cm2.

rules.display_text:
Openings or reductions in effective panel height within a composite front hoop bracing or a composite front bulkhead support must not exceed a total area of 625 cm2.
[Figure 7: Front hoop bracing, main hoop bracing and steering wheel requirements — see figure on page 30]

blocks.text: Any alternative material used for the front bulkhead must have a perimeter shear strength equivalent to a 1.5 mm thick steel plate.

rules.display_text: Any alternative material used for the front bulkhead must have a perimeter shear strength equivalent to a 1.5 mm thick steel plate.

blocks.text: If the front bulkhead is part of a composite structure and is modeled as an “L” shape, the EI of the front bulkhead about the vertical and lateral axes must be equivalent to a steel tube meeting the requirements for the front bulkhead. The length of the section perpendicular to the bulkhead may be a maximum of 25 mm measured from the rearmost face of the bulkhead.

rules.display_text: If the front bulkhead is part of a composite structure and is modeled as an “L” shape, the EI of the front bulkhead about the vertical and lateral axes must be equivalent to a steel tube meeting the requirements for the front bulkhead. The length of the section perpendicular to the bulkhead may be a maximum of 25 mm measured from the rearmost face of the bulkhead.

blocks.text: The front bulkhead must be supported back to the front hoop by a minimum of three tubes on each side; an upper member, a lower member and diagonal bracing to provide triangulation.

The upper support member must be attached to the front bulkhead a maximum of 50 mm below the top-most surface of the front bulkhead, and attached to the front hoop a maximum of 50 mm below the upper side impact member. If the attachment point of the upper member is greater than 100 mm above the upper side impact member, node-to-node triangulated bracing is required to transfer load to the main hoop.
The lower support member must be attached to the base of the front bulkhead and the base of the front hoop.
The diagonal bracing must triangulate the upper and lower support members node-to-node.

rules.display_text:
The front bulkhead must be supported back to the front hoop by a minimum of three tubes on each side; an upper member, a lower member and diagonal bracing to provide triangulation.
▪ The upper support member must be attached to the front bulkhead a maximum of 50 mm below the top-most surface of the front bulkhead, and attached to the front hoop a maximum of 50 mm below the upper side impact member. If the attachment point of the upper member is greater than 100 mm above the upper side impact member, node-to-node triangulated bracing is required to transfer load to the main hoop.
▪ The lower support member must be attached to the base of the front bulkhead and the base of the front hoop.
▪ The diagonal bracing must triangulate the upper and lower support members node-to-node.

blocks.text: If the front bulkhead support is part of a composite structure, it must have equivalent EI to the sum of the EI of the six baseline steel tubes that it replaces and it must not be counted towards the composite front hoop bracing structures for the structural equivalency documentation, i.e. T 3.12.5.

rules.display_text: If the front bulkhead support is part of a composite structure, it must have equivalent EI to the sum of the EI of the six baseline steel tubes that it replaces and it must not be counted towards the composite front hoop bracing structures for the structural equivalency documentation, i.e. T 3.12.5.

blocks.text: The EI of the vertical side of the front bulkhead support structure must be equivalent to at least the EI of one baseline steel tube that it replaces.

rules.display_text: The EI of the vertical side of the front bulkhead support structure must be equivalent to at least the EI of one baseline steel tube that it replaces.

blocks.text: The perimeter shear strength of the monocoque laminate in the front bulkhead support structure must be at least 4 kN.

rules.display_text: The perimeter shear strength of the monocoque laminate in the front bulkhead support structure must be at least 4 kN.

blocks.text: The side impact structure must consist of at least three steel tubes, see T 3.2, on each side of the cockpit, see Figure 8.
The upper member must connect the main hoop and the front hoop.
The upper member must be at a height between 240 mm and 320 mm above the lowest inside chassis point between the front and main hoop.
The lower member must connect the bottom of the main hoop and the bottom of the front hoop.
The diagonal member must triangulate the upper and lower member between the roll hoops node-to-node.

rules.display_text:
The side impact structure must consist of at least three steel tubes, see T 3.2, on each side of the cockpit, see Figure 8.
▪ The upper member must connect the main hoop and the front hoop.
▪ The upper member must be at a height between 240 mm and 320 mm above the lowest inside chassis point between the front and main hoop.
▪ The lower member must connect the bottom of the main hoop and the bottom of the front hoop.
▪ The diagonal member must triangulate the upper and lower member between the roll hoops node-to-node.

blocks.text: Other impact structures, see CV 1.3.2, EV 4.4.2 and EV 5.5.2, must be fully triangulated structures and consist of at least three steel tubes, see T 3.2, on each side and rearward of the component that needs to be protected.
If the component projects outwards from the roll hoops to the side, the front of the component must also be protected.
The upper member must not be higher than 320 mm above the lowest inside chassis point between the front and main hoop.

rules.display_text:
Other impact structures, see CV 1.3.2, EV 4.4.2 and EV 5.5.2, must be fully triangulated structures and consist of at least three steel tubes, see T 3.2, on each side and rearward of the component that needs to be protected.
▪ If the component projects outwards from the roll hoops to the side, the front of the component must also be protected.
▪ The upper member must not be higher than 320 mm above the lowest inside chassis point between the front and main hoop.

blocks.text: No part of the TSAC, motor(s) or mountings may be within 25 mm of the rearmost impact structure. The TSAC must not attach directly to the rearmost impact structure; non-structural components, such as cooling ducts are permitted. A minimum 12.5 mm clearance from each side impact structure must be maintained to the TSAC and motor(s); local attachment to side impact structures and the bottom is allowed.

rules.display_text: No part of the TSAC, motor(s) or mountings may be within 25 mm of the rearmost impact structure. The TSAC must not attach directly to the rearmost impact structure; non-structural components, such as cooling ducts are permitted. A minimum 12.5 mm clearance from each side impact structure must be maintained to the TSAC and motor(s); local attachment to side impact structures and the bottom is allowed.
changelog: Extended the minimum clearance requirement to the side impact structures (12.5 mm); side impact structures (and bottom) may still be used for attachment locally

blocks.text: If the impact structure is part of a composite structure, the following is required:

The region of the structure up to a height of 320 mm above the lowest inside chassis point between the front and main hoop must have an EI equal to the three baseline steel tubes that it replaces. An example for side impact structure is given in Figure 9.
The vertical impact structure must have an EI equivalent to two baseline steel tubes and half the horizontal floor must have an EI equivalent to one baseline steel tube.
The vertical impact structure must have an absorbed energy equivalent to two baseline steel tubes, exceeding 65 J.
The perimeter shear strength must be at least 7.5 kN.

rules.display_text:
If the impact structure is part of a composite structure, the following is required:
▪ The region of the structure up to a height of 320 mm above the lowest inside chassis point between the front and main hoop must have an EI equal to the three baseline steel tubes that it replaces. An example for side impact structure is given in Figure 9.
▪ The vertical impact structure must have an EI equivalent to two baseline steel tubes and half the horizontal floor must have an EI equivalent to one baseline steel tube.
▪ The vertical impact structure must have an absorbed energy equivalent to two baseline steel tubes, exceeding 65 J.
▪ The perimeter shear strength must be at least 7.5 kN.

blocks.text: The rear impact structure must be positioned such that its diagonal member or equivalent composite structure reacts the loads induced by the IA during vehicle impact, for any position of the minimum IA volume up to 350 mm above the ground.

rules.display_text:
The rear impact structure must be positioned such that its diagonal member or equivalent composite structure reacts the loads induced by the IA during vehicle impact, for any position of the minimum IA volume up to 350 mm above the ground.
[Figure 8: Side impact structure — see figure on page 31]
[Figure 9: Side impact structure monocoque — see figure on page 32]
changelog: Added rule to limit hole size in (rear) impact structures whilst maintaining minimum required load paths as an alternative to penetration prevention

blocks.text: If two parts of the primary structure are bolted together, each attachment point between the two parts must be able to carry a load of 30 kN in any direction.

rules.display_text: If two parts of the primary structure are bolted together, each attachment point between the two parts must be able to carry a load of 30 kN in any direction.

blocks.text: Data obtained from the laminate perimeter shear strength test must be used to prove that adequate shear area is provided.

rules.display_text: Data obtained from the laminate perimeter shear strength test must be used to prove that adequate shear area is provided.

blocks.text: Each attachment point requires a minimum of two 8 mm metric grade 8.8 critical fasteners, see T 10.1, and steel backing plates of minimum nominal thickness 2 mm and at least ISO 7093-1 washer size.

rules.display_text: Each attachment point requires a minimum of two 8 mm metric grade 8.8 critical fasteners, see T 10.1, and steel backing plates of minimum nominal thickness 2 mm and at least ISO 7093-1 washer size.
changelog: Clarified steel washers compliant with ISO 7093-1 or equivalent standards may be used as backing plates

blocks.text: For the attachment of front hoop bracing, main hoop bracing and main hoop bracing support to the primary structure the use of one 10 mm metric grade 8.8 bolt is sufficient, if the bolt is on the centerline of the tube, see Figure 10.

rules.display_text:
For the attachment of front hoop bracing, main hoop bracing and main hoop bracing support to the primary structure the use of one 10 mm metric grade 8.8 bolt is sufficient, if the bolt is on the centerline of the tube, see Figure 10.
[Figure 10: Bolted roll hoop bracing support — see figure on page 32]

blocks.text: For the AIP to front bulkhead attachment, and if two panels or plates of the primary structure are bolted together, for each 200 mm of reference perimeter a minimum of one 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolt(s) must be used, rounded up to the next integer. The bolts must be evenly distributed over the circumference using good engineering practices. The reference perimeter is the outside perimeter of the attached part at the connection.

rules.display_text: For the AIP to front bulkhead attachment, and if two panels or plates of the primary structure are bolted together, for each 200 mm of reference perimeter a minimum of one 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolt(s) must be used, rounded up to the next integer. The bolts must be evenly distributed over the circumference using good engineering practices. The reference perimeter is the outside perimeter of the attached part at the connection.
changelog: Clarified rule by removing redundant sentence

blocks.text: For each bolt and its corresponding insert of T 3.16.5 an exception in favor of blind inserts or alternative backing plate dimensions may be given only if the actual configuration is physically tested and documented in the SES and/or ASES. Each bolt and its corresponding insert must withstand a force of 15 kN in both the axial pull-out and the weakest radial direction.

rules.display_text: For each bolt and its corresponding insert of T 3.16.5 an exception in favor of blind inserts or alternative backing plate dimensions may be given only if the actual configuration is physically tested and documented in the SES and/or ASES. Each bolt and its corresponding insert must withstand a force of 15 kN in both the axial pull-out and the weakest radial direction.
changelog: Allowed alternative backing plate dimensions only for physically tested attachments (blind inserts)

blocks.text: Each vehicle must be equipped with an IA assembly consisting of an IA and AIP.

rules.display_text: Each vehicle must be equipped with an IA assembly consisting of an IA and AIP.

blocks.text: The IA must:
be installed forward of the front bulkhead.
be at least 100 mm high and 200 mm wide for a minimum distance of 200 mm forward of the front bulkhead.
not be positioned more than 350 mm above the ground, for any portion of the required 100 mm × 200 mm × 200 mm volume, in any ready-to-race configuration.
not be able to penetrate the front bulkhead in the event of an impact.
be securely mounted directly to the AIP.
not be part of the non-structural bodywork.
be designed with a closed front section.
not be wider or higher than the AIP.

rules.display_text:
The IA must:
▪ be installed forward of the front bulkhead.
▪ be at least 100 mm high and 200 mm wide for a minimum distance of 200 mm forward of the front bulkhead.
▪ not be positioned more than 350 mm above the ground, for any portion of the required 100 mm × 200 mm × 200 mm volume, in any ready-to-race configuration.
▪ not be able to penetrate the front bulkhead in the event of an impact.
▪ be securely mounted directly to the AIP.
▪ not be part of the non-structural bodywork.
▪ be designed with a closed front section.
▪ not be wider or higher than the AIP.
changelog: Specified IA position in ready-to-race configuration

blocks.text: The baseline design for the Anti Intrusion Plate (AIP) is a 1.5 mm solid steel or 4.0 mm solid aluminium plate.
If the IA and AIP (IA assembly) are bolted to the front bulkhead, it must be the same size as the outside dimensions of the front bulkhead.
If it is welded to the front bulkhead, it must extend at least to the centerline of the front bulkhead tubing in all directions.
The AIP must not extend past the outside edges of the front bulkhead.

rules.display_text:
The baseline design for the Anti Intrusion Plate (AIP) is a 1.5 mm solid steel or 4.0 mm solid aluminium plate.
▪ If the IA and AIP (IA assembly) are bolted to the front bulkhead, it must be the same size as the outside dimensions of the front bulkhead.
▪ If it is welded to the front bulkhead, it must extend at least to the centerline of the front bulkhead tubing in all directions.
▪ The AIP must not extend past the outside edges of the front bulkhead.

blocks.text: Alternative AIP designs are permissible if equivalency to T 3.17.3 is proven by physical testing as in T 3.19.2.

rules.display_text: Alternative AIP designs are permissible if equivalency to T 3.17.3 is proven by physical testing as in T 3.19.2.

blocks.text: The IA may be attached to the AIP by a minimum of four 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolts that are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10. Attachment(s) using adhesive must be able to carry a load of 60 kN in any direction.

rules.display_text: The IA may be attached to the AIP by a minimum of four 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolts that are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10. Attachment(s) using adhesive must be able to carry a load of 60 kN in any direction.

blocks.text: The attachment of the IA assembly must be designed to provide an adequate load path for transverse and vertical loads in the event of off-center and off-axis impacts. Segmented foam attenuators must have the segments bonded together to prevent sliding or parallelogramming.

rules.display_text: The attachment of the IA assembly must be designed to provide an adequate load path for transverse and vertical loads in the event of off-center and off-axis impacts. Segmented foam attenuators must have the segments bonded together to prevent sliding or parallelogramming.

blocks.text: A team may use one of the “standard” FSAE IAs without physical testing, provided that all of the following is fulfilled:

A 1.5 mm solid steel AIP is used, that is welded along its full perimeter to a steel bulkhead or a 4 mm solid aluminium AIP is used, that is bolted to any bulkhead with a minimum of eight 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolts.
The adhesive used to mount the “standard” IA to the AIP has a shear strength of at least 24 MPa.
T 3.19.4 is fulfilled regarding aerodynamic device and sensor positions relative to the AIP.

If the front bulkhead has an overall width greater than 400 mm and/or an overall height greater than 350 mm, a diagonal or X-bracing that is a front bulkhead support tube or an approved equivalent per T 3.2, or equivalent for monocoque bulkheads, must be included.
If the “standard” honeycomb IA is used, the IA must be of pre-crushed type.
If one or more of the above conditions are not met, physical testing must be carried out to prove that the AIP does not permanently deflect more than 25 mm.

rules.display_text:
A team may use one of the “standard” FSAE IAs without physical testing, provided that all of the following is fulfilled:
▪ A 1.5 mm solid steel AIP is used, that is welded along its full perimeter to a steel bulkhead or a 4 mm solid aluminium AIP is used, that is bolted to any bulkhead with a minimum of eight 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolts.
▪ The adhesive used to mount the “standard” IA to the AIP has a shear strength of at least 24 MPa.
▪ T 3.19.4 is fulfilled regarding aerodynamic device and sensor positions relative to the AIP.
▪ If the front bulkhead has an overall width greater than 400 mm and/or an overall height greater than 350 mm, a diagonal or X-bracing that is a front bulkhead support tube or an approved equivalent per T 3.2, or equivalent for monocoque bulkheads, must be included.
▪ If the “standard” honeycomb IA is used, the IA must be of pre-crushed type.
If one or more of the above conditions are not met, physical testing must be carried out to prove that the AIP does not permanently deflect more than 25 mm.

blocks.text: All teams must submit an IA data report using the Impact Attenuator Data (IAD) template provided at the competition website.

rules.display_text: All teams must submit an IA data report using the Impact Attenuator Data (IAD) template provided at the competition website.

blocks.text: The IA assembly, when mounted on the front of a vehicle with a total mass of 300 kg and impacting a solid, non-yielding impact barrier with a velocity of impact of 7 m/s, must meet the following requirements:
Decelerate the vehicle at a rate not exceeding 20 g average and 40 g peak.
The energy absorbed in this event must meet or exceed 7350 J.
Teams using the standard IA are not required to submit test data with their IAD report, but all other requirements must be included.

Equivalent (higher) test velocities are only allowed to accommodate for a lower total testing mass, as long as the energy absorbed is 7350 J or more. If these requirements cannot be met, a team must use the standard IA.

rules.display_text:
The IA assembly, when mounted on the front of a vehicle with a total mass of 300 kg and impacting a solid, non-yielding impact barrier with a velocity of impact of 7 m/s, must meet the following requirements:
▪ Decelerate the vehicle at a rate not exceeding 20 g average and 40 g peak.
▪ The energy absorbed in this event must meet or exceed 7350 J.
▪ Teams using the standard IA are not required to submit test data with their IAD report, but all other requirements must be included.
Equivalent (higher) test velocities are only allowed to accommodate for a lower total testing mass, as long as the energy absorbed is 7350 J or more. If these requirements cannot be met, a team must use the standard IA.

blocks.text: During the IA test:
The IA must be attached to the AIP using the intended vehicle attachment method.

The IA assembly must be attached to a test fixture that has geometry representative of the intended primary structure and equal or higher stiffness and strength. When no baseline design for the AIP is used, see T 3.17.3, the test fixture must be a copy of the intended primary structure (i.e. materials, lay-up, joining methods).
There must be at least 50 mm clearance rearwards of the AIP to the test fixture.
No part of the AIP may permanently deflect more than 25 mm beyond the position of the AIP before the test.
The representative test fixture of the intended primary structure may not be structurally compromised (i.e. no cracks) after the test.

rules.display_text:
During the IA test:
▪ The IA must be attached to the AIP using the intended vehicle attachment method.
▪ The IA assembly must be attached to a test fixture that has geometry representative of the intended primary structure and equal or higher stiffness and strength. When no baseline design for the AIP is used, see T 3.17.3, the test fixture must be a copy of the intended primary structure (i.e. materials, lay-up, joining methods).
▪ There must be at least 50 mm clearance rearwards of the AIP to the test fixture.
▪ No part of the AIP may permanently deflect more than 25 mm beyond the position of the AIP before the test.
▪ The representative test fixture of the intended primary structure may not be structurally compromised (i.e. no cracks) after the test.

blocks.text: Teams using IAs (typically structural noses) directly attached to the front bulkhead, which shortcut the load path through the bulk of the AIP, must conduct an additional test. This test must prove that the AIP can withstand a load of 120 kN (300 kg multiplied by 40 g), where the load applicator matches the minimum IA dimensions.

rules.display_text: Teams using IAs (typically structural noses) directly attached to the front bulkhead, which shortcut the load path through the bulk of the AIP, must conduct an additional test. This test must prove that the AIP can withstand a load of 120 kN (300 kg multiplied by 40 g), where the load applicator matches the minimum IA dimensions.

blocks.text: Vehicles with aerodynamic devices and/or sensors forward of the front bulkhead must not exceed the peak deceleration of T 3.19.1 for the combination of their IA assembly and the non-crushable object(s). One of the following three methods must be used to prove the design does not exceed 120 kN:

Physical testing of the IA assembly including any non-crushable object(s) or geometrically representative dummies thereof forward of the AIP. When non-crushable object(s) are located in front view of the AIP, physical testing is required.
Combining the peak force from physical testing of the IA assembly with the failure load for the mounting of the non-crushable object(s), calculated from fastener shear and/or link buckling.
Combining the “standard” IA peak load of 95 kN with the failure load for the mounting of the non-crushable object(s), calculated from fastener shear and/or link buckling.

rules.display_text:
Vehicles with aerodynamic devices and/or sensors forward of the front bulkhead must not exceed the peak deceleration of T 3.19.1 for the combination of their IA assembly and the non-crushable object(s). One of the following three methods must be used to prove the design does not exceed 120 kN:
▪ Physical testing of the IA assembly including any non-crushable object(s) or geometrically representative dummies thereof forward of the AIP. When non-crushable object(s) are located in front view of the AIP, physical testing is required.
▪ Combining the peak force from physical testing of the IA assembly with the failure load for the mounting of the non-crushable object(s), calculated from fastener shear and/or link buckling.
▪ Combining the “standard” IA peak load of 95 kN with the failure load for the mounting of the non-crushable object(s), calculated from fastener shear and/or link buckling.

blocks.text: Dynamic testing (sled, pendulum, drop tower, etc.) of the IA may only be conducted at a dedicated test facility. This facility may be part of the university, but must be supervised by professional staff. Teams are not allowed to design their own dynamic test apparatus.

rules.display_text: Dynamic testing (sled, pendulum, drop tower, etc.) of the IA may only be conducted at a dedicated test facility. This facility may be part of the university, but must be supervised by professional staff. Teams are not allowed to design their own dynamic test apparatus.

blocks.text: When using acceleration data from the dynamic test, the average deceleration must be calculated based on the raw unfiltered data. If peaks above the 40 g limit are present in the data, a 100 Hz, 3rd order, low pass Butterworth (−3 dB at 100 Hz) filter may be applied.

rules.display_text: When using acceleration data from the dynamic test, the average deceleration must be calculated based on the raw unfiltered data. If peaks above the 40 g limit are present in the data, a 100 Hz, 3rd order, low pass Butterworth (−3 dB at 100 Hz) filter may be applied.

blocks.text: All non-crushable objects (e.g. pedals, master cylinders, hydraulic reservoirs) must be rearward of the rear most plane of the front bulkhead and at least 25 mm behind the AIP at any time, except for sensors, aerodynamic devices and their mountings.

rules.display_text: All non-crushable objects (e.g. pedals, master cylinders, hydraulic reservoirs) must be rearward of the rear most plane of the front bulkhead and at least 25 mm behind the AIP at any time, except for sensors, aerodynamic devices and their mountings.

blocks.text: Sensor and aerodynamic devices may extend forward of the AIP, but their chassis attachment point must be located rearward of the AIP.

rules.display_text: Sensor and aerodynamic devices may extend forward of the AIP, but their chassis attachment point must be located rearward of the AIP.

blocks.text: The size of the cockpit opening needs to be sufficient for the template shown on the left of Figure 11 to pass vertically from the cockpit opening to below the upper side impact member when held horizontally. The template may be moved fore and aft.

rules.display_text: The size of the cockpit opening needs to be sufficient for the template shown on the left of Figure 11 to pass vertically from the cockpit opening to below the upper side impact member when held horizontally. The template may be moved fore and aft.

blocks.text: If the side impact structure is not made of tubes, the template must pass until it is 320 mm above the lowest inside chassis point between the front and main hoop.

rules.display_text: If the side impact structure is not made of tubes, the template must pass until it is 320 mm above the lowest inside chassis point between the front and main hoop.

blocks.text: The steering wheel, seat and all padding may be removed for the template to fit. Any other parts may only be removed if they are integrated with the steering wheel.

rules.display_text: The steering wheel, seat and all padding may be removed for the template to fit. Any other parts may only be removed if they are integrated with the steering wheel.

blocks.text: The cockpit must provide a free internal cross section sufficient for the template shown on the right in Figure 11 to pass from the cockpit opening to a point 100 mm rearwards of the face of the rearmost pedal in an inoperative position. The template may be moved up and down. Adjustable pedals must be in their most forward position.

rules.display_text: The cockpit must provide a free internal cross section sufficient for the template shown on the right in Figure 11 to pass from the cockpit opening to a point 100 mm rearwards of the face of the rearmost pedal in an inoperative position. The template may be moved up and down. Adjustable pedals must be in their most forward position.

blocks.text: The steering wheel and any padding that can be removed without the use of tools while the driver is seated may be removed for the template to fit.

rules.display_text: The steering wheel and any padding that can be removed without the use of tools while the driver is seated may be removed for the template to fit.

blocks.text: The driver’s feet and legs must be completely contained within the primary structure when the driver is seated normally and the driver’s feet are touching the pedals. In side and front views, any part of the driver’s feet or legs must not extend above or outside of this structure.

rules.display_text:
The driver’s feet and legs must be completely contained within the primary structure when the driver is seated normally and the driver’s feet are touching the pedals. In side and front views, any part of the driver’s feet or legs must not extend above or outside of this structure.
[Figure 11: Cockpit opening template (left) and cockpit internal cross section template (right) — see figure on page 35]

blocks.text: When seated normally and restrained by the driver’s restraint system, the helmet of a 95th percentile male and all of the team’s drivers must, see Figure 12:
be a minimum of 50 mm away from the straight line drawn from the top of the main hoop to the top of the front hoop.
be a minimum of 50 mm away from the straight line drawn from the top of the main hoop to the lower end of the main hoop bracing if the bracing extends rearwards.
be no further rearwards than the rear surface of the main hoop if the main hoop bracing extends forwards.

rules.display_text:
When seated normally and restrained by the driver’s restraint system, the helmet of a 95th percentile male and all of the team’s drivers must, see Figure 12:
▪ be a minimum of 50 mm away from the straight line drawn from the top of the main hoop to the top of the front hoop.
▪ be a minimum of 50 mm away from the straight line drawn from the top of the main hoop to the lower end of the main hoop bracing if the bracing extends rearwards.
▪ be no further rearwards than the rear surface of the main hoop if the main hoop bracing extends forwards.
[Figure 12: Minimum helmet clearance — see figure on page 36]

blocks.text: The 95th percentile male is represented by a two dimensional figure consisting of two circles of 200 mm diameter (one representing the hips and buttocks and one representing the shoulder region) and one circle of 300 mm (representing the head with helmet).

rules.display_text: The 95th percentile male is represented by a two dimensional figure consisting of two circles of 200 mm diameter (one representing the hips and buttocks and one representing the shoulder region) and one circle of 300 mm (representing the head with helmet).

blocks.text: The two 200 mm circles are connected by a straight line measuring 490 mm. The 300 mm circle is connected by a straight line measuring 280 mm with the upper 200 mm circle.

rules.display_text: The two 200 mm circles are connected by a straight line measuring 490 mm. The 300 mm circle is connected by a straight line measuring 280 mm with the upper 200 mm circle.

blocks.text: The figure has to be positioned in the vehicle as follows, see Figure 13:
The seat adjusted to the rearmost position
The pedals adjusted to the frontmost position
The bottom 200 mm circle placed on the seat bottom. The distance between the center of the circle and the rearmost actuation face of the pedals must be minimum 915 mm.
The middle circle positioned on the seat back
The upper 300 mm circle positioned 25 mm away from the head restraint.

rules.display_text:
The figure has to be positioned in the vehicle as follows, see Figure 13:
▪ The seat adjusted to the rearmost position
▪ The pedals adjusted to the frontmost position
▪ The bottom 200 mm circle placed on the seat bottom. The distance between the center of the circle and the rearmost actuation face of the pedals must be minimum 915 mm.
▪ The middle circle positioned on the seat back
▪ The upper 300 mm circle positioned 25 mm away from the head restraint.
[Figure 13: Percy placement — see figure on page 36]

blocks.text: If there is any chassis member alongside the driver at the height of the neck of any of the drivers in the team, a metal tube or piece of sheet metal must be attached to the chassis to prevent the driver’s shoulders from passing under that chassis member.

rules.display_text: If there is any chassis member alongside the driver at the height of the neck of any of the drivers in the team, a metal tube or piece of sheet metal must be attached to the chassis to prevent the driver’s shoulders from passing under that chassis member.

blocks.text: Any harness attachment to a monocoque must be using one 10 mm metric grade 8.8 bolt or two 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolts (or bolts of an equivalent standard) and steel backing plates with a minimum thickness of 2 mm.

rules.display_text: Any harness attachment to a monocoque must be using one 10 mm metric grade 8.8 bolt or two 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolts (or bolts of an equivalent standard) and steel backing plates with a minimum thickness of 2 mm.

blocks.text: Any harness that is fastened to the primary structure using brackets must use two 8 mm metric grade 8.8 or stronger fasteners.

rules.display_text: Any harness that is fastened to the primary structure using brackets must use two 8 mm metric grade 8.8 or stronger fasteners.

blocks.text: It must be proven that the attachments for shoulder and lap belts can support a load of 13 kN and the attachment points of the anti-submarine belts can support a load of 6.5 kN.

rules.display_text: It must be proven that the attachments for shoulder and lap belts can support a load of 13 kN and the attachment points of the anti-submarine belts can support a load of 6.5 kN.

blocks.text: If the lap belts and anti-submarine belts are attached less than 100 mm apart, these must support a total load of 19.5 kN.

rules.display_text: If the lap belts and anti-submarine belts are attached less than 100 mm apart, these must support a total load of 19.5 kN.

blocks.text: If the belts are attached to a laminated structure or the mounting brackets and tabs are not made from steel at least 1.6 mm thick, physical testing is required. The following requirements must be met:
Load is applied to a test sample representing the tubular or laminated structure and must use the same brackets and tabs
Edges of the test fixture supporting the sample must be a minimum of 125 mm from the load application point.
The width of the shoulder harness test sample must not be any wider than the shoulder harness panel height used to show equivalency for the shoulder harness mounting bar.
Designs with attachments near a free edge must not support the free edge during the test.
Harness loads must be tested with the worst case for the range of the angles specified for the driver’s harness.

rules.display_text:
If the belts are attached to a laminated structure or the mounting brackets and tabs are not made from steel at least 1.6 mm thick, physical testing is required. The following requirements must be met:
▪ Load is applied to a test sample representing the tubular or laminated structure and must use the same brackets and tabs
▪ Edges of the test fixture supporting the sample must be a minimum of 125 mm from the load application point.
▪ The width of the shoulder harness test sample must not be any wider than the shoulder harness panel height used to show equivalency for the shoulder harness mounting bar.
▪ Designs with attachments near a free edge must not support the free edge during the test.
▪ Harness loads must be tested with the worst case for the range of the angles specified for the driver’s harness.

blocks.text: The lowest point of the driver’s seat must in side view not extend below the upper face of the lowest side impact structure member or have a longitudinal tube (or tubes) that meets the material requirements for the side impact structure, see T 3.2, passing underneath the lowest point of the seat.

rules.display_text: The lowest point of the driver’s seat must in side view not extend below the upper face of the lowest side impact structure member or have a longitudinal tube (or tubes) that meets the material requirements for the side impact structure, see T 3.2, passing underneath the lowest point of the seat.

blocks.text: Adequate heat insulation must be provided to ensure that the driver is not able to contact any parts of the vehicle with a surface temperature above 60 °C. The insulation may be external to the cockpit or incorporated with the driver’s seat or firewall. The design must address all three types of heat transfer with the following minimum requirements between the heat source and the part that the driver could contact:
Conduction insulation by:
No direct contact, or
a heat resistant, conduction insulation material with a minimum thickness of 8 mm.
Convection insulation by a minimum air gap of 25 mm.
Radiation insulation by:
A solid metal heat shield with a minimum thickness of 0.4 mm or
reflective foil or tape when combined with T 4.6.2.a.ii.

rules.display_text:
Adequate heat insulation must be provided to ensure that the driver is not able to contact any parts of the vehicle with a surface temperature above 60 °C. The insulation may be external to the cockpit or incorporated with the driver’s seat or firewall. The design must address all three types of heat transfer with the following minimum requirements between the heat source and the part that the driver could contact:
(a) Conduction insulation by:
  (i) No direct contact, or
  (ii) a heat resistant, conduction insulation material with a minimum thickness of 8 mm.
(b) Convection insulation by a minimum air gap of 25 mm.
(c) Radiation insulation by:
  (i) A solid metal heat shield with a minimum thickness of 0.4 mm or
  (ii) reflective foil or tape when combined with T 4.6.2.a.ii.

blocks.text: All vehicles must have a floor closeout made of one or more panels, which separate the driver from the ground.

rules.display_text: All vehicles must have a floor closeout made of one or more panels, which separate the driver from the ground.

blocks.text: The closeout must extend from the front bulkhead to the firewall.

rules.display_text: The closeout must extend from the front bulkhead to the firewall.

blocks.text: The panels must be made of a solid, non-brittle material.

rules.display_text: The panels must be made of a solid, non-brittle material.

blocks.text: If multiple panels are used, gaps between panels must not exceed 3 mm.

rules.display_text: If multiple panels are used, gaps between panels must not exceed 3 mm.

blocks.text: A firewall must separate the cockpit from all components of the fuel supply system, hydraulic fluid (except brake system and dampers), flammable liquids, the LV battery and any TS component, see EV 1.1.1.

rules.display_text: A firewall must separate the cockpit from all components of the fuel supply system, hydraulic fluid (except brake system and dampers), flammable liquids, the LV battery and any TS component, see EV 1.1.1.

blocks.text: The firewall must cover any straight line between the parts mentioned in T 4.8.1 and any part of the tallest driver below a plane 100 mm above the bottom of the helmet.

rules.display_text: The firewall must cover any straight line between the parts mentioned in T 4.8.1 and any part of the tallest driver below a plane 100 mm above the bottom of the helmet.

blocks.text: The firewall must be a non-permeable surface made from a rigid, fire resistant material, see T 1.2.1, which must be securely mounted to the vehicle’s structure.

rules.display_text: The firewall must be a non-permeable surface made from a rigid, fire resistant material, see T 1.2.1, which must be securely mounted to the vehicle’s structure.

blocks.text: Any firewall must seal completely against the passage of fluids, especially at the sides and the floor of the cockpit.

rules.display_text: Any firewall must seal completely against the passage of fluids, especially at the sides and the floor of the cockpit.

blocks.text: Pass-throughs for wiring, cables, etc. are allowed if grommets, cable glands or connectors are used to seal the pass-through.

rules.display_text: Pass-throughs for wiring, cables, etc. are allowed if grommets, cable glands or connectors are used to seal the pass-through.

blocks.text: Multiple panels may be used to form the firewall but must overlap at least 5 mm and be sealed at the joints. Any sealing material must not be vital to the structural integrity of the firewall.

rules.display_text: Multiple panels may be used to form the firewall but must overlap at least 5 mm and be sealed at the joints. Any sealing material must not be vital to the structural integrity of the firewall.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] The TS firewall between driver and TS components must be composed of two layers:
One solid layer, facing the TS side, must be made of aluminium with a thickness of at least 0.5 mm. This part of the TS firewall must be grounded according to EV 3.1.
The second layer, facing the driver, must be made of an electrically insulating and fire retardant material, see T 1.2.1. The second layer must not be made of CFRP.
The thickness of the second layer must be sufficient to prevent penetrating this layer with a 4 mm wide screwdriver and 250 N of force.
A sample of the TS firewall must be presented at Technical Inspection.

rules.display_text:
[EV ONLY] The TS firewall between driver and TS components must be composed of two layers:
▪ One solid layer, facing the TS side, must be made of aluminium with a thickness of at least 0.5 mm. This part of the TS firewall must be grounded according to EV 3.1.
▪ The second layer, facing the driver, must be made of an electrically insulating and fire retardant material, see T 1.2.1. The second layer must not be made of CFRP.
▪ The thickness of the second layer must be sufficient to prevent penetrating this layer with a 4 mm wide screwdriver and 250 N of force.
A sample of the TS firewall must be presented at Technical Inspection.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] Conductive parts, except for the chassis and firewall mounting points, must not protrude through the TS firewall or must be properly insulated on the driver’s side. The driver must not be able to touch uninsulated firewall mounting points while operating the vehicle.

rules.display_text: [EV ONLY] Conductive parts, except for the chassis and firewall mounting points, must not protrude through the TS firewall or must be properly insulated on the driver’s side. The driver must not be able to touch uninsulated firewall mounting points while operating the vehicle.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] TS parts outside of the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16 and EV 4.4.3, do not need a firewall.

rules.display_text: [EV ONLY] TS parts outside of the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16 and EV 4.4.3, do not need a firewall.

blocks.text: All vehicle controls must be operated from inside the cockpit without any part of the driver, e.g. hands, arms or elbows, being outside the vertical planes tangent to the outermost surface of the side impact structure.

rules.display_text: All vehicle controls must be operated from inside the cockpit without any part of the driver, e.g. hands, arms or elbows, being outside the vertical planes tangent to the outermost surface of the side impact structure.

blocks.text: The driver must have adequate visibility to the front and sides of the vehicle. Seated in a normal driving position, the driver must have a minimum field of vision of 100° to either side. The required visibility may be obtained by the driver turning their head and/or the use of mirrors.

rules.display_text: The driver must have adequate visibility to the front and sides of the vehicle. Seated in a normal driving position, the driver must have a minimum field of vision of 100° to either side. The required visibility may be obtained by the driver turning their head and/or the use of mirrors.

blocks.text: If mirrors are required to meet T 4.10.1, they must remain in place and be adjusted to enable the required visibility throughout all dynamic disciplines.

rules.display_text: If mirrors are required to meet T 4.10.1, they must remain in place and be adjusted to enable the required visibility throughout all dynamic disciplines.

blocks.text: All drivers must be able to exit to the side of the vehicle in less than 5 s with the driver in the fully seated position, hands in the driving position on the connected steering wheel (in all possible steering system positions) and wearing the required driver equipment as in T 13.3. The egress time stops when the driver has both feet on the ground.

rules.display_text: All drivers must be able to exit to the side of the vehicle in less than 5 s with the driver in the fully seated position, hands in the driving position on the connected steering wheel (in all possible steering system positions) and wearing the required driver equipment as in T 13.3. The egress time stops when the driver has both feet on the ground.

blocks.text: 6-point system — consists of a two-piece lap belt (minimum width 50 mm), two shoulder straps (minimum width 75 mm) and two leg or anti-submarine straps (minimum width 50 mm).

rules.display_text: 6-point system — consists of a two-piece lap belt (minimum width 50 mm), two shoulder straps (minimum width 75 mm) and two leg or anti-submarine straps (minimum width 50 mm).

blocks.text: 7-point system — same as the 6-point system except it has three anti-submarine straps.

rules.display_text: 7-point system — same as the 6-point system except it has three anti-submarine straps.

blocks.text: upright driving position — position with a seat back angled at 30° or less from the vertical as measured along the line joining the two 200 mm circles of the 95th percentile male template as defined in T 4.3 and positioned per T 4.3.4.

rules.display_text: upright driving position — position with a seat back angled at 30° or less from the vertical as measured along the line joining the two 200 mm circles of the 95th percentile male template as defined in T 4.3 and positioned per T 4.3.4.

blocks.text: reclined driving position — position with a seat back angled at more than 30° from the vertical as measured along the line joining the two 200 mm circles of the 95th percentile male template as defined in T 4.3 and positioned per T 4.3.4

rules.display_text: reclined driving position — position with a seat back angled at more than 30° from the vertical as measured along the line joining the two 200 mm circles of the 95th percentile male template as defined in T 4.3 and positioned per T 4.3.4

blocks.text: All drivers must use a 6-point or 7-point restraint harness meeting the following specifications:
All driver restraint systems must meet SFI Specification 16.1, SFI Specification 16.5, SFI Specification 16.6 or FIA specification 8853/2016.
The belts must bear the appropriate dated labels.
The material of all straps must be in perfect condition.
There must be a single metal-to-metal latch type quick release for all straps.

All lap belts must incorporate a tilt lock adjuster (“quick adjuster”). A tilt lock adjuster in each portion of the lap belt is highly recommended. Lap belts with “pull-up” adjusters are recommended over “pull-down” adjusters.
Vehicles with a “reclined driving position” must have either anti-submarine belts with tilt lock adjusters (“quick adjusters”) or have two sets of anti-submarine belts installed.
The shoulder harness must be the “over-the-shoulder type”. Only separate shoulder straps are allowed (i.e. “Y”-type shoulder straps are not allowed). The “H”-type configuration is allowed.
The shoulder harness straps must be threaded through the three bar adjusters in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.
When a Frontal Head Restraint (FHR) device is used by the driver, minimum 50 mm wide shoulder harnesses are allowed.

rules.display_text:
All drivers must use a 6-point or 7-point restraint harness meeting the following specifications:
▪ All driver restraint systems must meet SFI Specification 16.1, SFI Specification 16.5, SFI Specification 16.6 or FIA specification 8853/2016.
▪ The belts must bear the appropriate dated labels.
▪ The material of all straps must be in perfect condition.
▪ There must be a single metal-to-metal latch type quick release for all straps.
▪ All lap belts must incorporate a tilt lock adjuster (“quick adjuster”). A tilt lock adjuster in each portion of the lap belt is highly recommended. Lap belts with “pull-up” adjusters are recommended over “pull-down” adjusters.
▪ Vehicles with a “reclined driving position” must have either anti-submarine belts with tilt lock adjusters (“quick adjusters”) or have two sets of anti-submarine belts installed.
▪ The shoulder harness must be the “over-the-shoulder type”. Only separate shoulder straps are allowed (i.e. “Y”-type shoulder straps are not allowed). The “H”-type configuration is allowed.
▪ The shoulder harness straps must be threaded through the three bar adjusters in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.
▪ When a Frontal Head Restraint (FHR) device is used by the driver, minimum 50 mm wide shoulder harnesses are allowed.
