blocks.text: SFI spec harnesses must be replaced following December 31st of the 2nd year after the date of manufacture as indicated by the label. FIA spec harnesses must be replaced following December 31st of the year marked on the label.

rules.display_text: SFI spec harnesses must be replaced following December 31st of the 2nd year after the date of manufacture as indicated by the label. FIA spec harnesses must be replaced following December 31st of the year marked on the label.

blocks.text: The restraint system must be worn tightly at all times.

rules.display_text: The restraint system must be worn tightly at all times.

rules.title: Belt, Strap and Harness Installation - General
rules.section_title: Belt, Strap and Harness Installation - General
Belt, Strap and Harness Installation - General

blocks.text: The lap belt, shoulder harness and anti-submarine strap(s) must be securely mounted to the primary structure. This structure and any guide or support for the belts must meet the minimum requirements of T 3.2.

rules.display_text: The lap belt, shoulder harness and anti-submarine strap(s) must be securely mounted to the primary structure. This structure and any guide or support for the belts must meet the minimum requirements of T 3.2.

rules.section_title: Belt, Strap and Harness Installation - General

blocks.text: Harnesses, belts and straps must not pass through a firewall, i.e. all harness attachment points must be on the driver’s side of any firewall.

rules.display_text: Harnesses, belts and straps must not pass through a firewall, i.e. all harness attachment points must be on the driver’s side of any firewall.

rules.section_title: Belt, Strap and Harness Installation - General

blocks.text: The attachment of the driver’s restraint system requires an approved SES per T 3.7. The lap belts and anti submarine belts must not be routed over the sides of the seat. Where the belts or harness pass through a hole in the seat, the seat must be rolled or grommeted to prevent chafing of the belts.

rules.display_text: The attachment of the driver’s restraint system requires an approved SES per T 3.7. The lap belts and anti submarine belts must not be routed over the sides of the seat. Where the belts or harness pass through a hole in the seat, the seat must be rolled or grommeted to prevent chafing of the belts.

blocks.text: The lap belt must pass around the pelvic area below the anterior superior iliac spines (the hip bones).

rules.display_text: The lap belt must pass around the pelvic area below the anterior superior iliac spines (the hip bones).

blocks.text: The lap belts must come through the seat at the bottom of the sides of the seat to maximize the wrap of the pelvic surface and continue in a straight line to the anchorage point.

rules.display_text: The lap belts must come through the seat at the bottom of the sides of the seat to maximize the wrap of the pelvic surface and continue in a straight line to the anchorage point.

blocks.text: In side view, the lap belt must be capable of pivoting freely by using either a shouldered bolt or an eye bolt attachment.

rules.display_text: In side view, the lap belt must be capable of pivoting freely by using either a shouldered bolt or an eye bolt attachment.

blocks.text: With an “upright driving position”, in side view the lap belt must be at an angle of between 45 ° and 65° to the horizontal.

rules.display_text: With an “upright driving position”, in side view the lap belt must be at an angle of between 45 ° and 65° to the horizontal.

blocks.text: With a “reclined driving position”, in side view the lap belt must be between an angle of 60° and 80° to the horizontal.

rules.display_text: With a “reclined driving position”, in side view the lap belt must be between an angle of 60° and 80° to the horizontal.

blocks.text: In “upright driving position” the centerline of the lap belt at the seat bottom should be between 0 mm to 76 mm forward of the seat back to seat bottom junction as in Figure 14. In “reclined driving position” it may also be rearward of the junction point.

rules.display_text: In “upright driving position” the centerline of the lap belt at the seat bottom should be between 0 mm to 76 mm forward of the seat back to seat bottom junction as in Figure 14. In “reclined driving position” it may also be rearward of the junction point.

blocks.text: The shoulder harness must be mounted behind the driver to a structure that meets the requirements of the primary structure. However, it cannot be mounted to the main hoop bracing or attendant structure without additional bracing to prevent loads being transferred into the main hoop bracing.

rules.display_text: The shoulder harness must be mounted behind the driver to a structure that meets the requirements of the primary structure. However, it cannot be mounted to the main hoop bracing or attendant structure without additional bracing to prevent loads being transferred into the main hoop bracing.

blocks.text: If the harness is mounted to a tube that is not straight, the joints between this tube and the structure to which it is mounted must be reinforced in side view by triangulation tubes to prevent torsional rotation of the harness mounting tube. Supporting calculations are required. Analysis method: Use 7 kN load per attachment and the range of angles in T 5.5.5, calculate that the bent shoulder harness bar triangulation stresses are less than as welded yield strength T 3.2.4 for combined bending and shear and does not fail in column buckling. If the team chooses not to perform the strength analysis T 3.2.6 applies.

rules.display_text: If the harness is mounted to a tube that is not straight, the joints between this tube and the structure to which it is mounted must be reinforced in side view by triangulation tubes to prevent torsional rotation of the harness mounting tube. Supporting calculations are required. Analysis method: Use 7 kN load per attachment and the range of angles in T 5.5.5, calculate that the bent shoulder harness bar triangulation stresses are less than as welded yield strength T 3.2.4 for combined bending and shear and does not fail in column buckling. If the team chooses not to perform the strength analysis T 3.2.6 applies.

blocks.text: The strength of any shoulder harness bar and bracing tubes must be proven in the relevant tab of the team’s SES submission.

rules.display_text: The strength of any shoulder harness bar and bracing tubes must be proven in the relevant tab of the team’s SES submission.

blocks.text: The shoulder harness mounting points must be between 180 mm and 230 mm apart, measured center to center. When a FHR is used, the shoulder harness mounting must comply with the FHR manufacturer’s instructions and FIA guidance.

rules.display_text: The shoulder harness mounting points must be between 180 mm and 230 mm apart, measured center to center. When a FHR is used, the shoulder harness mounting must comply with the FHR manufacturer’s instructions and FIA guidance.
changelog: Allowed variation on the shoulder harness mounting distance between belts in favor of FHR usage

blocks.text: From the driver’s shoulders rearwards to the mounting point or structural guide, the shoulder harness must be between 10° above the horizontal and 20° below the horizontal as in Figure 14.

rules.display_text:
From the driver’s shoulders rearwards to the mounting point or structural guide, the shoulder harness must be between 10° above the horizontal and 20° below the horizontal as in Figure 14.
[Figure 14: Lap belt and shoulder harness mounting — see figure on page 41]

blocks.text: The anti-submarine belts of a 6 point harness must be mounted in one of the following setups:
With the belts going vertically down from the groin, or angled up to 20° rearwards. The anchorage points must be approximately 100 mm apart.
With the anchorage points on the primary structure at or near the lap belt anchorages, the driver sitting on the anti-submarine belts and the belts coming up around the groin to the release buckle.

rules.display_text:
The anti-submarine belts of a 6 point harness must be mounted in one of the following setups:
▪ With the belts going vertically down from the groin, or angled up to 20° rearwards. The anchorage points must be approximately 100 mm apart.
▪ With the anchorage points on the primary structure at or near the lap belt anchorages, the driver sitting on the anti-submarine belts and the belts coming up around the groin to the release buckle.

blocks.text: A head restraint must be provided on the vehicle to limit the rearward motion of the driver’s head.

rules.display_text: A head restraint must be provided on the vehicle to limit the rearward motion of the driver’s head.

blocks.text: The head restraint must:
be vertical or near vertical in side view.

be padded with an energy absorbing material with a minimum thickness of 40 mm that meets either the SFI 45.2 standard, or is listed in the FIA technical list n°17 as a type A or B material for single seater cars.
include a rectangular area of at least a minimum width and height of 150 mm.
be located so that for each driver:
the restraint is no more than 25 mm away from the back of the driver’s helmet, with the driver in their normal driving position.
the contact point of the back of the driver’s helmet on the head restraint is no less than 50 mm from any edge of the head restraint.

rules.display_text:
The head restraint must:
▪ be vertical or near vertical in side view.
▪ be padded with an energy absorbing material with a minimum thickness of 40 mm that meets either the SFI 45.2 standard, or is listed in the FIA technical list n°17 as a type A or B material for single seater cars.
▪ include a rectangular area of at least a minimum width and height of 150 mm.
▪ be located so that for each driver:
  ▪ the restraint is no more than 25 mm away from the back of the driver’s helmet, with the driver in their normal driving position.
  ▪ the contact point of the back of the driver’s helmet on the head restraint is no less than 50 mm from any edge of the head restraint.
changelog: Added allowed material for head restraint

blocks.text: The head restraint and its mounting must withstand a force of 890 N applied in the rearward direction at any point on its surface.

rules.display_text: The head restraint and its mounting must withstand a force of 890 N applied in the rearward direction at any point on its surface.

blocks.text: Any portion of the roll bar, roll bar bracing or chassis which might be contacted by the driver’s helmet must be covered with a minimum thickness of 12 mm of padding which meets SFI spec 45.1 or FIA 8857-2001.

rules.display_text: Any portion of the roll bar, roll bar bracing or chassis which might be contacted by the driver’s helmet must be covered with a minimum thickness of 12 mm of padding which meets SFI spec 45.1 or FIA 8857-2001.

blocks.text: All moving suspension and steering system components and other sharp edges inside the cockpit between the front hoop and a vertical plane 100 mm rearward of the pedals, must be shielded with solid material.

rules.display_text: All moving suspension and steering system components and other sharp edges inside the cockpit between the front hoop and a vertical plane 100 mm rearward of the pedals, must be shielded with solid material.

blocks.text: Covers over suspension and steering system components must be removable to allow inspection of the mounting points.

rules.display_text: Covers over suspension and steering system components must be removable to allow inspection of the mounting points.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be equipped with a hydraulic brake system that acts on all four wheels and is operated by a single control.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must be equipped with a hydraulic brake system that acts on all four wheels and is operated by a single control.

blocks.text: The brake system must have two independent hydraulic circuits such that in the case of a leak or failure at any point in the system, effective braking power is maintained on at least two wheels. Each hydraulic circuit must have its own fluid reserve, either by the use of separate reservoirs or by the use of a dammed reservoir.

rules.display_text: The brake system must have two independent hydraulic circuits such that in the case of a leak or failure at any point in the system, effective braking power is maintained on at least two wheels. Each hydraulic circuit must have its own fluid reserve, either by the use of separate reservoirs or by the use of a dammed reservoir.

blocks.text: The brake system must be sealed to prevent leakage.

rules.display_text: The brake system must be sealed to prevent leakage.

blocks.text: While parts of the brake system are disconnected, e.g. by a quick-release decoupling
[EV ONLY] the vehicle must not be able to enter R2D mode, see EV 4.11.7.
the ASB must not pass its initial checkup sequence, see T 15.3.1, in autonomous mode.

rules.display_text:
While parts of the brake system are disconnected, e.g. by a quick-release decoupling
▪ [EV ONLY] the vehicle must not be able to enter R2D mode, see EV 4.11.7.
▪ the ASB must not pass its initial checkup sequence, see T 15.3.1, in autonomous mode.

provisions.text: [EV ONLY] the vehicle must not be able to enter R2D mode, see EV 4.11.7.

blocks.text: A single brake acting on a limited-slip differential is acceptable.

rules.display_text: A single brake acting on a limited-slip differential is acceptable.

blocks.text: “Brake-by-wire” systems are prohibited in manual mode.

rules.display_text: “Brake-by-wire” systems are prohibited in manual mode.

blocks.text: Unarmored plastic brake lines are prohibited.

rules.display_text: Unarmored plastic brake lines are prohibited.

blocks.text: The brake system must be protected from failure of the drivetrain, see T 7.3.2, from touching any movable part and from minor collisions.

rules.display_text: The brake system must be protected from failure of the drivetrain, see T 7.3.2, from touching any movable part and from minor collisions.

blocks.text: Any part of the brake system must be within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18.

rules.display_text: Any part of the brake system must be within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18.

blocks.text: The brake pedal, including its load-transferring face and mounting, must withstand a 2 kN force without failure of the brake system or pedal box. The whole pedal box assembly must be securely mounted to the primary structure without excessive deformation under driver-applied loads. This may be tested by pressing the pedal with the maximum force an official can exert when seated normally.

rules.display_text: The brake pedal, including its load-transferring face and mounting, must withstand a 2 kN force without failure of the brake system or pedal box. The whole pedal box assembly must be securely mounted to the primary structure without excessive deformation under driver-applied loads. This may be tested by pressing the pedal with the maximum force an official can exert when seated normally.
changelog: Changed wording for pedal box and pedal box assembly

blocks.text: The brake pedal, including pedal face, must be fabricated from steel or aluminium or machined from steel, aluminium or titanium.

rules.display_text: The brake pedal, including pedal face, must be fabricated from steel or aluminium or machined from steel, aluminium or titanium.

blocks.text: Adjustable pedals must have a positive stop to prevent loosening from the chassis.

rules.display_text: Adjustable pedals must have a positive stop to prevent loosening from the chassis.

blocks.text: The first 90 % of the brake pedal travel may be used to regenerate brake energy without actuating the hydraulic brake system. The remaining brake pedal travel must directly actuate the hydraulic brake system, but brake energy regeneration may remain active.

rules.display_text: The first 90 % of the brake pedal travel may be used to regenerate brake energy without actuating the hydraulic brake system. The remaining brake pedal travel must directly actuate the hydraulic brake system, but brake energy regeneration may remain active.

blocks.text: A BOTS must be installed on the vehicle as part of the SDC, as in EV 6 or CV 4.1. This switch must be installed so that in the event of a failure in at least one of the brake circuits the brake pedal over-travel results in the SDC being opened. This must function for all possible brake pedal and brake balance settings without damaging any part of the vehicle.

rules.display_text: A BOTS must be installed on the vehicle as part of the SDC, as in EV 6 or CV 4.1. This switch must be installed so that in the event of a failure in at least one of the brake circuits the brake pedal over-travel results in the SDC being opened. This must function for all possible brake pedal and brake balance settings without damaging any part of the vehicle.

blocks.text: Repeated actuation of the switch must not close the SDC, and it must be designed so that the driver cannot reset it.

rules.display_text: Repeated actuation of the switch must not close the SDC, and it must be designed so that the driver cannot reset it.

blocks.text: The BOTS must be a push-pull, push-rotate or flip type mechanical switch. It may consist of a series connection of switches.

rules.display_text: The BOTS must be a push-pull, push-rotate or flip type mechanical switch. It may consist of a series connection of switches.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be equipped with one brake light that is illuminated if and only if
the hydraulic brake system is actuated
[EV ONLY] or the electric brake system is actuated, see EV 2.2.3

rules.display_text:
The vehicle must be equipped with one brake light that is illuminated if and only if
▪ the hydraulic brake system is actuated
▪ [EV ONLY] or the electric brake system is actuated, see EV 2.2.3

provisions.text: [EV ONLY] or the electric brake system is actuated, see EV 2.2.3

blocks.text: The brake light must
be a red light.
be clearly visible from the rear.
meet requirements according to T 11.10.

rules.display_text:
The brake light must
▪ be a red light.
▪ be clearly visible from the rear.
▪ meet requirements according to T 11.10.

blocks.text: In side view the brake light must be oriented vertically and mounted between the wheel centerline and driver’s shoulder level. Viewed from the back it must be positioned approximately at the vehicle’s centerline.

rules.display_text: In side view the brake light must be oriented vertically and mounted between the wheel centerline and driver’s shoulder level. Viewed from the back it must be positioned approximately at the vehicle’s centerline.

blocks.text: Movement of the vehicle without a person in the vehicle and with the master switch(es) in the off position must be possible.

rules.display_text: Movement of the vehicle without a person in the vehicle and with the master switch(es) in the off position must be possible.

blocks.text: [CV ONLY] Water-cooled internal combustion engines must only use plain water as the coolant.

rules.display_text: [CV ONLY] Water-cooled internal combustion engines must only use plain water as the coolant.

blocks.text: Other cooling systems may only use plain water, air or oil as the coolant, see T 1.2.2.

rules.display_text: Other cooling systems may only use plain water, air or oil as the coolant, see T 1.2.2.

blocks.text: Cooling systems using plain water (except outboard wheel motors and their cooling hoses) must have a heat resistant (Permanently rated for at least 100 °C), rigid and securely mounted cover which covers any part of the tallest driver below a plane 100 mm above the bottom of the helmet.

rules.display_text: Cooling systems using plain water (except outboard wheel motors and their cooling hoses) must have a heat resistant (Permanently rated for at least 100 °C), rigid and securely mounted cover which covers any part of the tallest driver below a plane 100 mm above the bottom of the helmet.

blocks.text: Any cooling or lubrication system must be sealed to prevent leakage.

rules.display_text: Any cooling or lubrication system must be sealed to prevent leakage.

blocks.text: Separate catch cans must be employed to retain fluids other than plain water from any vents of the cooling system or combustion engine lubrication system. Each catch can must have a minimum volume of 10 % of the fluid being contained or 900 mL whichever is greater.

rules.display_text: Separate catch cans must be employed to retain fluids other than plain water from any vents of the cooling system or combustion engine lubrication system. Each catch can must have a minimum volume of 10 % of the fluid being contained or 900 mL whichever is greater.

blocks.text: Any vent for systems containing plain water must have a catch can with a minimum volume of 10 % of the fluid being contained or 100 mL, whichever is greater.

rules.display_text: Any vent for systems containing plain water must have a catch can with a minimum volume of 10 % of the fluid being contained or 100 mL, whichever is greater.

blocks.text: All parts of the engine, motor(s) cooling and lubrication system, including their mountings, must be rated for at least 100 °C or the temperatures the respective fluid may reach, whichever is higher.

rules.display_text: All parts of the engine, motor(s) cooling and lubrication system, including their mountings, must be rated for at least 100 °C or the temperatures the respective fluid may reach, whichever is higher.

blocks.text: Catch cans must be securely mounted and located rearwards of the firewall below the driver’s shoulder level.

rules.display_text: Catch cans must be securely mounted and located rearwards of the firewall below the driver’s shoulder level.
changelog: Removed requirement to mount catch cans to the chassis

blocks.text: Any catch can must vent through a hose with a minimum internal diameter of 3 mm down to the bottom level of the chassis and must exit outside the bodywork.

rules.display_text: Any catch can must vent through a hose with a minimum internal diameter of 3 mm down to the bottom level of the chassis and must exit outside the bodywork.

blocks.text: The lowest point of any lubrication system can only be lower than the line between the lowest point of the main hoop and the lowest triangulated chassis member behind the lubrication system if it is protected from hitting the ground by a structure mounted directly to the chassis.

rules.display_text: The lowest point of any lubrication system can only be lower than the line between the lowest point of the main hoop and the lowest triangulated chassis member behind the lubrication system if it is protected from hitting the ground by a structure mounted directly to the chassis.
changelog: Clarified rule

blocks.text: Exposed rotating final drivetrain parts, such as gears, clutches, chains and belts must be fitted with scatter shields. Scatter shields and their mountings must:
Be constructed of non-perforated 2 mm steel or 3 mm aluminium alloy 6061-T6.
Be attached with 6 mm metric grade 8.8 or stronger and must comply with T 10.1.
The mounting of exposed rotating final drivetrain parts, except unmodified OEM parts must follow T 10.1.

rules.display_text:
Exposed rotating final drivetrain parts, such as gears, clutches, chains and belts must be fitted with scatter shields. Scatter shields and their mountings must:
▪ Be constructed of non-perforated 2 mm steel or 3 mm aluminium alloy 6061-T6.
▪ Be attached with 6 mm metric grade 8.8 or stronger and must comply with T 10.1.
The mounting of exposed rotating final drivetrain parts, except unmodified OEM parts must follow T 10.1.
changelog: Added exception for unmodified OEM parts

blocks.text: In addition to T 7.3.2, scatter shields must:
Cover chains and belts from the drive sprocket to the driven sprocket/chain wheel/belt or pulley.
Start and end parallel to the lowest point of the driven sprocket/chain wheel/belt or pulley.
Be at least three times the width of the chain or belt and be centered at the centerline of the chain or belt

rules.display_text:
In addition to T 7.3.2, scatter shields must:
▪ Cover chains and belts from the drive sprocket to the driven sprocket/chain wheel/belt or pulley.
▪ Start and end parallel to the lowest point of the driven sprocket/chain wheel/belt or pulley.
▪ Be at least three times the width of the chain or belt and be centered at the centerline of the chain or belt

blocks.text: The tractive electric motor(s) must have a housing or separate scatter shield from non-perforated 2 mm aluminium alloy 6061-T6 or equivalent. The scatter shield may be split into two equal sections, each 1 mm thick.

rules.display_text: The tractive electric motor(s) must have a housing or separate scatter shield from non-perforated 2 mm aluminium alloy 6061-T6 or equivalent. The scatter shield may be split into two equal sections, each 1 mm thick.

blocks.text: Finger guards are required to cover any parts that spin while the vehicle is stationary. Finger guards may be made of lighter material, sufficient to resist finger forces. Mesh or perforated material may be used but must prevent the passage of a 12 mm diameter object through the guard.

rules.display_text: Finger guards are required to cover any parts that spin while the vehicle is stationary. Finger guards may be made of lighter material, sufficient to resist finger forces. Mesh or perforated material may be used but must prevent the passage of a 12 mm diameter object through the guard.

blocks.text: A specifically designed structure mounted on the vehicle to guide the airflow around the vehicle, increasing the downforce acting on the vehicle and/or lowering its drag. The mounting of this structure is not regarded as an aerodynamic device, unless it is intentionally designed to be one.

rules.display_text: A specifically designed structure mounted on the vehicle to guide the airflow around the vehicle, increasing the downforce acting on the vehicle and/or lowering its drag. The mounting of this structure is not regarded as an aerodynamic device, unless it is intentionally designed to be one.

blocks.text: Height restrictions:
All aerodynamic devices forward of a vertical plane through the leading edge of the front tires must be lower than 350 mm from the ground.

All aerodynamic devices rearward of a vertical plane through the rearmost portion of the front face of the driver head restraint support, excluding any padding, set to its most rearward position must be lower than 1100 mm from the ground.

All other aerodynamic devices must be lower than the virtual horizontal plane defined by the topmost points of the two tires on the left or right side of the vehicle, whichever side is closer to the device.

rules.display_text:
Height restrictions:
▪ All aerodynamic devices forward of a vertical plane through the leading edge of the front tires must be lower than 350 mm from the ground.
▪ All aerodynamic devices rearward of a vertical plane through the rearmost portion of the front face of the driver head restraint support, excluding any padding, set to its most rearward position must be lower than 1100 mm from the ground.
▪ All other aerodynamic devices must be lower than the virtual horizontal plane defined by the topmost points of the two tires on the left or right side of the vehicle, whichever side is closer to the device.
changelog: Changed height restrictions

blocks.text: Width restrictions:

All aerodynamic devices lower than the topmost points of the tires and further rearward than a vertical plane through the leading edge of the front tire, must not be wider than a vertical plane touching the most outboard point of the front and rear wheel/tire.
All aerodynamic devices between the top edge of the rear tires and 700 mm above the ground, must not be wider than 150 mm inboard of the most inboard point of each rear tire.
All aerodynamic devices between 700 mm and 1100 mm above the ground, must not extend outboard of the most outboard point of the rear wheel/tire.

rules.display_text:
Width restrictions:
▪ All aerodynamic devices lower than the topmost points of the tires and further rearward than a vertical plane through the leading edge of the front tire, must not be wider than a vertical plane touching the most outboard point of the front and rear wheel/tire.
▪ All aerodynamic devices between the top edge of the rear tires and 700 mm above the ground, must not be wider than 150 mm inboard of the most inboard point of each rear tire.
▪ All aerodynamic devices between 700 mm and 1100 mm above the ground, must not extend outboard of the most outboard point of the rear wheel/tire.
changelog: Changed width restrictions

blocks.text: Length restrictions:
All aerodynamic devices must not extend further rearward than 250 mm from the rearmost part of the rear tires.
All aerodynamic devices must not extend further forward than 700 mm from the fronts of the front tires.

rules.display_text:
Length restrictions:
▪ All aerodynamic devices must not extend further rearward than 250 mm from the rearmost part of the rear tires.
▪ All aerodynamic devices must not extend further forward than 700 mm from the fronts of the front tires.

blocks.text: All restrictions must be fulfilled with the wheels pointing straight and with any suspension setup with or without a driver seated in the vehicle.

rules.display_text:
All restrictions must be fulfilled with the wheels pointing straight and with any suspension setup with or without a driver seated in the vehicle.
[Figure 15: Maximum dimensions and positioning of aerodynamic devices. The positioning space is further restricted, see T 2.1. — see figure on page 45]

blocks.text: Any aerodynamic device must be able to withstand a force of 200 N distributed over a minimum surface of 225 cm2 and not deflect more than 10 mm in the load carrying direction.

rules.display_text: Any aerodynamic device must be able to withstand a force of 200 N distributed over a minimum surface of 225 cm2 and not deflect more than 10 mm in the load carrying direction.

blocks.text: Any aerodynamic device must be able to withstand a force of 50 N applied in any direction at any point and not deflect more than 25 mm.

rules.display_text: Any aerodynamic device must be able to withstand a force of 50 N applied in any direction at any point and not deflect more than 25 mm.

rules.title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems
rules.chapter_title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems
changelog: Unified requirements regarding shielding for CGS and HPHS

rules.title: Definitions
rules.chapter_title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems
Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems

blocks.text: Compressed Gas System (CGS) — any system that uses a compressed gas as an actuating medium, except for gas springs.

rules.display_text: Compressed Gas System (CGS) — any system that uses a compressed gas as an actuating medium, except for gas springs.

rules.chapter_title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems

blocks.text: High Pressure Hydraulic System (HPHS) — any system that uses a non-compressible fluid that is pressurized at 2100 kPa or higher as an actuating medium. Any part of the brake system, see T 6, that is not part of the ASB, see T 15, is not considered HPHS.

rules.display_text: High Pressure Hydraulic System (HPHS) — any system that uses a non-compressible fluid that is pressurized at 2100 kPa or higher as an actuating medium. Any part of the brake system, see T 6, that is not part of the ASB, see T 15, is not considered HPHS.

rules.title: General requirements
rules.chapter_title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems
Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems

blocks.text: All parts of any CGS or HPHS must be designed for the maximum possible operating pressure.

rules.display_text: All parts of any CGS or HPHS must be designed for the maximum possible operating pressure.

rules.chapter_title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems

blocks.text: All parts of any CGS or HPHS and their mountings must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16, and must be protected from collision or damage.

rules.display_text: All parts of any CGS or HPHS and their mountings must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16, and must be protected from collision or damage.

rules.chapter_title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems

blocks.text: The driver and anyone standing outside the vehicle must be shielded from:
All gas cylinders/tanks and their pressure regulators of any CGS.
All parts of any HPHS.
The shielding must be steel or aluminium with a minimum thickness of 1 mm.

rules.display_text:
The driver and anyone standing outside the vehicle must be shielded from:
▪ All gas cylinders/tanks and their pressure regulators of any CGS.
▪ All parts of any HPHS.
The shielding must be steel or aluminium with a minimum thickness of 1 mm.

rules.title: Compressed Gas Systems
rules.chapter_title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems
Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems

blocks.text: The working gas of any CGS must be air or pure nitrogen (𝑁2).

rules.display_text: The working gas of any CGS must be air or pure nitrogen (𝑁2).

rules.chapter_title: Compressed Gas Systems and High Pressure Hydraulic Systems

blocks.text: The maximum possible operating pressure inside any CGS must not exceed 10 bar. Gas cylinders/tanks may exceed this limit, if a (series connection of) pressure regulator(s) which limit(s) the output pressure to a maximum of 10 bar is mounted directly onto them.

blocks.text: Critical fasteners are defined as bolts, nuts, and other fasteners utilized in the primary structure, the (autonomous) steering, (autonomous) brake, driver’s harness, suspension systems and those specifically designated as critical fasteners in the respective rule.

rules.display_text: Critical fasteners are defined as bolts, nuts, and other fasteners utilized in the primary structure, the (autonomous) steering, (autonomous) brake, driver’s harness, suspension systems and those specifically designated as critical fasteners in the respective rule.

blocks.text: All threaded critical fasteners must be steel, at least 4 mm metric grade 8.8 (unmodified OEM parts 3 mm metric grade 8.8), equivalent size or of that specified in the referencing rule, whichever is larger. The strength classification of critical fasteners must be identifiable.

rules.display_text: All threaded critical fasteners must be steel, at least 4 mm metric grade 8.8 (unmodified OEM parts 3 mm metric grade 8.8), equivalent size or of that specified in the referencing rule, whichever is larger. The strength classification of critical fasteners must be identifiable.

blocks.text: All threaded critical fasteners must be of the type hexagon bolts (ISO 4017, ISO 4014 or an equivalent standard) or socket head cap screws (ISO 4762, DIN 7984, ISO 7379 or an equivalent standard) including their fine-pitch thread versions.

rules.display_text: All threaded critical fasteners must be of the type hexagon bolts (ISO 4017, ISO 4014 or an equivalent standard) or socket head cap screws (ISO 4762, DIN 7984, ISO 7379 or an equivalent standard) including their fine-pitch thread versions.

blocks.text: Any bolted joint in the primary structure and mounting of the TSAC to the chassis, using either tabs or brackets, must have an edge distance ratio “e/D” of 1.5 or greater. “D” equals the hole diameter and “e” equals the distance from the hole centerline to the nearest free edge of the tab or bracket. Any tabs attaching suspension members to the primary structure are not required to meet this rule.

rules.display_text: Any bolted joint in the primary structure and mounting of the TSAC to the chassis, using either tabs or brackets, must have an edge distance ratio “e/D” of 1.5 or greater. “D” equals the hole diameter and “e” equals the distance from the hole centerline to the nearest free edge of the tab or bracket. Any tabs attaching suspension members to the primary structure are not required to meet this rule.

blocks.text: All threaded critical fasteners attached to the chassis must not be lower than the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16.

rules.display_text: All threaded critical fasteners attached to the chassis must not be lower than the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16.
changelog: Added rule for critical fasteners attached to the chassis

blocks.text: For steering and suspension systems, alternative fasteners are allowed if equivalency to T 10.1.2 and T 10.1.3 can be shown.

rules.display_text: For steering and suspension systems, alternative fasteners are allowed if equivalency to T 10.1.2 and T 10.1.3 can be shown.

blocks.text: All critical fasteners must be secured from unintentional loosening by the use of positive locking mechanisms.

rules.display_text: All critical fasteners must be secured from unintentional loosening by the use of positive locking mechanisms.

blocks.text: The following methods are accepted as positive locking mechanisms:
Correctly installed safety wiring.
Cotter pins.
Nylon lock nuts (ISO 7040, ISO 10512, EN 1663 or an equivalent standard) for locations where no temperature rating above 80 °C is required.
Prevailing torque lock nuts (DIN 980, ISO 7042 or an equivalent standard, and jet nuts or K-nuts).
Locking plates.
Tab washers.
Any locking mechanism based on pre-tensioning or an adhesive is not considered a positive locking mechanism.

rules.display_text:
The following methods are accepted as positive locking mechanisms:
▪ Correctly installed safety wiring.
▪ Cotter pins.
▪ Nylon lock nuts (ISO 7040, ISO 10512, EN 1663 or an equivalent standard) for locations where no temperature rating above 80 °C is required.
▪ Prevailing torque lock nuts (DIN 980, ISO 7042 or an equivalent standard, and jet nuts or K-nuts).
▪ Locking plates.
▪ Tab washers.
Any locking mechanism based on pre-tensioning or an adhesive is not considered a positive locking mechanism.

blocks.text: Snap or retaining rings according to DIN 471, DIN 472, or equivalent standard are allowed in unmodified OEM applications or for securing bearings or springs or brake disc floaters given that they do not bear any loads under normal driving conditions. The groove must be in pristine condition and manufactured according to the standard of the snap or retaining ring.

The groove must be in pristine condition and manufactured according to the standard of the snap or retaining ring.

blocks.text: A minimum of two full threads must project from any lock nut.

rules.display_text: A minimum of two full threads must project from any lock nut.

blocks.text: All spherical rod ends and spherical bearings on the steering or suspension system must be in double shear or captured by having a screw/bolt head or washer with an outer diameter that is larger than the spherical bearing housing inner diameter.

rules.display_text: All spherical rod ends and spherical bearings on the steering or suspension system must be in double shear or captured by having a screw/bolt head or washer with an outer diameter that is larger than the spherical bearing housing inner diameter.

blocks.text: Adjustable tie-rod ends must be constrained with a jam nut to prevent loosening.

rules.display_text: Adjustable tie-rod ends must be constrained with a jam nut to prevent loosening.

blocks.text: Other positive locking mechanisms than specified can only be accepted for brake disc floaters, given they are unmodified OEM applications and installed according to the manufacturer’s specifications.

blocks.text: The Low Voltage System (LVS) is defined as
[CV ONLY] all electrical circuits of the vehicle.
[EV ONLY] every electrical part that is not part of the TS, see EV 1.1.1

blocks.text: The maximum allowed voltage that may occur between any two electrical connections in the LVS is 60 V DC or 50 V AC RMS.

blocks.text: All LVS parts must be adequately insulated.

rules.display_text: All LVS parts must be adequately insulated.

blocks.text: [CV ONLY] The following systems are excluded from the LVS voltage limit, see T 11.1.2:
High voltage systems for ignition
High voltage systems for injectors
Voltages internal to unmodified OEM charging systems designed for < 60 V DC output.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] The LVS must not use orange wiring or conduit.

rules.display_text: [EV ONLY] The LVS must be grounded to the chassis.

blocks.text: Batteries to operate a real-time clock as well as battery-operated driver communication and onboard cameras are not part of the LVS.

blocks.text: Master switches, see T 11.3, EV 6.2, and T 14.5, must be a mechanical switch of the rotary type, with a red, removable handle. The handle must have a width of at least 50 mm and must only be removable in electrically open position. They must be direct acting, i.e. they must not act through a relay or logic.

rules.display_text: Master switches, see T 11.3, EV 6.2, and T 14.5, must be a mechanical switch of the rotary type, with a red, removable handle. The handle must have a width of at least 50 mm and must only be removable in electrically open position. They must be direct acting, i.e. they must not act through a relay or logic.

blocks.text: Master switches must be located on the right side of the vehicle, in proximity to the main hoop, at the 95th percentile male driver’s shoulder height, as defined in T 4.3, and be easily actuated from outside the vehicle. The center of any master switch must not be mounted lower than the vertical distance of the template’s, see T 4.3, middle circle center to the ground surface multiplied by 0.8.

blocks.text: The “ON” position of the switch must be in the horizontal position and must be marked accordingly. The “OFF” position of the master switch must also be clearly marked.

blocks.text: A system of three shutdown buttons must be installed on the vehicle.

rules.display_text: A system of three shutdown buttons must be installed on the vehicle.

blocks.text: Each shutdown button must be a push-pull or push-rotate mechanical emergency switch where pushing the button opens the SDC, see EV 6.1 and CV 4.1.

rules.display_text: Each shutdown button must be a push-pull or push-rotate mechanical emergency switch where pushing the button opens the SDC, see EV 6.1 and CV 4.1.

blocks.text: One button must be located on each side of the vehicle behind the driver’s compartment at approximately the level of the driver’s head. The minimum allowed diameter of the shutdown buttons on both sides of the vehicle is 40 mm. The buttons must be easily reachable from outside the vehicle.

blocks.text: One shutdown button serves as a cockpit-mounted shutdown button and must:
have a minimum diameter of 24 mm.
be located in easy reach of a belted-in driver.
be alongside of the steering wheel and unobstructed by the steering wheel or any other part of the vehicle.

blocks.text: A standalone non-programmable circuit, the BSPD, must open the SDC, see EV 6.1 and CV 4.1, when hard braking occurs, whilst
[EV ONLY] ≥5 kW power is delivered to the motors.
[CV ONLY] the throttle position is more than 25 % over idle position.
The SDC must remain open until power cycling the LVMS or the BSPD may reset itself if the opening condition is no longer present for more than 10 s.

blocks.text: Standalone is defined as there is no additional functionality implemented on all required PCBs. The interfaces must be reduced to the minimum necessary signals, i.e. power supply, required sensors and the SDC. Supply and sensor signals must not be routed through any other devices before entering the BSPD. If other systems use the sensors in parallel, the team must show at Technical Inspection they do not interfere with the BSPD.

blocks.text: Battery packs based on lithium chemistry other than lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) and all hybrid system energy storages regardless of chemistry type:
must have a fire retardant casing, see T 1.2.1.
must include overcurrent protection that trips at or below the maximum specified discharge current of the cells.

must include overtemperature protection of at least 30 % of the cells, meeting EV 5.8.5, that trips when any cell leaves the allowed temperature range according to the manufacturer’s datasheet, but not more than 60 °C, for more than 1 s and disconnects the battery.
must include voltage protection of all cells that trips when any cell leaves the allowed voltage range according to the manufacturer’s datasheet for more than 500 ms and disconnects the battery.
It must be possible to display all cell voltages and measured temperatures, e.g. by connecting a laptop.
must meet EV 5.8.14.
Signals needed to fulfill these requirements are SCS, see T 11.9.

rules.display_text:
Battery packs based on lithium chemistry other than lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) and all hybrid system energy storages regardless of chemistry type:
▪ must have a fire retardant casing, see T 1.2.1.
▪ must include overcurrent protection that trips at or below the maximum specified discharge current of the cells.
▪ must include overtemperature protection of at least 30 % of the cells, meeting EV 5.8.5, that trips when any cell leaves the allowed temperature range according to the manufacturer’s datasheet, but not more than 60 °C, for more than 1 s and disconnects the battery.
▪ must include voltage protection of all cells that trips when any cell leaves the allowed voltage range according to the manufacturer’s datasheet for more than 500 ms and disconnects the battery.
▪ It must be possible to display all cell voltages and measured temperatures, e.g. by connecting a laptop.
▪ must meet EV 5.8.14.
▪ Signals needed to fulfill these requirements are SCS, see T 11.9.

blocks.text: The foot pedal must return to the 0 % position when not actuated. The foot pedal must have a positive stop preventing the mounted sensors from being damaged or overstressed. blocks.text: Any of the following SCS single failures must result in a safe state of all connected systems:
Failures of signals transmitted by cable:
Open circuit
Short circuit to ground
Failures of analog sensor signals transmitted by cable:
Short circuit to supply voltage
Failures of sensor signals used in programmable devices:
Implausibility due to out of range signals, e.g. mechanically impossible angle of an angle sensor.
Failures of digitally transmitted signals by cable or wireless:
Data corruption (e.g. checked by a checksum)
Loss and delay of messages (e.g. checked by transmission time outs)
Signals might be a member of multiple signal classes, e.g. analog signals transmitted by cable might be a member of T 11.9.2.a, T 11.9.2.b and T 11.9.2.c.

rules.display_text:
Any of the following SCS single failures must result in a safe state of all connected systems:
(a) Failures of signals transmitted by cable:
  ▪ Open circuit
  ▪ Short circuit to ground
(b) Failures of analog sensor signals transmitted by cable:
  ▪ Short circuit to supply voltage
(c) Failures of sensor signals used in programmable devices:
  ▪ Implausibility due to out of range signals, e.g. mechanically impossible angle of an angle sensor.
(d) Failures of digitally transmitted signals by cable or wireless:
  ▪ Data corruption (e.g. checked by a checksum)
  ▪ Loss and delay of messages (e.g. checked by transmission time outs)
Signals might be a member of multiple signal classes, e.g. analog signals transmitted by cable might be a member of T 11.9.2.a, T 11.9.2.b and T 11.9.2.c.

blocks.text: If a signal failure is correctable, e.g. due to redundancy or worst case values, the safe state must be entered as soon as an additional non correctable failure occurs.

rules.display_text: If a signal failure is correctable, e.g. due to redundancy or worst case values, the safe state must be entered as soon as an additional non correctable failure occurs.

blocks.text: The maximum allowed delay of messages according to T 11.9.2.d must be chosen depending on the impact of delayed messages to the connected system, but must not exceed 500 ms.

blocks.text: Safe state is defined depending on the signals as follows:
Signals only influencing indicators – Indicating a failure of its own function or of the connected system
LV battery signals – At least one pole is electrically disconnected from the rest of the vehicle
ASSI, see T 14.9 – indicating “AS Off”
[EV ONLY] For all other signals – opened SDC and opened AIRs
[CV ONLY] For all other signals – opened SDC and stopped engine

rules.display_text:

▪ [CV ONLY] For all other signals – opened SDC and stopped engine

blocks.text: Indicators according to T 11.9.1 with safe state “illuminated” (e.g. absence of failures is not actively indicated) must be illuminated for 1 s to 3 s for visible check after power cycling the LVMS.

blocks.text: Any system status light(s), see T 6.3 and T 14.9, must meet the following requirements:
Black background.
Rectangular, triangular or near round shape.
Minimum illuminated surface of 15 cm2 with even luminous intensity.
Clearly visible in very bright sunlight.
If LED lights are used without a diffuser, they must not be more than 20 mm apart.
If a single line of LED lights is used, the minimum length is 150 mm.

blocks.text: All sensors, cameras and components must be securely mounted.

rules.display_text: All sensors must fulfill the local legislative specifications (i.e. eye-protection classification for laser sensors, power limitation for radar sensors, etc.) in the country of competition.

blocks.text: Each vehicle is assigned a number at the time of its entry into an event.

rules.display_text: Each vehicle is assigned a number at the time of its entry into an event.

blocks.text: Vehicle numbers must appear on the vehicle at the front and both sides as follows:
Height: At least 150 mm high;
Font: Roman Sans-Serif characters. Italic, outline, serif, or shadow numbers are prohibited.
Stroke width and spacing between numbers: At least 20 mm.
Color: Either white numbers on a black background or black numbers on a white background.
Background shape: The number background must be one of the following: round, oval, square or rectangular. There must be at least 25 mm between the edge of the numbers and the edge of the background.
Clear: The numbers must not be obscured by parts of the vehicle.
Alignment: In front view the number at the front and in side view the numbers on the sides must be horizontally aligned.

rules.display_text:
Vehicle numbers must appear on the vehicle at the front and both sides as follows:
▪ Height: At least 150 mm high;
▪ Font: Roman Sans-Serif characters. Italic, outline, serif, or shadow numbers are prohibited.
▪ Stroke width and spacing between numbers: At least 20 mm.
▪ Color: Either white numbers on a black background or black numbers on a white background.
▪ Background shape: The number background must be one of the following: round, oval, square or rectangular. There must be at least 25 mm between the edge of the numbers and the edge of the background.
▪ Clear: The numbers must not be obscured by parts of the vehicle.
▪ Alignment: In front view the number at the front and in side view the numbers on the sides must be horizontally aligned.

blocks.text: Combustion Hybrid Vehicles have to be identified by an additional marking next to all three vehicle numbers with the capital letters “HY” in Roman Sans-Serif characters at least 75 mm high in white on a red background.

rules.display_text: Combustion Hybrid Vehicles have to be identified by an additional marking next to all three vehicle numbers with the capital letters “HY” in Roman Sans-Serif characters at least 75 mm high in white on a red background.

blocks.text: The university name must be written fully. Only the following abbreviations in the university name are allowed, if the city name is written fully:
University → Uni
Technical University → TU
University of Applied Sciences → UAS
Berufsakademie → BA
If the university officially uses an abbreviation in their proper name, this abbreviation is allowed.

blocks.text: The university name must be displayed and written in Roman Sans-Serif characters that are at least 50 mm tall, in front of the main hoop on both sides of the vehicle. The top of each character must not be more than 50 mm below the top of the bodywork.

rules.display_text: The event organizers provide timing equipment for all vehicles.

blocks.text: Each team must have a removable device (called the push bar) that attaches to the rear of the vehicle and allows two people to push and pull the vehicle while standing erect behind the vehicle.

rules.display_text: Each team must have a removable device (called the push bar) that attaches to the rear of the vehicle and allows two people to push and pull the vehicle while standing erect behind the vehicle.

blocks.text: The push bar must have a red color.

rules.display_text: The push bar must have a red color.

blocks.text: The university name must be written on the push bar. The characters must be clearly visible and placed on a high contrast background.

rules.display_text: The university name must be written on the push bar. The characters must be clearly visible and placed on a high contrast background.

blocks.text: The push bar must be capable of slowing and stopping the forward motion of the vehicle and pulling it rearwards.

rules.display_text: The push bar must be capable of slowing and stopping the forward motion of the vehicle and pulling it rearwards.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] Two pairs of high-voltage insulating gloves and a multimeter with two 4 mm banana plug test leads rated for 600 V CAT III or better must be attached to the push bar. The HV gloves must be protected by a case or similar means from mechanical damage, humidity and sunlight. It must be possible to open the case without using tools.

blocks.text: Each team must have one or two removable devices (jacks) that hold the vehicle, so that all driven wheels are at least 75 mm off the ground.

rules.display_text: Each team must have one or two removable devices (jacks) that hold the vehicle, so that all driven wheels are at least 75 mm off the ground.

blocks.text: Lifting the vehicle and positioning of the device(s) must be done by the team in a safe way.

rules.display_text: Lifting the vehicle and positioning of the device(s) must be done by the team in a safe way.

blocks.text: In lifted position:
The vehicle must be adequately supported and stable.
It must be safe for a driver to enter and exit the vehicle, without additional devices.
The device(s) must not extend out of the vehicle’s projected surface area.

blocks.text: On both sides of the vehicle the device’s pickup points must be indicated by orange triangles.

blocks.text: The equipment specified below must be worn by the driver anytime while in the cockpit with the engine running or with the TS active for electric vehicles and anytime between starting a dynamic discipline and either finishing or abandoning a dynamic discipline. Removal of any driver equipment during the discipline results in a DQ.

blocks.text: A well-fitting, unmodified, closed face helmet that meets one of the following certifications and is labeled as such:
Snell SA2020, EA2016, SA2025 or newer

Open-faced helmets and off-road helmets (helmets without integrated eye shields) are not approved. All helmets to be used in the event must be presented during Technical Inspection where approved helmets are stickered.

SFI 38.1

SFI 3.2A/5 (or higher)
SFI 3.4/5 (or higher)

blocks.text: Fire resistant clothing must not be older than 10 years, recognizable since no FIA hologram label present.

rules.display_text: Fire resistant clothing must not be older than 10 years, recognizable since no FIA hologram label present.

blocks.text: Arm restraints are required and must be worn such that the driver can release them and exit the vehicle unassisted regardless of the vehicle’s position. Arm restraints must be commercially manufactured according to SFI Standard 3.3 or equivalent.

rules.display_text: Arm restraints are required and must be worn such that the driver can release them and exit the vehicle unassisted regardless of the vehicle’s position. Arm restraints must be commercially manufactured according to SFI Standard 3.3 or equivalent.

blocks.text: All driver equipment covered in T 13.3 must be in good condition. Specifically, it must not have any tears, rips, open seams, areas of significant wear or abrasion or stains which might compromise fire resistant performance. Teams must be able to show that the clothing still meets the requirements of T 13.3 if driver’s clothing is embroidered. This requires, but is not limited to, that only the outer shell is perforated. The officials reserve the right to impound all non-approved driver equipment until the end of the event.

rules.display_text: All driver equipment covered in T 13.3 must be in good condition. Specifically, it must not have any tears, rips, open seams, areas of significant wear or abrasion or stains which might compromise fire resistant performance. blocks.text: Driver communication equipment must be securely mounted to the vehicle, except for the microphone and speakers worn by the driver. Wired driver communication equipment, must automatically disconnect during driver egress. The connector must be placed behind the driver’s shoulder and the cable length reduced to the minimum.

USA, Canada and Brazil: 10BC or 1A 10BC
Europe: 34B or 5A 34B

blocks.text: Each vehicle must implement a full AS according to T 14, to run in autonomous mode.

rules.display_text: Each vehicle must implement a full AS according to T 14, to run in autonomous mode.

blocks.text: [CV ONLY] The following definitions apply to maintain the same wording as for EVs:
R2D – engine is running and a gear is engaged.
TS active – engine is running but gearbox is in neutral, also assumed for TS not active.
TS activation button – engine start button
AIR - fuel pump relay, see Figure 20

rules.display_text:
[CV ONLY] The following definitions apply to maintain the same wording as for EVs:
▪ R2D – engine is running and a gear is engaged.
▪ TS active – engine is running but gearbox is in neutral, also assumed for TS not active.
▪ TS activation button – engine start button

blocks.text: The officials provide a standardized data logger that must be installed during the event. Further specifications for the data logger and required hardware and software interfaces can be found in the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: The officials provide a standardized data logger that must be installed during the event. Further specifications for the data logger and required hardware and software interfaces can be found in the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: The team needs to provide two sets of signals to the data logger:
Basic set of signals as defined in the Event Handbook
Vehicle-individual set of signals that is monitored by the ASB to ensure redundancy and fault detection

rules.display_text:
The team needs to provide two sets of signals to the data logger:
▪ Basic set of signals as defined in the Event Handbook
▪ Vehicle-individual set of signals that is monitored by the ASB to ensure redundancy and fault detection

blocks.text: [CV ONLY] The mounting of the data logger must be sealed during Technical Inspection.

rules.display_text: [CV ONLY] The mounting of the data logger must be sealed during Technical Inspection.

blocks.text: Every vehicle must be equipped with a standard RES specified in the Event Handbook. The system consists of two parts, the remote control and the vehicle module.

rules.display_text: Every vehicle must be equipped with a standard RES specified in the Event Handbook. The system consists of two parts, the remote control and the vehicle module.

blocks.text: The RES must be purchased by the team.

rules.display_text: The RES must be purchased by the team.

blocks.text: The RES has two functions:
When the remote emergency stop button is pressed, it must open the SDC defined in T 14.4.
When the “Go” button is pressed, the preselected autonomous mission is started.

rules.display_text:
The RES has two functions:
▪ When the remote emergency stop button is pressed, it must open the SDC defined in T 14.4.
▪ When the “Go” button is pressed, the preselected autonomous mission is started.

blocks.text: The RES vehicle module must be directly, see T 1.3.1, integrated in the vehicle’s SDC with one of its relays hard-wired in series to the shutdown buttons.

rules.display_text: The RES vehicle module must be directly, see T 1.3.1, integrated in the vehicle’s SDC with one of its relays hard-wired in series to the shutdown buttons.

blocks.text: The RES relay, which is integrated into the SDC, must be bypassed by a normally closed relay, when driving manually. The relay must:
be directly supplied, see T 1.3.1, by the ASMS, see T 14.5.
have a safety certified forcibly guided or a mirrored normally open contact which is directly connected, see T 1.3.1, in series to the ASMS.

rules.display_text:
The RES relay, which is integrated into the SDC, must be bypassed by a normally closed relay, when driving manually. The relay must:
▪ be directly supplied, see T 1.3.1, by the ASMS, see T 14.5.
▪ have a safety certified forcibly guided or a mirrored normally open contact which is directly connected, see T 1.3.1, in series to the ASMS.

blocks.text: The antenna of the RES must be mounted unobstructed and without interfering parts in proximity, e.g. other antennas, etc.

rules.display_text: The antenna of the RES must be mounted unobstructed and without interfering parts in proximity, e.g. other antennas, etc.

blocks.text: The SDC may only be closed by the AS, if the following conditions are fulfilled:
Manual Driving: Manual Mission is selected, the AS has checked that ASB is deactivated, i.e. no autonomous brake actuation possible.
Autonomous Driving: Autonomous Mission is selected, ASMS is switched on and sufficient brake pressure is built up, i.e. brakes are closed.

rules.display_text:
The SDC may only be closed by the AS, if the following conditions are fulfilled:
▪ Manual Driving: Manual Mission is selected, the AS has checked that ASB is deactivated, i.e. no autonomous brake actuation possible.
▪ Autonomous Driving: Autonomous Mission is selected, ASMS is switched on and sufficient brake pressure is built up, i.e. brakes are closed.

blocks.text: Each vehicle must be equipped with an ASMS according to T 11.2.

rules.display_text: Each vehicle must be equipped with an ASMS according to T 11.2.

blocks.text: The ASMS must be mounted in the middle of a completely blue circular area of ≥50 mm diameter placed on a high contrast background.

rules.display_text: The ASMS must be mounted in the middle of a completely blue circular area of ≥50 mm diameter placed on a high contrast background.

blocks.text: The ASMS must be marked with “AS”.

rules.display_text: The ASMS must be marked with “AS”.

blocks.text: The power supply of all steering and brake actuators must be switched by the LVMS and the ASMS. Other than the direct acting requirement stated in T 11.2.1, a relay with its coil supplied by the ASMS may be used in parallel to the ASMS.

rules.display_text: The power supply of all steering and brake actuators must be switched by the LVMS and the ASMS. Other than the direct acting requirement stated in T 11.2.1, a relay with its coil supplied by the ASMS may be used in parallel to the ASMS.
changelog: Clarified exception of T 11.2.1

blocks.text: When the ASMS is in “Off” position, the following must be fulfilled:
No steering, braking and propulsion actuation can be performed by request of the autonomous system.
The sensors and the processing units can stay operational.
The vehicle must be able to be pushed as specified in A 6.6.
It must be possible to operate the vehicle manually as a normal CV or EV.

rules.display_text:
When the ASMS is in “Off” position, the following must be fulfilled:
▪ No steering, braking and propulsion actuation can be performed by request of the autonomous system.
▪ The sensors and the processing units can stay operational.
▪ The vehicle must be able to be pushed as specified in A 6.6.
▪ It must be possible to operate the vehicle manually as a normal CV or EV.

blocks.text: While the ASMS is switched to the “On” position
no person may be (seated) inside the vehicle.
no other manual steps other than activating the TS may be performed at the vehicle.

rules.display_text:
While the ASMS is switched to the “On” position
▪ no person may be (seated) inside the vehicle.
▪ no other manual steps other than activating the TS may be performed at the vehicle.

blocks.text: The ASMS must be fitted with a “lockout/tagout” capability to prevent accidental activation of the AS. The ASR must ensure that the ASMS is locked in the off position whenever the vehicle is outside the dynamic area or driven in manual mode.

rules.display_text: The ASMS must be fitted with a “lockout/tagout” capability to prevent accidental activation of the AS. The ASR must ensure that the ASMS is locked in the off position whenever the vehicle is outside the dynamic area or driven in manual mode.

blocks.text: Steering system actuation, i.e. movement, must only happen if the vehicle is in R2D mode or during “AS Emergency”, see T 14.8.3.

rules.display_text: Steering system actuation, i.e. movement, must only happen if the vehicle is in R2D mode or during “AS Emergency”, see T 14.8.3.

blocks.text: Manual steering must be possible without manual release steps, e.g. operating manual valves and/or (dis-)connecting mechanical elements, while the ASMS is switched “Off”.

rules.display_text: Manual steering must be possible without manual release steps, e.g. operating manual valves and/or (dis-)connecting mechanical elements, while the ASMS is switched “Off”.

blocks.text: Actuators may be disconnected if the decoupling mechanism cannot block manual operation in any position.

rules.display_text: Actuators may be disconnected if the decoupling mechanism cannot block manual operation in any position.

blocks.text: Sensors according to T 11.12 may be repositioned to multiple fixed positions if full rules compliance is ensured in all fixed positions.

rules.display_text: Sensors according to T 11.12 may be repositioned to multiple fixed positions if full rules compliance is ensured in all fixed positions.

blocks.text: The mechanisms used for actuator decoupling, see T 14.7.1, or sensor repositioning, see T 14.7.2, must ensure that
no parts except covers are removed from the vehicle.
covers are only removed from the vehicle temporarily during the process.
all parts remain in physical contact to the vehicle without using a tether line or similar, i.e. fasteners may be loosened but must not be fully undone.
they are securely locked in all (fixed) positions.

rules.display_text:
The mechanisms used for actuator decoupling, see T 14.7.1, or sensor repositioning, see T 14.7.2, must ensure that
▪ no parts except covers are removed from the vehicle.
▪ covers are only removed from the vehicle temporarily during the process.
▪ all parts remain in physical contact to the vehicle without using a tether line or similar, i.e. fasteners may be loosened but must not be fully undone.
▪ they are securely locked in all (fixed) positions.

blocks.text: The EBS is considered to be “activated”, if the power supply path defined in T 15.2.2 is cut after passing the initial checkup sequence, see T 15.3.1. Brakes may only be released by operating the deactivation point(s) defined in T 15.1.7.

rules.display_text: The EBS is considered to be “activated”, if the power supply path defined in T 15.2.2 is cut after passing the initial checkup sequence, see T 15.3.1. Brakes may only be released by operating the deactivation point(s) defined in T 15.1.7.

blocks.text: The EBS is no longer considered to be activated, if all brakes have been released using the deactivation point(s) defined in T 15.1.7.

rules.display_text: The EBS is no longer considered to be activated, if all brakes have been released using the deactivation point(s) defined in T 15.1.7.

blocks.text: The status of the AS must be determined according to the flowchart in Figure 16.

rules.display_text:
The status of the AS must be determined according to the flowchart in Figure 16.
