blocks.text: In autonomous mode, R2D mode may only be entered by the “Go” signal from the RES, after the system has remained in “AS Ready” for at least 5 s.

rules.display_text: In autonomous mode, R2D mode may only be entered by the “Go” signal from the RES, after the system has remained in “AS Ready” for at least 5 s.

blocks.text: In autonomous mode, the vehicle must not start moving, until the system has remained in “AS Driving” for at least 3 s.

rules.display_text: In autonomous mode, the vehicle must not start moving, until the system has remained in “AS Driving” for at least 3 s.

blocks.text: The vehicle must include three ASSIs that must indicate the status of the AS, as defined in T 14.8, correlating to illumination as shown:
During “AS Driving” and “AS Emergency” the ASSIs must be flashing continuously with a frequency between 2 Hz and 5 Hz and a duty cycle of 50 %. The ASSIs must not perform any other functions.

rules.display_text:
The vehicle must include three ASSIs that must indicate the status of the AS, as defined in T 14.8, correlating to illumination as shown:
[Table — see table on page 57]
  AS Off | AS Ready | AS Driving | AS Emergency | AS Finished
  off | yellow continuous | yellow flashing | blue flashing | blue continuous
During “AS Driving” and “AS Emergency” the ASSIs must be flashing continuously with a frequency between 2 Hz and 5 Hz and a duty cycle of 50 %. The ASSIs must not perform any other functions.

blocks.text: One ASSI must be located on each side of the vehicle behind the driver’s compartment, in a region 160 mm below the top of the main hoop and 600 mm above the ground. The third ASSI must be located at the rear of the vehicle, on the vehicle centerline, in a region 160 mm below the top of the main hoop and 100 mm above the brake light.

rules.display_text: One ASSI must be located on each side of the vehicle behind the driver’s compartment, in a region 160 mm below the top of the main hoop and 600 mm above the ground. The third ASSI must be located at the rear of the vehicle, on the vehicle centerline, in a region 160 mm below the top of the main hoop and 100 mm above the brake light.

blocks.text: The entire illuminated surface of at least one ASSI must be visible:
from any angle of the vehicle from a point 1.60 m vertically from ground level, within 3 m horizontal radius from the top of the main hoop.
in direct sunlight.

rules.display_text:
The entire illuminated surface of at least one ASSI must be visible:
▪ from any angle of the vehicle from a point 1.60 m vertically from ground level, within 3 m horizontal radius from the top of the main hoop.
▪ in direct sunlight.
changelog: Clarified ASSI visibility requirements

blocks.text: Each ASSI must meet the requirements according to T 11.10.

rules.display_text: Each ASSI must meet the requirements according to T 11.10.

blocks.text: The status “AS Emergency” has to be indicated by an intermittent sound with the following parameters:
on-/off-frequency: 1 Hz to 5 Hz
duty cycle 50 %
sound level between 80 dB(A) and 90 dB(A), fast weighting in a radius of 2 m around the vehicle.
duration between 8 s and 10 s after entering “AS Emergency”

rules.display_text:
The status “AS Emergency” has to be indicated by an intermittent sound with the following parameters:
▪ on-/off-frequency: 1 Hz to 5 Hz
▪ duty cycle 50 %
▪ sound level between 80 dB(A) and 90 dB(A), fast weighting in a radius of 2 m around the vehicle.
▪ duration between 8 s and 10 s after entering “AS Emergency”

blocks.text: The AS must at least implement the following missions:
Acceleration
Skidpad
[DC ONLY] Autocross
[DC ONLY] Trackdrive
EBS Test
Inspection
Manual Driving

rules.display_text:
The AS must at least implement the following missions:
▪ Acceleration
▪ Skidpad
▪ [DC ONLY] Autocross
▪ [DC ONLY] Trackdrive
▪ EBS Test
▪ Inspection
▪ Manual Driving

provisions.text: [DC ONLY] Autocross
[DC ONLY] Trackdrive

blocks.text: The Inspection Mission is defined by slowly spinning the drivetrain and actuating the steering system with a sine wave while the vehicle is jacked up and all wheels are removed. After 25 s to 30 s the AS must transition to “AS Finished”.

rules.display_text: The Inspection Mission is defined by slowly spinning the drivetrain and actuating the steering system with a sine wave while the vehicle is jacked up and all wheels are removed. After 25 s to 30 s the AS must transition to “AS Finished”.

blocks.text: It must be possible to select any mission without the use of an external device.

rules.display_text: It must be possible to select any mission without the use of an external device.

blocks.text: The selected mission must be indicated by the Autonomous Mission Indicator (AMI).

rules.display_text: The selected mission must be indicated by the Autonomous Mission Indicator (AMI).

blocks.text: The AMI must be easily readable by any person standing next to the ASMS and can either be part of the dashboard or located next to the ASMS.

rules.display_text: The AMI must be easily readable by any person standing next to the ASMS and can either be part of the dashboard or located next to the ASMS.

blocks.text: Before the event, all teams must submit a clearly structured documentation of their entire AS, including ASB, called ASF.

rules.display_text: Before the event, all teams must submit a clearly structured documentation of their entire AS, including ASB, called ASF.

blocks.text: To run in autonomous mode, the vehicle must be equipped with an ASB that features an EBS, see T 15.2, as part of it.

rules.display_text: To run in autonomous mode, the vehicle must be equipped with an ASB that features an EBS, see T 15.2, as part of it.

blocks.text: All parts of the ASB and their mountings must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16, with the following exceptions:
brake system according to T 6
deactivation point(s) according to T 15.1.8

rules.display_text:
All parts of the ASB and their mountings must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16, with the following exceptions:
▪ brake system according to T 6
▪ deactivation point(s) according to T 15.1.8

blocks.text: The TS is not considered to be a brake system.

rules.display_text: The TS is not considered to be a brake system.

blocks.text: Manual braking must always be possible. In case of manual and autonomous braking simultaneously, always the highest of both pressures must be applied to the brakes.

rules.display_text: Manual braking must always be possible. In case of manual and autonomous braking simultaneously, always the highest of both pressures must be applied to the brakes.

blocks.text: Master brake cylinders must not be connected in series.

rules.display_text: Master brake cylinders must not be connected in series.

blocks.text: The ASB may be part of the hydraulic brake system. For all components inside the vehicle’s brake circuit T 6 is applied. On all remaining pneumatic and hydraulic components T 9 applies.

rules.display_text: The ASB may be part of the hydraulic brake system. For all components inside the vehicle’s brake circuit T 6 is applied. On all remaining pneumatic and hydraulic components T 9 applies.

blocks.text: The ASB must be designed so that it can be easily deactivated by two deactivation points.

rules.display_text: The ASB must be designed so that it can be easily deactivated by two deactivation points.

blocks.text: Any deactivation point of the ASB must:
work without the aid of electrical power
be in proximity to each other
be mounted within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18
either be mounted in proximity to the ASMS or on the top side of the vehicle between front bulkhead and front hoop close to the vehicle’s centerline
be protected against unintended actuation, e.g. by being hit by a cone, while driving
be operable by maximum two simple push/pull and/or turning actions, the order and direction of these actions must be shown next to the deactivation points.
be marked with “Brake release”
have a red handle

rules.display_text:
Any deactivation point of the ASB must:
▪ work without the aid of electrical power
▪ be in proximity to each other
▪ be mounted within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18
▪ either be mounted in proximity to the ASMS or on the top side of the vehicle between front bulkhead and front hoop close to the vehicle’s centerline
▪ be protected against unintended actuation, e.g. by being hit by a cone, while driving
▪ be operable by maximum two simple push/pull and/or turning actions, the order and direction of these actions must be shown next to the deactivation points.
▪ be marked with “Brake release”
▪ have a red handle

blocks.text: The EBS must only use passive systems which are primarily designed and manufactured for the purpose of mechanically storing energy. Electrical power-loss at EBS must lead to a direct emergency brake maneuver with the performance specified in T 15.4.

rules.display_text: The EBS must only use passive systems which are primarily designed and manufactured for the purpose of mechanically storing energy. Electrical power-loss at EBS must lead to a direct emergency brake maneuver with the performance specified in T 15.4.
changelog: Clarified requirements on mechanical energy storage

blocks.text: The EBS must be supplied by
LVMS
ASMS
the forcibly guided or mirrored normally open contact of the relay according to T 14.3.5
RES
a relay which is supplied by the SDC, i.e. parallel to the AIRs, but must not be delayed.

rules.display_text:
The EBS must be supplied by
▪ LVMS
▪ ASMS
▪ the forcibly guided or mirrored normally open contact of the relay according to T 14.3.5
▪ RES
▪ a relay which is supplied by the SDC, i.e. parallel to the AIRs, but must not be delayed.
changelog: Clarified which relay contact to use for EBS supply
Clarified that the EBS must also be switched by the RES

blocks.text: An initial check has to be performed to ensure that the ASB is able to
operate as specified in T 15.3.2 and T 15.3.4
build up brake pressure as expected
before AS transitions to “AS Ready”.

rules.display_text:
An initial check has to be performed to ensure that the ASB is able to
▪ operate as specified in T 15.3.2 and T 15.3.4
▪ build up brake pressure as expected
before AS transitions to “AS Ready”.

blocks.text: After the initial check the ASB and its SCS must be continuously monitored for failures.

rules.display_text: After the initial check the ASB and its SCS must be continuously monitored for failures.

blocks.text: The functionality required to achieve T 15.3.1 including brake actuation and T 15.3.2 must be implemented on a single PCB. Sensor signals may be routed and preprocessed through additional PCBs.

rules.display_text: The functionality required to achieve T 15.3.1 including brake actuation and T 15.3.2 must be implemented on a single PCB. Sensor signals may be routed and preprocessed through additional PCBs.
changelog: Clarified that brake actuation is included

blocks.text: The vehicle must automatically transition to the safe state, if:
the functionality according to T 15.2.1 cannot be ensured.
an (additional) single point of failure would lead to total loss of brake capability.

If the ASB actuates the brake system, see T 6, exclusively through the brake pedal, see T 6.1.10, and equivalent to the actuation by the driver’s foot the transition to the safe state does not need to be ensured in the event of a failure of the brake pedal itself.

rules.display_text:
The vehicle must automatically transition to the safe state, if:
▪ the functionality according to T 15.2.1 cannot be ensured.
▪ an (additional) single point of failure would lead to total loss of brake capability.
If the ASB actuates the brake system, see T 6, exclusively through the brake pedal, see T 6.1.10, and equivalent to the actuation by the driver’s foot the transition to the safe state does not need to be ensured in the event of a failure of the brake pedal itself.
changelog: Clarified redundancy requirement for brake pedal

blocks.text: The safe state is the vehicle at a standstill, brakes engaged to prevent the vehicle from rolling, and an open SDC.

rules.display_text: The safe state is the vehicle at a standstill, brakes engaged to prevent the vehicle from rolling, and an open SDC.

blocks.text: To get to the safe state, the vehicle must perform an autonomous brake maneuver described in section T 15.4 and IN 11.2.

rules.display_text: To get to the safe state, the vehicle must perform an autonomous brake maneuver described in section T 15.4 and IN 11.2.

blocks.text: The system reaction time, i.e. the time between opening of the SDC and the start of the deceleration, must not exceed 200 ms.

rules.display_text: The system reaction time, i.e. the time between opening of the SDC and the start of the deceleration, must not exceed 200 ms.

blocks.text: The average deceleration must be greater than 10 m/s2 under dry track conditions.

rules.display_text: The average deceleration must be greater than 10 m/s2 under dry track conditions.

blocks.text: In case of a single failure the ASB should be designed to achieve at least half of the performance specified in T 15.4.2.

rules.display_text: In case of a single failure the ASB should be designed to achieve at least half of the performance specified in T 15.4.2.

blocks.text: Whilst decelerating, the vehicle must remain in a stable driving condition.

rules.display_text: Whilst decelerating, the vehicle must remain in a stable driving condition.

blocks.text: The engine(s) used to power the vehicle must be piston engine(s) using a four-stroke primary heat cycle with a displacement not exceeding 710 cm3 per cycle. Hybrid powertrains are allowed with electric motors that are connected to the engine, gearbox, wheels, exhaust turbines or superchargers. Hybrid powertrains must use a purely electrical energy storage. Starter motors that cannot provide propulsion when the engine is running are not considered hybrid.

rules.display_text: The engine(s) used to power the vehicle must be piston engine(s) using a four-stroke primary heat cycle with a displacement not exceeding 710 cm3 per cycle. Hybrid powertrains are allowed with electric motors that are connected to the engine, gearbox, wheels, exhaust turbines or superchargers. Hybrid powertrains must use a purely electrical energy storage. Starter motors that cannot provide propulsion when the engine is running are not considered hybrid.

blocks.text: Each vehicle must be equipped with an on-board starter, which must be used to start the vehicle.

rules.display_text: Each vehicle must be equipped with an on-board starter, which must be used to start the vehicle.

blocks.text: For autonomous operation, the vehicle must be equipped with an additional engine start button next to the LVMS, see T 11.3, that can be easily actuated from outside the vehicle. Using the external engine start button, the engine may only start if
the ASMS, see T 14.5, is switched on and
the gearbox is in neutral.

rules.display_text:
For autonomous operation, the vehicle must be equipped with an additional engine start button next to the LVMS, see T 11.3, that can be easily actuated from outside the vehicle. Using the external engine start button, the engine may only start if
▪ the ASMS, see T 14.5, is switched on and
▪ the gearbox is in neutral.

blocks.text: If CV 1.2.2 requires an additional engine start button, there must be a green light next to it, that indicates that the gearbox is in neutral. It must be marked with the letter “N”. This letter must have a minimum height of 25 mm.

rules.display_text: If CV 1.2.2 requires an additional engine start button, there must be a green light next to it, that indicates that the gearbox is in neutral. It must be marked with the letter “N”. This letter must have a minimum height of 25 mm.

blocks.text: The AS must not be able to (re-)start the engine.

rules.display_text: The AS must not be able to (re-)start the engine.

blocks.text: All parts of the engine air and fuel control systems (including the throttle and the complete air intake system, including the air filter and any air boxes) must lie within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18.

rules.display_text: All parts of the engine air and fuel control systems (including the throttle and the complete air intake system, including the air filter and any air boxes) must lie within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18.

blocks.text: Any portion of the air intake system that is less than 350 mm above the ground must be protected from impacts, see T 3.15. Impact protection must follow T 3.16 when having bolted attachments.

rules.display_text: Any portion of the air intake system that is less than 350 mm above the ground must be protected from impacts, see T 3.15. Impact protection must follow T 3.16 when having bolted attachments.

blocks.text: The intake manifold must be securely mounted to the engine block or cylinder head with brackets and mechanical fasteners that are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10. This mounting must ensure that the intake manifold including the injectors is securely mounted. Rubber bushings or hoses are not considered a secure mounting.

rules.display_text: The intake manifold must be securely mounted to the engine block or cylinder head with brackets and mechanical fasteners that are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10. This mounting must ensure that the intake manifold including the injectors is securely mounted. Rubber bushings or hoses are not considered a secure mounting.

blocks.text: Intake systems with significant mass or cantilever from the cylinder head must be supported to prevent stress to the intake system resulting from engine movement and chassis torsion.

rules.display_text: Intake systems with significant mass or cantilever from the cylinder head must be supported to prevent stress to the intake system resulting from engine movement and chassis torsion.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be equipped with a throttle body. The throttle body may be of any size or design.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must be equipped with a throttle body. The throttle body may be of any size or design.

blocks.text: The throttle must be actuated mechanically by a foot pedal, i.e. via a cable or a rod system, see CV 1.5, or by an ETC system, see CV 1.6.

rules.display_text: The throttle must be actuated mechanically by a foot pedal, i.e. via a cable or a rod system, see CV 1.5, or by an ETC system, see CV 1.6.

blocks.text: Throttle position is defined as percentage of travel from fully closed to fully open where 0 % is fully closed and 100 % is fully open. The idle position is the average position of the throttle body while the engine is idling.

rules.display_text: Throttle position is defined as percentage of travel from fully closed to fully open where 0 % is fully closed and 100 % is fully open. The idle position is the average position of the throttle body while the engine is idling.

blocks.text: The throttle system mechanism must be protected from debris ingress to prevent jamming.

rules.display_text: The throttle system mechanism must be protected from debris ingress to prevent jamming.

blocks.text: CV 1.5 can only be used if no AS is used.

rules.display_text: CV 1.5 can only be used if no AS is used.

blocks.text: The throttle actuation system must use at least two return springs located at the throttle body, so that the failure of any one of the two springs does not prevent the throttle returning to the idle position.

rules.display_text: The throttle actuation system must use at least two return springs located at the throttle body, so that the failure of any one of the two springs does not prevent the throttle returning to the idle position.

blocks.text: Each return spring must be capable of returning the throttle to the idle position with the other disconnected.

rules.display_text: Each return spring must be capable of returning the throttle to the idle position with the other disconnected.

blocks.text: Springs in the TPS are not allowed as return springs.

rules.display_text: Springs in the TPS are not allowed as return springs.

blocks.text: Throttle cables must be located at least 50 mm from any exhaust system component and out of the exhaust stream.

rules.display_text: Throttle cables must be located at least 50 mm from any exhaust system component and out of the exhaust stream.

blocks.text: Throttle cables or rods must have smooth operation and must not have the possibility of binding or sticking. They must be protected from being bent or kinked by the driver’s foot during operation or when entering the vehicle.

rules.display_text: Throttle cables or rods must have smooth operation and must not have the possibility of binding or sticking. They must be protected from being bent or kinked by the driver’s foot during operation or when entering the vehicle.

blocks.text: A positive pedal stop must be incorporated on the accelerator pedal to prevent over-stressing the throttle cable or actuation system.

rules.display_text: A positive pedal stop must be incorporated on the accelerator pedal to prevent over-stressing the throttle cable or actuation system.

blocks.text: CV 1.6 only applies if ETC is used.

rules.display_text: CV 1.6 only applies if ETC is used.

blocks.text: The team must be able to demonstrate the functionality of all safety features and error detections of the ETC system at Technical Inspection, see IN .

rules.display_text: The team must be able to demonstrate the functionality of all safety features and error detections of the ETC system at Technical Inspection, see IN .

blocks.text: The ETC system must be equipped with at least the following sensors:
Accelerator Pedal Position Sensors (APPSs) as defined in T 11.8.
Two Throttle Position Sensors (TPSs) to measure the throttle position.

rules.display_text:
The ETC system must be equipped with at least the following sensors:
▪ Accelerator Pedal Position Sensors (APPSs) as defined in T 11.8.
▪ Two Throttle Position Sensors (TPSs) to measure the throttle position.

blocks.text: All ETC signals are SCS, see T 11.9.

rules.display_text: All ETC signals are SCS, see T 11.9.

blocks.text: When power is removed, the electronic throttle must immediately close at least to idle position ±5 %. An interval of one second is allowed for the throttle to close to idle, failure to achieve this within the required interval must result in immediate disabling of power to ignition, fuel injectors and fuel pump. This action must remain active until the TPS signals indicate the throttle has returned to idle position ±5 % for at least one second.

rules.display_text: When power is removed, the electronic throttle must immediately close at least to idle position ±5 %. An interval of one second is allowed for the throttle to close to idle, failure to achieve this within the required interval must result in immediate disabling of power to ignition, fuel injectors and fuel pump. This action must remain active until the TPS signals indicate the throttle has returned to idle position ±5 % for at least one second.

blocks.text: If plausibility does not occur between the values of at least two TPSs and this persists for more than 100 ms, the power to the electronic throttle must be immediately shut down. Plausibility is defined as a deviation of less than ten percentage points between the sensor values as defined in CV 1.4.3 and no detected failures as defined in T 11.9. AS must check this signal consistency on a low level itself.

rules.display_text: If plausibility does not occur between the values of at least two TPSs and this persists for more than 100 ms, the power to the electronic throttle must be immediately shut down. Plausibility is defined as a deviation of less than ten percentage points between the sensor values as defined in CV 1.4.3 and no detected failures as defined in T 11.9. AS must check this signal consistency on a low level itself.

blocks.text: The electronic throttle must use at least two sources of energy capable of returning the throttle to the closed position. One of the sources may be the device that normally actuates the throttle, e.g. a DC motor, but the other device(s) must be a return spring that can return the throttle to the idle position in the event of a loss of actuator power.

rules.display_text: The electronic throttle must use at least two sources of energy capable of returning the throttle to the closed position. One of the sources may be the device that normally actuates the throttle, e.g. a DC motor, but the other device(s) must be a return spring that can return the throttle to the idle position in the event of a loss of actuator power.

blocks.text: Springs in the TPSs are not acceptable as return springs.

rules.display_text: Springs in the TPSs are not acceptable as return springs.

blocks.text: The power to the electronic throttle must be immediately shut down, as defined in CV 1.6.5, if the throttle position differs by more than 10 % from the expected target TPS position for more than 500 ms.

rules.display_text: The power to the electronic throttle must be immediately shut down, as defined in CV 1.6.5, if the throttle position differs by more than 10 % from the expected target TPS position for more than 500 ms.

blocks.text: In order to limit the power capability from the engine(s), a single circular restrictor must be placed in the intake system and all engine(s) airflow must pass through this restrictor. The only allowed sequences of components are the following:
For naturally aspirated engines, the sequence must be: throttle body, restrictor, and engine, see Figure 17
For turbocharged or supercharged engines, the sequence must be: restrictor, compressor, throttle body, engine, see Figure 18

rules.display_text:
In order to limit the power capability from the engine(s), a single circular restrictor must be placed in the intake system and all engine(s) airflow must pass through this restrictor. The only allowed sequences of components are the following:
▪ For naturally aspirated engines, the sequence must be: throttle body, restrictor, and engine, see Figure 17
▪ For turbocharged or supercharged engines, the sequence must be: restrictor, compressor, throttle body, engine, see Figure 18

blocks.text: The maximum restrictor diameters which must be respected at all times during the event are:
Gasoline fueled vehicles - 20 mm
E 85 fueled vehicles - 19 mm

rules.display_text:
The maximum restrictor diameters which must be respected at all times during the event are:
▪ Gasoline fueled vehicles - 20 mm
▪ E 85 fueled vehicles - 19 mm

blocks.text: The restrictor must be located to facilitate measurement during the Technical Inspection process.

rules.display_text: The restrictor must be located to facilitate measurement during the Technical Inspection process.

blocks.text: The circular restricting cross section must not be movable or flexible in any way, e.g. the restrictor must not be part of the movable portion of a barrel throttle body.

rules.display_text:
The circular restricting cross section must not be movable or flexible in any way, e.g. the restrictor must not be part of the movable portion of a barrel throttle body.
[Figure 17: Intake configuration for naturally aspirated engines. — see figure on page 63]
[Figure 18: Intake configuration for turbocharged or supercharged engines. — see figure on page 63]

blocks.text: The intake air may be cooled with an intercooler. Only ambient air may be used to remove heat from the intercooler system. Air-to-air and water-to-air intercoolers are allowed. The coolant of a water-to-air intercooler system must be plain water without any additives.

rules.display_text: The intake air may be cooled with an intercooler. Only ambient air may be used to remove heat from the intercooler system. Air-to-air and water-to-air intercoolers are allowed. The coolant of a water-to-air intercooler system must be plain water without any additives.

blocks.text: If pop-off valves, recirculation valves, or heat exchangers (intercoolers) are used, they may only be positioned in the intake system as shown in Figure 18.

rules.display_text: If pop-off valves, recirculation valves, or heat exchangers (intercoolers) are used, they may only be positioned in the intake system as shown in Figure 18.

blocks.text: Plenums anywhere upstream of the throttle body are prohibited. A “plenum” is any tank or volume that is a significant enlargement of the normal intake runner system.

rules.display_text: Plenums anywhere upstream of the throttle body are prohibited. A “plenum” is any tank or volume that is a significant enlargement of the normal intake runner system.

blocks.text: The maximum allowable internal diameter of the intake runner system between the restrictor and throttle body is 60 mm diameter, or the equivalent area of 2827 mm2 if non-circular.

rules.display_text: The maximum allowable internal diameter of the intake runner system between the restrictor and throttle body is 60 mm diameter, or the equivalent area of 2827 mm2 if non-circular.

blocks.text: Any crankcase or engine lubrication vent lines routed to the intake system must be connected upstream of the intake system restrictor.

rules.display_text: Any crankcase or engine lubrication vent lines routed to the intake system must be connected upstream of the intake system restrictor.

blocks.text: Crankcase breathers that pass through the oil catch tank(s) to exhaust systems, or vacuum devices that connect directly to the exhaust system, are prohibited.

rules.display_text: Crankcase breathers that pass through the oil catch tank(s) to exhaust systems, or vacuum devices that connect directly to the exhaust system, are prohibited.

blocks.text: The available fuel types are unleaded gasoline 98RON and E 85.

rules.display_text: The available fuel types are unleaded gasoline 98RON and E 85.

blocks.text: The vehicles must be operated with the fuel provided at the event.

rules.display_text: The vehicles must be operated with the fuel provided at the event.

blocks.text: No agents other than fuel and air may be induced into the combustion chamber.

rules.display_text: No agents other than fuel and air may be induced into the combustion chamber.

blocks.text: The temperature of fuel introduced into the fuel system must not be changed with the intent to improve calculated efficiency.

rules.display_text: The temperature of fuel introduced into the fuel system must not be changed with the intent to improve calculated efficiency.

blocks.text: The fuel tank must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16, except the fuel filler neck if it is 350 mm above the ground.

rules.display_text: The fuel tank must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16, except the fuel filler neck if it is 350 mm above the ground.

blocks.text: All parts of the fuel storage and supply system must lie within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18.

rules.display_text: All parts of the fuel storage and supply system must lie within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18.

blocks.text: All parts of the fuel storage and supply system must be adequately protected against any heat sources and located at least 50 mm from any exhaust system component.

rules.display_text: All parts of the fuel storage and supply system must be adequately protected against any heat sources and located at least 50 mm from any exhaust system component.

blocks.text: All parts of the fuel system which can come in contact with the fuel must be rated for permanent contact with fuel.

rules.display_text: All parts of the fuel system which can come in contact with the fuel must be rated for permanent contact with fuel.

blocks.text: The fuel tank is defined as the part of the fuel containment device that is in contact with the fuel. It may be made of a rigid material or a flexible material.

rules.display_text: The fuel tank is defined as the part of the fuel containment device that is in contact with the fuel. It may be made of a rigid material or a flexible material.

blocks.text: The fuel tank must be securely mounted to the vehicle structure with mountings that allow some flexibility such that chassis flex cannot unintentionally load the fuel tank.

rules.display_text: The fuel tank must be securely mounted to the vehicle structure with mountings that allow some flexibility such that chassis flex cannot unintentionally load the fuel tank.

blocks.text: The fuel tank must not touch any part of the vehicle other than its mounting and parts of the fuel system at any time.

rules.display_text: The fuel tank must not touch any part of the vehicle other than its mounting and parts of the fuel system at any time.

blocks.text: Any fuel tank that is made from a flexible material, for example a bladder fuel cell or a bag tank, must be enclosed within a rigid fuel tank container which is securely mounted to the vehicle structure. Fuel tank containers (containing a bladder fuel cell or bag tank) may be load carrying.

rules.display_text: Any fuel tank that is made from a flexible material, for example a bladder fuel cell or a bag tank, must be enclosed within a rigid fuel tank container which is securely mounted to the vehicle structure. Fuel tank containers (containing a bladder fuel cell or bag tank) may be load carrying.

blocks.text: The fuel system must have a provision for emptying the fuel tank if required.

rules.display_text: The fuel system must have a provision for emptying the fuel tank if required.

blocks.text: The fuel tank, by design, must not have a variable capacity.

rules.display_text: The fuel tank, by design, must not have a variable capacity.

rules.title: Fuel Lines for Low Pressure Systems
rules.section_title: Fuel Lines for Low Pressure Systems
Fuel Lines for Low Pressure Systems

blocks.text: Fuel lines between fuel tank and fuel rail and return lines must:

have reinforced rubber fuel lines with an abrasion protection with a fuel hose clamp which has a full 360° wrap, a nut and bolt system for tightening and rolled edges to prevent the clamp cutting into the hose, or
have metal braided hoses with crimped-on or reusable, threaded fittings.
be rated for temperatures of at least 120 °C.

rules.display_text:
Fuel lines between fuel tank and fuel rail and return lines must:
▪ have reinforced rubber fuel lines with an abrasion protection with a fuel hose clamp which has a full 360° wrap, a nut and bolt system for tightening and rolled edges to prevent the clamp cutting into the hose, or
▪ have metal braided hoses with crimped-on or reusable, threaded fittings.
▪ be rated for temperatures of at least 120 °C.

rules.section_title: Fuel Lines for Low Pressure Systems

blocks.text: The use of unmodified OEM fuel lines and connectors, including those manufactured from plastic, is acceptable.

rules.display_text: The use of unmodified OEM fuel lines and connectors, including those manufactured from plastic, is acceptable.

rules.section_title: Fuel Lines for Low Pressure Systems

blocks.text: For reinforced rubber fuel lines with hose & clamp style connections beaded or barbed hose fittings must be used.

rules.display_text: For reinforced rubber fuel lines with hose & clamp style connections beaded or barbed hose fittings must be used.

rules.section_title: Fuel Lines for Low Pressure Systems

blocks.text: Fuel lines must be securely mounted.

rules.display_text: Fuel lines must be securely mounted.

rules.section_title: Fuel Lines for Low Pressure Systems

blocks.text: All fuel lines must be shielded from possible rotating equipment failure or collision damage.

rules.display_text: All fuel lines must be shielded from possible rotating equipment failure or collision damage.

rules.section_title: Fuel Lines for Low Pressure Systems

blocks.text: All fuel lines must be fitted in such a way that any leakage cannot result in the accumulation of fuel in the cockpit.

rules.display_text: All fuel lines must be fitted in such a way that any leakage cannot result in the accumulation of fuel in the cockpit.

blocks.text: The following requirements apply to LPI fuel systems:
The fuel lines must comply with CV 2.4.

The fuel rail must be securely mounted to the engine cylinder block, cylinder head, or intake manifold with mechanical fasteners. The threaded fasteners used to secure the fuel rail are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10.

The use of fuel rails made from plastic, carbon fiber or rapid prototyping flammable materials is prohibited. However, the use of unmodified OEM Fuel Rails manufactured from these materials is acceptable.

rules.display_text:
The following requirements apply to LPI fuel systems:
▪ The fuel lines must comply with CV 2.4.
▪ The fuel rail must be securely mounted to the engine cylinder block, cylinder head, or intake manifold with mechanical fasteners. The threaded fasteners used to secure the fuel rail are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10.
▪ The use of fuel rails made from plastic, carbon fiber or rapid prototyping flammable materials is prohibited. However, the use of unmodified OEM Fuel Rails manufactured from these materials is acceptable.

blocks.text: The following requirements apply to HPI and DI fuel systems:

All high pressure fuel lines must be stainless steel rigid line or Aeroquip FC807 smooth bore PTFE hose with stainless steel reinforcement and visible Nomex tracer yarn. Use of elastomeric seals is prohibited. Lines must be securely mounted every 100 mm by mechanical fasteners to structural engine components.

The fuel rail must be securely mounted to the engine cylinder head with mechanical fasteners. The fastening method must be sufficient to hold the fuel rail in place with the maximum regulated pressure acting on the injector internals and neglecting any assistance from in-cylinder pressure acting on the injector tip. The threaded fasteners used to secure the fuel rail are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10.
The fuel pump must be securely mounted to structural engine components.

A fuel pressure regulator must be fitted between the high and low pressure sides of the fuel system in parallel with the DI boost pump. The external regulator must be used even if the DI boost pump comes equipped with an internal regulator.
Before the Tilt Test specified in IN 7, engines fitted with mechanically actuated fuel pumps must be run to fill and pressure the system downstream of the high pressure pump.

rules.display_text:
The following requirements apply to HPI and DI fuel systems:
▪ All high pressure fuel lines must be stainless steel rigid line or Aeroquip FC807 smooth bore PTFE hose with stainless steel reinforcement and visible Nomex tracer yarn. Use of elastomeric seals is prohibited. Lines must be securely mounted every 100 mm by mechanical fasteners to structural engine components.
▪ The fuel rail must be securely mounted to the engine cylinder head with mechanical fasteners. The fastening method must be sufficient to hold the fuel rail in place with the maximum regulated pressure acting on the injector internals and neglecting any assistance from in-cylinder pressure acting on the injector tip. The threaded fasteners used to secure the fuel rail are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10.
▪ The fuel pump must be securely mounted to structural engine components.
▪ A fuel pressure regulator must be fitted between the high and low pressure sides of the fuel system in parallel with the DI boost pump. The external regulator must be used even if the DI boost pump comes equipped with an internal regulator.
▪ Before the Tilt Test specified in IN 7, engines fitted with mechanically actuated fuel pumps must be run to fill and pressure the system downstream of the high pressure pump.

rules.title: Fuel Tank Filler Neck and Sight Tube
rules.section_title: Fuel Tank Filler Neck and Sight Tube
Fuel Tank Filler Neck and Sight Tube

blocks.text: The fuel tank must have a filler neck which:
has at least an inner diameter of 35 mm at any point between the fuel tank and the top of the fuel filler cap.
is accompanied by a clear fuel resistant sight tube above the top of the fuel tank with a length of at least 125 mm vertical height for reading the fuel level, see Figure 19.
is made of material that is permanently rated for temperatures of at least 120 °C.

rules.display_text:
The fuel tank must have a filler neck which:
▪ has at least an inner diameter of 35 mm at any point between the fuel tank and the top of the fuel filler cap.
▪ is accompanied by a clear fuel resistant sight tube above the top of the fuel tank with a length of at least 125 mm vertical height for reading the fuel level, see Figure 19.
▪ is made of material that is permanently rated for temperatures of at least 120 °C.
[Figure 19: Minimum requirements fuel tank filler neck. — see figure on page 66]

rules.section_title: Fuel Tank Filler Neck and Sight Tube

blocks.text: A clear filler neck tube may be used as a sight tube.

rules.display_text: A clear filler neck tube may be used as a sight tube.

rules.section_title: Fuel Tank Filler Neck and Sight Tube

blocks.text: Above the lowest point of the sight tube, the filler neck must not be angled more than 30° from the vertical.

rules.display_text: Above the lowest point of the sight tube, the filler neck must not be angled more than 30° from the vertical.

rules.section_title: Fuel Tank Filler Neck and Sight Tube

blocks.text: A permanent, non-movable, clear and easily visible fuel level line must be located between 12 mm and 25 mm below the top of the visible portion of the sight tube. This line is used as the fill line for the Tilt Test, see IN 7.1, and before and after Endurance to measure the amount of fuel used during Endurance.

rules.display_text: A permanent, non-movable, clear and easily visible fuel level line must be located between 12 mm and 25 mm below the top of the visible portion of the sight tube. This line is used as the fill line for the Tilt Test, see IN 7.1, and before and after Endurance to measure the amount of fuel used during Endurance.

rules.section_title: Fuel Tank Filler Neck and Sight Tube

blocks.text: The filler neck opening must be directly accessible without removing any parts of the vehicle except for the fuel filler cap.

rules.display_text: The filler neck opening must be directly accessible without removing any parts of the vehicle except for the fuel filler cap.

rules.section_title: Fuel Tank Filler Neck and Sight Tube

blocks.text: The filler neck must have a fuel filler cap that can withstand severe vibrations or high pressures such as could occur during a vehicle rollover event.

rules.display_text: The filler neck must have a fuel filler cap that can withstand severe vibrations or high pressures such as could occur during a vehicle rollover event.

blocks.text: The fuel tank must be capable of being filled to capacity without manipulating the tank or the vehicle in any manner. The fuel system must be designed in a way that during refueling of the vehicle on a level surface, the formation of air cavities or other effects that cause the fuel level observed at the sight tube to drop after movement or operation of the vehicle (other than due to consumption) is prevented.

rules.display_text: The fuel tank must be capable of being filled to capacity without manipulating the tank or the vehicle in any manner. The fuel system must be designed in a way that during refueling of the vehicle on a level surface, the formation of air cavities or other effects that cause the fuel level observed at the sight tube to drop after movement or operation of the vehicle (other than due to consumption) is prevented.

blocks.text: The fuel system must be designed such that the spillage during refueling cannot contact the driver position, exhaust system, hot engine parts, or the ignition system.

rules.display_text: The fuel system must be designed such that the spillage during refueling cannot contact the driver position, exhaust system, hot engine parts, or the ignition system.

blocks.text: The fuel tank venting systems must be designed such that fuel cannot spill during hard cornering or acceleration.

rules.display_text: The fuel tank venting systems must be designed such that fuel cannot spill during hard cornering or acceleration.

blocks.text: All fuel vent lines must be equipped with a check valve to prevent fuel leakage when the tank is inverted. All fuel vent lines must exit outside the bodywork.

rules.display_text: All fuel vent lines must be equipped with a check valve to prevent fuel leakage when the tank is inverted. All fuel vent lines must exit outside the bodywork.

blocks.text: The exhaust outlet must be routed to the side or rear of the vehicle and so that the driver is not subjected to fumes at any speed considering the draft of the vehicle.

rules.display_text: The exhaust outlet must be routed to the side or rear of the vehicle and so that the driver is not subjected to fumes at any speed considering the draft of the vehicle.

blocks.text: The exhaust outlet(s) must not extend more than 450 mm behind the centerline of the rear axle and must be no more than 600 mm above the ground.

rules.display_text: The exhaust outlet(s) must not extend more than 450 mm behind the centerline of the rear axle and must be no more than 600 mm above the ground.

blocks.text: Any exhaust components (headers, mufflers, etc.) that protrude from the side of the chassis in front of the rear axle must be shielded to prevent contact by persons approaching the vehicle or a driver exiting the vehicle. The temperature of the outer surface must not be harmful to a person touching it.

rules.display_text: Any exhaust components (headers, mufflers, etc.) that protrude from the side of the chassis in front of the rear axle must be shielded to prevent contact by persons approaching the vehicle or a driver exiting the vehicle. The temperature of the outer surface must not be harmful to a person touching it.

blocks.text: The application of fibrous/absorbent material, e.g. “headerwrap”, to the outside of an exhaust manifold or exhaust system is prohibited.

rules.display_text: The application of fibrous/absorbent material, e.g. “headerwrap”, to the outside of an exhaust manifold or exhaust system is prohibited.

blocks.text: The maximum sound level test speed for a given engine is the engine speed that corresponds to an average piston speed of 15.25 m/s. The calculated speed is rounded to the nearest 500 rpm. The maximum allowed sound level up to this calculated speed is 110 dB(C), fast weighting.

rules.display_text: The maximum sound level test speed for a given engine is the engine speed that corresponds to an average piston speed of 15.25 m/s. The calculated speed is rounded to the nearest 500 rpm. The maximum allowed sound level up to this calculated speed is 110 dB(C), fast weighting.

blocks.text: The idle test speed for a given engine is up to the team and determined by their calibrated idle speed. If the idle speed varies then the vehicle is tested across the range of idle speeds determined by the team. At idle the maximum allowed sound level is 103 dB(C), fast weighting.

rules.display_text: The idle test speed for a given engine is up to the team and determined by their calibrated idle speed. If the idle speed varies then the vehicle is tested across the range of idle speeds determined by the team. At idle the maximum allowed sound level is 103 dB(C), fast weighting.

blocks.text: The Shutdown Circuit (SDC) directly controls all electric power to the ignition, fuel injectors and all fuel pumps. It must act through a minimum of two mechanical relays. One relay for the fuel pump and at least one relay for injection and ignition. An explanatory schematic of the required SDC is shown in Figure 20.

rules.display_text: Hybrid Storage Container (HSC) — the electric energy storage system, including the AIR and overcurrent protection, that is used in the hybrid system.

blocks.text: Moving energy into the HSC from a different electric storage system is prohibited during any dynamic discipline.

rules.display_text: Moving energy into the HSC from a different electric storage system is prohibited during any dynamic discipline.

blocks.text: A firewall, see T 4.8, must be present between the HSC and the fuel tank.

rules.display_text: A firewall, see T 4.8, must be present between the HSC and the fuel tank.

blocks.text: The HSC must be positioned according to T 11.7.2, all other hybrid system components must be positioned within the surface envelope, see T 1.1.18.

blocks.text: Motors must meet EV 2.1.

rules.display_text: Motors must meet EV 2.1.

blocks.text: The hybrid system may only be activated when the combustion engine is running or during engine start.

rules.display_text: The hybrid system may only be activated when the combustion engine is running or during engine start.

blocks.text: The HSC must be attached to the primary structure, see T 1.1.12, according to T 3.3.1.

rules.display_text: The HSC must be attached to the primary structure, see T 1.1.12, according to T 3.3.1.

blocks.text: A disconnection mechanism, designed as an AIR must be integrated inside of the HSC, disconnecting the positive pole of the HSC. The AIR must be compliant with EV 5.6.3.

rules.display_text: A disconnection mechanism, designed as an AIR must be integrated inside of the HSC, disconnecting the positive pole of the HSC. The AIR must be compliant with EV 5.6.3.

blocks.text: The maximum combined total weight of all elements in the hybrid system that store the electric energy, e.g. battery cells or supercapacitors, including all casings and tabs that are integral to them, is 3 kg.

rules.display_text: The maximum combined total weight of all elements in the hybrid system that store the electric energy, e.g. battery cells or supercapacitors, including all casings and tabs that are integral to them, is 3 kg.

blocks.text: Holes, both internal and external, in the HSC, are only allowed for the wiring harness, ventilation, cooling, or fasteners. The total cutout area must be below 25 % of the area of the respective single wall.

blocks.text: Tractive System (TS) — every part that is electrically connected to the motors and TS accumulators. The LVS may be supplied by the TS if a galvanic isolation between both systems is ensured.

rules.display_text: Tractive System (TS) — every part that is electrically connected to the motors and TS accumulators. The LVS may be supplied by the TS if a galvanic isolation between both systems is ensured.

blocks.text: TS enclosures — every housing or enclosure that contains parts of the TS.

rules.display_text: TS enclosures — every housing or enclosure that contains parts of the TS.

blocks.text: Galvanic Isolation — two electric circuits are defined as galvanically isolated if all of the following conditions are true:
The resistance between both circuits is ≥500 Ω/V, related to the maximum TS voltage of the vehicle, at a test voltage of maximum TS voltage or 250 V, whichever is higher.
The isolation test voltage RMS, AC for 1 min, between both circuits is higher than three times the maximum TS voltage or 750 V, whichever is higher.
The working voltage of the isolation barrier, if specified in the datasheet, is higher than the maximum TS voltage.
Capacitors that bridge galvanic isolation must be class-Y capacitors.

rules.display_text:
Galvanic Isolation — two electric circuits are defined as galvanically isolated if all of the following conditions are true:
▪ The resistance between both circuits is ≥500 Ω/V, related to the maximum TS voltage of the vehicle, at a test voltage of maximum TS voltage or 250 V, whichever is higher.
▪ The isolation test voltage RMS, AC for 1 min, between both circuits is higher than three times the maximum TS voltage or 750 V, whichever is higher.
▪ The working voltage of the isolation barrier, if specified in the datasheet, is higher than the maximum TS voltage.
Capacitors that bridge galvanic isolation must be class-Y capacitors.

blocks.text: High Current Path — any path of a TS circuitry that, during normal operation, carries more than 1 A.

rules.display_text: High Current Path — any path of a TS circuitry that, during normal operation, carries more than 1 A.

blocks.text: Only electric motors are allowed.

rules.display_text: Only electric motors are allowed.

rules.display_text: Motor attachments must follow T 10.

rules.display_text: Motor casings must follow T 7.3.

blocks.text: The motor(s) must be connected to the TS accumulator through a motor controller.

rules.display_text: The motor(s) must be connected to the TS accumulator through a motor controller.

blocks.text: The TS power at the outlet of the TSAC must not exceed 80 kW.

rules.display_text: The TS power at the outlet of the TSAC must not exceed 80 kW.

rules.display_text: The TS current at the outlet of the TSAC must not exceed 500 A.

rules.display_text: Regenerating energy is allowed and unrestricted with regard to power.

blocks.text: Wheels must not be spun in reverse.

rules.display_text: Wheels must not be spun in reverse.

blocks.text: TS enclosures, see EV 1.1.2, must consist of either
a grounded solid layer made of at least 0.5 mm thick electrically conductive material, aluminium or better, see EV 3.1.3 or

be made out of electrically insulating materials providing an insulation resistance of at least 2 MΩ, measured at a voltage of 500 V, between the inside and the outside of the enclosure. The TS enclosure must be rigid and must prevent possible mechanical penetrations. Protruding electrically conductive parts, such as fasteners or connectors, must follow EV 3.1.2
The TSAC might use at least 0.9 mm thick steel layer as the grounded layer.

rules.display_text:
TS enclosures, see EV 1.1.2, must consist of either
▪ a grounded solid layer made of at least 0.5 mm thick electrically conductive material, aluminium or better, see EV 3.1.3 or
▪ be made out of electrically insulating materials providing an insulation resistance of at least 2 MΩ, measured at a voltage of 500 V, between the inside and the outside of the enclosure. blocks.text: Electrically conductive seat, driver harness, and firewall mounting points as well as the aluminium layer of the TS firewall, see T 4.8, and the LVS ground measuring point, see EV 4.7.8, must be grounded, see EV 3.1.3.

blocks.text: An electrically conductive part is grounded if its resistance to LVS ground is below 100 mΩ, measured with a current of 1 A, and the grounding wire is able to continuously carry at least 10 % of the TS accumulator main fuse current rating.

rules.display_text: An electrically conductive part is grounded if its resistance to LVS ground is below 100 mΩ, measured with a current of 1 A, and the grounding wire is able to continuously carry at least 10 % of the TS accumulator main fuse current rating.

blocks.text: The rotating part of the wheels does not need to be grounded.

blocks.text: All electric systems must have appropriate overcurrent protection.

rules.display_text: All electric systems must have appropriate overcurrent protection.

blocks.text: The continuous current rating of the overcurrent protection must not be greater than the continuous current rating of any electric component, for example, wire, busbar, or other conductors that it protects. blocks.text: All used fuses must have an interrupt current rating that is higher than the theoretical short circuit current of the system that it protects.

rules.display_text: All used fuses must have an interrupt current rating that is higher than the theoretical short circuit current of the system that it protects.

blocks.text: All overcurrent protection devices must be rated for the highest voltage in the systems they protect. All devices used must be rated for DC.

blocks.text: All overcurrent protection devices that are part of the TS must not rely on programmable logic. The overcurrent protection function of motor controllers/inverters for the motor outputs may rely on programmable logic.

blocks.text: All components in the TS must be rated for the maximum TS voltage. The TS area of a PCB, see EV 4.3.6, is considered as one component. Every input connected to the TS must be rated to the maximum TS voltage.

rules.display_text: All components in the TS must be rated for the maximum TS voltage. The TS area of a PCB, see EV 4.3.6, is considered as one component. Every input connected to the TS must be rated to the maximum TS voltage.

rules.display_text: All components must be rated for the maximum possible temperature that may occur during usage.

blocks.text: TS enclosures, see EV 1.1.2, must be labeled with reasonably sized stickers according to “ISO 7010-W012” (triangle with a black lightning bolt on a yellow background). The sticker must also contain the text “High Voltage” if the voltage is more than 60 V DC or 50 V AC RMS.

blocks.text: Teams must be prepared to demonstrate spacing on team-built equipment. For inaccessible circuitry, fully assembled spare boards must be available.

rules.display_text: Teams must be prepared to demonstrate spacing on team-built equipment. For inaccessible circuitry, fully assembled spare boards must be available.

blocks.text: Except what is allowed according to EV 4.4.3, all parts belonging to the TS including cables and wiring must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16. “Part” is the whole device such as the complete HVD.

rules.display_text: Except what is allowed according to EV 4.4.3, all parts belonging to the TS including cables and wiring must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16. “Part” is the whole device such as the complete HVD.

blocks.text: Any part of the TS that is less than 350 mm above the ground, except what is allowed according to EV 4.4.3, must be protected from impacts, see T 3.15. Impact protection must follow T 3.16 when having bolted attachments. TS wiring in front of the front hoop may alternatively be shielded by the front bulkhead support structure according to T 3.14.

rules.display_text: Any part of the TS that is less than 350 mm above the ground, except what is allowed according to EV 4.4.3, must be protected from impacts, see T 3.15. Impact protection must follow T 3.16 when having bolted attachments. TS wiring in front of the front hoop may alternatively be shielded by the front bulkhead support structure according to T 3.14.

blocks.text: Outboard wheel motors are allowed only if
an interlock is routed along the TS wiring such that the SDC, see EV 6, is opened before the TS wiring or its clamping fails
an interlock is routed along a suspension member such that the SDC, see EV 6, is opened if the suspension fails
TS wiring is not able to reach the cockpit opening or the driver regardless of where it breaks
wiring outside of the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16 is minimum length
wiring outside of an impact structure or front bulkhead support structure, see EV 4.4.2, is minimum length
Minimum length is the shortest distance plus extra wiring caused by bending radius.

rules.display_text:
Outboard wheel motors are allowed only if
▪ an interlock is routed along the TS wiring such that the SDC, see EV 6, is opened before the TS wiring or its clamping fails
▪ an interlock is routed along a suspension member such that the SDC, see EV 6, is opened if the suspension fails
▪ TS wiring is not able to reach the cockpit opening or the driver regardless of where it breaks
▪ wiring outside of the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16 is minimum length
▪ wiring outside of an impact structure or front bulkhead support structure, see EV 4.4.2, is minimum length
▪ Minimum length is the shortest distance plus extra wiring caused by bending radius.
