blocks.text: All live parts of the TS must be protected from being touched. This must include team members working on or inside the vehicle. This is tested with a 100 mm long, 6 mm diameter insulated test probe when the TS enclosures are in place.

rules.display_text: All live parts of the TS must be protected from being touched. This must include team members working on or inside the vehicle. This is tested with a 100 mm long, 6 mm diameter insulated test probe when the TS enclosures are in place.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: Insulation material that is rated for the maximum TS voltage must be used. Using only insulating tape or rubber-like paint for insulation is prohibited.

rules.display_text: Insulation material that is rated for the maximum TS voltage must be used. Using only insulating tape or rubber-like paint for insulation is prohibited.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: The temperature rating for TS wiring, connections, relays, and insulation must be appropriate for the expected surrounding temperatures but at least 85 °C.

rules.display_text: The temperature rating for TS wiring, connections, relays, and insulation must be appropriate for the expected surrounding temperatures but at least 85 °C.
changelog: Added relays to temperature rating requirement

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: TS components and TS enclosures must be protected from moisture in the form of rain or puddles, see IN 9.

rules.display_text: TS components and TS enclosures must be protected from moisture in the form of rain or puddles, see IN 9.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: It must be possible to clearly assign and prove the wire gauge, temperature rating, and insulation voltage to each used TS wire.

rules.display_text: It must be possible to clearly assign and prove the wire gauge, temperature rating, and insulation voltage to each used TS wire.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: All TS wiring must be completed to professional standards with appropriately sized conductors and terminals and with adequate strain relief and protection from loosening due to vibration etc.

rules.display_text: All TS wiring must be completed to professional standards with appropriately sized conductors and terminals and with adequate strain relief and protection from loosening due to vibration etc.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: TS wiring must be located out of the way of possible snagging or damage.

rules.display_text: TS wiring must be located out of the way of possible snagging or damage.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: All TS wiring that runs outside of TS enclosures must:
be enclosed in separate orange non-conductive conduit or use an orange shielded cable. The conduit must be securely mounted to the vehicle, but not to the wire, at least at each end.
be securely mounted at least at each end so that it can withstand a force of 200 N without straining the cable end crimp.
Bodywork is not sufficient to meet this enclosure requirement.

rules.display_text:
All TS wiring that runs outside of TS enclosures must:
▪ be enclosed in separate orange non-conductive conduit or use an orange shielded cable. The conduit must be securely mounted to the vehicle, but not to the wire, at least at each end.
▪ be securely mounted at least at each end so that it can withstand a force of 200 N without straining the cable end crimp.
Bodywork is not sufficient to meet this enclosure requirement.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: Any shielded TS cable must have the shield grounded.

rules.display_text: Any shielded TS cable must have the shield grounded.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: Every TS connector outside TS enclosures must include a pilot contact/interlock line which is part of the SDC. TS enclosures only used to avoid interlocks are prohibited.

rules.display_text: Every TS connector outside TS enclosures must include a pilot contact/interlock line which is part of the SDC. TS enclosures only used to avoid interlocks are prohibited.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: All TS connections must be designed so that they use intentional current paths through conductors such as copper or aluminium and must not rely on steel bolts to be the primary conductor.

rules.display_text: All TS connections must be designed so that they use intentional current paths through conductors such as copper or aluminium and must not rely on steel bolts to be the primary conductor.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: All materials used in a stack-up or as a fastener of a TS connection must ensure equal pressure across the full contact area over the entire temperature range.

rules.display_text: All materials used in a stack-up or as a fastener of a TS connection must ensure equal pressure across the full contact area over the entire temperature range.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: All electric connections, including bolts, nuts, and other fasteners, in the high current path, see EV 1.2.2, of the TS must be secured from unintentional loosening. Fasteners must use positive locking mechanisms, see T 10.2, that are suitable for high temperatures, see EV 4.5.3. Components, e.g. inverters, certified for automotive use might be allowed without a positive locking feature if connections are completed as recommended by the manufacturers’ datasheet and no positive locking is possible.

rules.display_text: All electric connections, including bolts, nuts, and other fasteners, in the high current path, see EV 1.2.2, of the TS must be secured from unintentional loosening. Fasteners must use positive locking mechanisms, see T 10.2, that are suitable for high temperatures, see EV 4.5.3. Components, e.g. inverters, certified for automotive use might be allowed without a positive locking feature if connections are completed as recommended by the manufacturers’ datasheet and no positive locking is possible.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: Teams must be prepared to demonstrate positive locking. For inaccessible connections, appropriate photographs must be available.

rules.display_text: Teams must be prepared to demonstrate positive locking. For inaccessible connections, appropriate photographs must be available.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Insulation, Wiring, and Conduit

blocks.text: Soldered connections in the TS high current path, see EV 1.2.2, are only allowed if all of the following are true:
connections on PCBs
the connected devices are not cells or wires
the devices are additionally mechanically secured against loosening

rules.display_text:
Soldered connections in the TS high current path, see EV 1.2.2, are only allowed if all of the following are true:
▪ connections on PCBs
▪ the connected devices are not cells or wires
▪ the devices are additionally mechanically secured against loosening

blocks.text: A data logger is provided by the officials and must be inserted during the event. The data logger measures TS voltage and TS current.

rules.display_text: A data logger is provided by the officials and must be inserted during the event. The data logger measures TS voltage and TS current.

blocks.text: The data logger must be in an easily accessible location so that it is possible to insert, remove, or replace it within 15 min in ready-to-race condition.

rules.display_text: The data logger must be in an easily accessible location so that it is possible to insert, remove, or replace it within 15 min in ready-to-race condition.

blocks.text: The data logger must not be placed within the TSAC.

rules.display_text: The data logger must not be placed within the TSAC.

blocks.text: All current supplying the TS must run through the data logger. The data logger must be inserted in the negative TS supply between the most negative AIR and the inverters.

rules.display_text: All current supplying the TS must run through the data logger. The data logger must be inserted in the negative TS supply between the most negative AIR and the inverters.

blocks.text: The TS voltage sense connection of the data logger must be directly connected, see T 1.3.1, to the most positive AIR on the vehicle side. If overcurrent protection is used, it must be a fuse.

rules.display_text: The TS voltage sense connection of the data logger must be directly connected, see T 1.3.1, to the most positive AIR on the vehicle side. If overcurrent protection is used, it must be a fuse.

blocks.text: The specification of the data logger is available in the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: The specification of the data logger is available in the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: Two TSMPs must be installed directly next to the master switches, see T 11.2.

rules.display_text: Two TSMPs must be installed directly next to the master switches, see T 11.2.

blocks.text: The TSMPs must be directly connected, see T 1.3.1, to the intermediate circuit capacitors even if the HVD has been removed or the TS accumulator is disconnected.

rules.display_text: The TSMPs must be directly connected, see T 1.3.1, to the intermediate circuit capacitors even if the HVD has been removed or the TS accumulator is disconnected.

blocks.text: 4 mm shrouded banana jacks rated for 600 V CAT III or better must be used.

rules.display_text: 4 mm shrouded banana jacks rated for 600 V CAT III or better must be used.

blocks.text: The TSMPs must be marked “TS+” and “TS-” and exclusively mounted on an orange background.

rules.display_text: The TSMPs must be marked “TS+” and “TS-” and exclusively mounted on an orange background.

blocks.text: The TSMPs must be protected by a non-conductive cover that can be opened without tools. The cover must always be mechanically linked to the vehicle.

rules.display_text: The TSMPs must be protected by a non-conductive cover that can be opened without tools. The cover must always be mechanically linked to the vehicle.

blocks.text: Each TSMP must be secured with a current limiting resistor according to the following table. Fusing the TSMPs is prohibited. The resistor’s power rating must be chosen such that they can continuously carry the current if both TSMPs are short-circuited.

rules.display_text:
Each TSMP must be secured with a current limiting resistor according to the following table. Fusing the TSMPs is prohibited. The resistor’s power rating must be chosen such that they can continuously carry the current if both TSMPs are short-circuited.
[Table — see table on page 74]
  Maximum TS Voltage | Resistor Value
  Umax <200 V DC | 5 kΩ
  200 V DC < Umax ≤400 V DC | 10 kΩ
  400 V DC < Umax ≤600 V DC | 15 kΩ

blocks.text: All electric connections needed to connect the TSMP to the intermediate circuit capacitors, including bolts, nuts, and other fasteners, must be secured from unintentional loosening by the use of positive locking mechanisms. Bolted connections must follow T 10.2, soldered connections EV 4.5.15.

rules.display_text: All electric connections needed to connect the TSMP to the intermediate circuit capacitors, including bolts, nuts, and other fasteners, must be secured from unintentional loosening by the use of positive locking mechanisms. Bolted connections must follow T 10.2, soldered connections EV 4.5.15.

blocks.text: Next to the TSMPs an LVS ground measuring point must be installed. A 4 mm black shrouded banana jack must be connected to LVS ground and must be marked “GND”.

rules.display_text: Next to the TSMPs an LVS ground measuring point must be installed. A 4 mm black shrouded banana jack must be connected to LVS ground and must be marked “GND”.

blocks.text: It must be possible to disconnect at least one pole of the TS accumulator by quickly removing an unobstructed and directly accessible element, fuse, or connector. It must be possible to remove the HVD without removing any bodywork. The HVD must be above 350 mm from the ground. Remote actuation of the HVD through a long handle, rope, or wire is not allowed.

rules.display_text: It must be possible to disconnect at least one pole of the TS accumulator by quickly removing an unobstructed and directly accessible element, fuse, or connector. It must be possible to remove the HVD without removing any bodywork. The HVD must be above 350 mm from the ground. Remote actuation of the HVD through a long handle, rope, or wire is not allowed.

blocks.text: Any trained person must be able to remove the HVD within 10 s when the vehicle is in ready-to-race condition.

rules.display_text: Any trained person must be able to remove the HVD within 10 s when the vehicle is in ready-to-race condition.
changelog: Changed description from ESO to trained person

blocks.text: A dummy connector or similar may be required to restore the system’s insulation, see EV 4.5. The dummy connector must be attached to the push bar, see T 13.1, if not in use.

rules.display_text: A dummy connector or similar may be required to restore the system’s insulation, see EV 4.5. The dummy connector must be attached to the push bar, see T 13.1, if not in use.
changelog: Changed wording from isolation to insulation

blocks.text: The HVD must be clearly marked with “HVD”.

rules.display_text: The HVD must be clearly marked with “HVD”.

blocks.text: No tools must be necessary to remove the HVD. An interlock is required, see EV 4.5.10.

rules.display_text: No tools must be necessary to remove the HVD. An interlock is required, see EV 4.5.10.

blocks.text: If a discharge circuit is required to meet EV 6.1.5, it must be designed to handle the maximum TS voltage permanently. After three subsequent discharges within 15 s in total, the discharge time specified in EV 6.1.5 may be exceeded. Full discharging functionality must be given after a reasonable time with a deactivated discharge circuit.

rules.display_text: If a discharge circuit is required to meet EV 6.1.5, it must be designed to handle the maximum TS voltage permanently. After three subsequent discharges within 15 s in total, the discharge time specified in EV 6.1.5 may be exceeded. Full discharging functionality must be given after a reasonable time with a deactivated discharge circuit.

blocks.text: The discharge circuit must be wired in a way that it is always active whenever the SDC is open. Furthermore, the discharge circuit must be fail-safe such that it still discharges the intermediate circuit capacitors if the HVD has been removed or the TS accumulator is disconnected.

rules.display_text: The discharge circuit must be wired in a way that it is always active whenever the SDC is open. Furthermore, the discharge circuit must be fail-safe such that it still discharges the intermediate circuit capacitors if the HVD has been removed or the TS accumulator is disconnected.

blocks.text: Fusing of the discharge main current path is prohibited.

rules.display_text: Fusing of the discharge main current path is prohibited.

blocks.text: The vehicles must include a single TSAL that must indicate the TS status. The TSAL must not perform any other functions. A TSAL with multiple LEDs in one housing is allowed.

rules.display_text: The vehicles must include a single TSAL that must indicate the TS status. The TSAL must not perform any other functions. A TSAL with multiple LEDs in one housing is allowed.

blocks.text: The TSAL itself must have a red light, flashing continuously with a frequency between 2 Hz and 5 Hz and a duty cycle of 50 %, active if and only if the LVS is active and the voltage across any DC-link capacitor exceeds
60 V DC or 50 V AC RMS
half the nominal TS voltage
whichever is lower.

rules.display_text:
The TSAL itself must have a red light, flashing continuously with a frequency between 2 Hz and 5 Hz and a duty cycle of 50 %, active if and only if the LVS is active and the voltage across any DC-link capacitor exceeds
▪ 60 V DC or 50 V AC RMS
▪ half the nominal TS voltage
whichever is lower.

blocks.text: The TSAL itself must have a green light, continuously on, active if and only if the LVS is active and ALL of the following conditions are true:
All AIRs are opened.
The pre-charge relay, see EV 5.7.2, is opened.
The voltage at the vehicle side of the AIRs inside the TSAC does not exceed 60 V DC or 50 V AC RMS.

rules.display_text:
The TSAL itself must have a green light, continuously on, active if and only if the LVS is active and ALL of the following conditions are true:
▪ All AIRs are opened.
▪ The pre-charge relay, see EV 5.7.2, is opened.
▪ The voltage at the vehicle side of the AIRs inside the TSAC does not exceed 60 V DC or 50 V AC RMS.

blocks.text: The mentioned voltage detection must be performed inside the respective TS enclosure.

rules.display_text: The mentioned voltage detection must be performed inside the respective TS enclosure.

blocks.text: The mentioned states of the relays (opened/closed) are the actual mechanical states. The mechanical state can differ from the intentional state, i.e. if a relay is stuck. Any circuitry detecting the mechanical state must meet EV 5.6.2.

rules.display_text: The mentioned states of the relays (opened/closed) are the actual mechanical states. The mechanical state can differ from the intentional state, i.e. if a relay is stuck. Any circuitry detecting the mechanical state must meet EV 5.6.2.

blocks.text: The voltage detection circuit of the red light and the relay state and voltage detection circuit of the green light must be independent. Any plausibility check between both lights is not allowed. A TSAL state with both lights simultaneously active might occur and must not be prevented.

rules.display_text: The voltage detection circuit of the red light and the relay state and voltage detection circuit of the green light must be independent. Any plausibility check between both lights is not allowed. A TSAL state with both lights simultaneously active might occur and must not be prevented.

blocks.text: The TSAL must:
be located lower than the highest point of the main hoop and including the mounting within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16.
be no lower than 75 mm from the highest point of the main hoop.
not be able to contact the driver’s helmet in any circumstances.

rules.display_text:
The TSAL must:
▪ be located lower than the highest point of the main hoop and including the mounting within the rollover protection envelope, see T 1.1.16.
▪ be no lower than 75 mm from the highest point of the main hoop.
▪ not be able to contact the driver’s helmet in any circumstances.

blocks.text: The entire illuminated surface of the TSAL must be clearly visible:
except for angles less than 10° on each side which are blocked by the main hoop.
from a point 1.60 m vertically from ground level, within 3 m horizontal radius from the TSAL.
in direct sunlight.

rules.display_text:
The entire illuminated surface of the TSAL must be clearly visible:
▪ except for angles less than 10° on each side which are blocked by the main hoop.
▪ from a point 1.60 m vertically from ground level, within 3 m horizontal radius from the TSAL.
▪ in direct sunlight.

blocks.text: The TSAL and all needed circuitry must be hard-wired electronics. Software control is not allowed.

rules.display_text: The TSAL and all needed circuitry must be hard-wired electronics. Software control is not allowed.

blocks.text: A green indicator light in the cockpit that is easily visible even in bright sunlight and clearly marked with “TS off” must light up if TSAL green light is on, see EV 4.10.3.

rules.display_text: A green indicator light in the cockpit that is easily visible even in bright sunlight and clearly marked with “TS off” must light up if TSAL green light is on, see EV 4.10.3.

blocks.text: Signals influencing the TSAL and the indicator according to EV 4.10.10 are SCS, see T 11.9. The individual safe state of each of the TSAL lights is off. The TSAL’s red light must not be illuminated for a visible check, see T 11.9.6.

rules.display_text: Signals influencing the TSAL and the indicator according to EV 4.10.10 are SCS, see T 11.9. The individual safe state of each of the TSAL lights is off. The TSAL’s red light must not be illuminated for a visible check, see T 11.9.6.

blocks.text: The TSAL’s red light voltage detection circuit, see EV 4.10.2, does not need to detect an open circuit, as required by T 11.9. A plausibility check must not be implemented.

rules.display_text: The TSAL’s red light voltage detection circuit, see EV 4.10.2, does not need to detect an open circuit, as required by T 11.9. A plausibility check must not be implemented.

blocks.text: The TSAL’s green light relay state detection circuit, see EV 4.10.3, does not need to detect an open circuit, as required by T 11.9, when the intentional state of the used (auxiliary) contact is opened. A plausibility check against the intentional relay state must be implemented in a way that the TSAL’s green light stays off after the open circuit is detectable.

rules.display_text: The TSAL’s green light relay state detection circuit, see EV 4.10.3, does not need to detect an open circuit, as required by T 11.9, when the intentional state of the used (auxiliary) contact is opened. A plausibility check against the intentional relay state must be implemented in a way that the TSAL’s green light stays off after the open circuit is detectable.

blocks.text: The TSAL’s green light voltage detection circuit, see EV 4.10.3, does not need to detect an open circuit, as required by T 11.9, when no voltage is present. A plausibility check against the intentional relay states must be implemented in a way that the TSAL’s green light stays off after the open circuit of the TS accumulator voltage detection circuit is detectable.

rules.display_text: The TSAL’s green light voltage detection circuit, see EV 4.10.3, does not need to detect an open circuit, as required by T 11.9, when no voltage is present. A plausibility check against the intentional relay states must be implemented in a way that the TSAL’s green light stays off after the open circuit of the TS accumulator voltage detection circuit is detectable.

blocks.text: The latching required by EV 4.10.13 and EV 4.10.14 must not be triggered during normal operation conditions and must only be reset by power cycling the LVS.

rules.display_text: The latching required by EV 4.10.13 and EV 4.10.14 must not be triggered during normal operation conditions and must only be reset by power cycling the LVS.

blocks.text: The TS is active if any of the AIRs or the pre-charge relay is closed.

rules.display_text: The TS is active if any of the AIRs or the pre-charge relay is closed.

blocks.text: The driver must be able to activate and deactivate the TS from within the cockpit without the assistance of any other person.

rules.display_text: The driver must be able to activate and deactivate the TS from within the cockpit without the assistance of any other person.

blocks.text: The ASR must be able to activate the TS from outside the vehicle with an external TS activation button in proximity to the TSMS if and only if the ASMS is in “On” position.

rules.display_text: The ASR must be able to activate the TS from outside the vehicle with an external TS activation button in proximity to the TSMS if and only if the ASMS is in “On” position.

blocks.text: Closing the SDC by any part defined in EV 6.1.2 must not (re-)activate the TS. Additional action must be required.

rules.display_text: Closing the SDC by any part defined in EV 6.1.2 must not (re-)activate the TS. Additional action must be required.

blocks.text: The AS must not be able to (re-)activate the TS.

rules.display_text: The AS must not be able to (re-)activate the TS.

blocks.text: The vehicle is in Ready-to-drive (R2D) mode as soon as the motors respond to the input of the APPS.

rules.display_text: The vehicle is in Ready-to-drive (R2D) mode as soon as the motors respond to the input of the APPS.

blocks.text: After the TS has been activated, additional actions must be required by the driver to set the vehicle to R2D mode, e.g. pressing a dedicated start button. The transition to R2D mode must only be possible during the actuation of the mechanical brakes and a simultaneous dedicated additional action.

rules.display_text: After the TS has been activated, additional actions must be required by the driver to set the vehicle to R2D mode, e.g. pressing a dedicated start button. The transition to R2D mode must only be possible during the actuation of the mechanical brakes and a simultaneous dedicated additional action.

blocks.text: The R2D mode must be left immediately when the SDC is opened.

rules.display_text: The R2D mode must be left immediately when the SDC is opened.

blocks.text: The vehicle must make a characteristic sound, continuously for at least 1 s and a maximum of 3 s while entering R2D mode.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must make a characteristic sound, continuously for at least 1 s and a maximum of 3 s while entering R2D mode.

blocks.text: The sound level must be a minimum of 80 dB(A) and a maximum of 90 dB(A), fast weighting in a radius of 2 m around the vehicle.

rules.display_text: The sound level must be a minimum of 80 dB(A) and a maximum of 90 dB(A), fast weighting in a radius of 2 m around the vehicle.

blocks.text: The used sound must be easily recognizable. No animal voices, song parts, or sounds that could be interpreted as offensive are allowed.

rules.display_text: The used sound must be easily recognizable. No animal voices, song parts, or sounds that could be interpreted as offensive are allowed.

blocks.text: The vehicle must not make any other sounds similar to the R2D sound.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must not make any other sounds similar to the R2D sound.

blocks.text: Cell — a battery cell or super-capacitor.

rules.display_text: Cell — a battery cell or super-capacitor.

blocks.text: Cell Energy — the maximum cell voltage times the nominal capacity of the used cell.

rules.display_text: Cell Energy — the maximum cell voltage times the nominal capacity of the used cell.

blocks.text: TS Accumulator — all cells that store the electric energy to be used by the TS as a whole.

blocks.text: Spare cells must be stored in an electrically insulated container made of fire retardant material, see T 1.2.1. The cells must be securely mounted inside the container to prevent any movement. The container must be labeled as specified in EV 5.3.5. If this container is placed within another container, the outer container must also be labeled in accordance with EV 5.3.5.

rules.display_text: Spare cells must be stored in an electrically insulated container made of fire retardant material, see T 1.2.1. blocks.text: Cells must be operated within the limits written in the datasheet or what is given in the respective rules, whichever is more restrictive.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – General Requirements

blocks.text: Each TSAC must be removable from the vehicle while still remaining rules compliant without the need to install extra components. A dummy connector or similar may be used to restore the system’s insulation, see EV 4.5.

rules.display_text: Each TSAC must be removable from the vehicle while still remaining rules compliant without the need to install extra components. A dummy connector or similar may be used to restore the system’s insulation, see EV 4.5.
changelog: Changed wording from isolation to insulation

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – General Requirements

blocks.text: It must be possible to open the TSAC for Technical Inspection.

rules.display_text: It must be possible to open the TSAC for Technical Inspection.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – General Requirements

blocks.text: When the TSAC is outside of the vehicle, it must be possible to remove all TS accumulator segments at any time without the need to move, lift, or tilt the TSAC. The time to remove each TS accumulator segment after opening the lid must be less than 15 min.

rules.display_text: When the TSAC is outside of the vehicle, it must be possible to remove all TS accumulator segments at any time without the need to move, lift, or tilt the TSAC. The time to remove each TS accumulator segment after opening the lid must be less than 15 min.
changelog: Added stack removal requirements

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – General Requirements

blocks.text: Each TS accumulator section, see EV 5.1.4, must never exceed a maximum voltage of 120 V DC, a maximum energy of 6 MJ, see EV 5.1.2, and a maximum mass of 12 kg.

rules.display_text: Each TS accumulator section, see EV 5.1.4, must never exceed a maximum voltage of 120 V DC, a maximum energy of 6 MJ, see EV 5.1.2, and a maximum mass of 12 kg.
changelog: Changed Segment to Section and removed the word “static”

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – General Requirements

blocks.text: The vehicle number, the university name, and the ESO phone numbers must be displayed and written in Roman Sans-Serif characters of at least 20 mm high on the lid of each TSAC. The characters must be clearly visible and placed on a high-contrast background.

rules.display_text: The vehicle number, the university name, and the ESO phone numbers must be displayed and written in Roman Sans-Serif characters of at least 20 mm high on the lid of each TSAC. The characters must be clearly visible and placed on a high-contrast background.

rules.title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration
rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration
changelog: Reorganized section

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: Every TSAC must contain at least one fuse and at least two AIRs, see EV 5.6 and EV 3.2.7.

rules.display_text: Every TSAC must contain at least one fuse and at least two AIRs, see EV 5.6 and EV 3.2.7.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: Every TSAC must have a prominent indicator, a voltmeter, or a red LED visible even in bright sunlight. If a red LED is used as an indicator, it must continuously illuminate at its full brightness whenever a voltage greater than 60 V DC or half the maximum TS voltage, whichever is lower, is present at the vehicle side of the AIRs.

rules.display_text: Every TSAC must have a prominent indicator, a voltmeter, or a red LED visible even in bright sunlight. If a red LED is used as an indicator, it must continuously illuminate at its full brightness whenever a voltage greater than 60 V DC or half the maximum TS voltage, whichever is lower, is present at the vehicle side of the AIRs.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: The indicator must be clearly visible while disconnecting the TSAC from the vehicles. The indicator must be clearly marked with “Voltage Indicator”

rules.display_text: The indicator must be clearly visible while disconnecting the TSAC from the vehicles. The indicator must be clearly marked with “Voltage Indicator”

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: The indicator must be hard-wired electronics without software control, directly and only supplied by the TS from the vehicle side of the AIRs, and always working, even if the TS accumulator is disconnected from the LVS or removed from the vehicle.

rules.display_text: The indicator must be hard-wired electronics without software control, directly and only supplied by the TS from the vehicle side of the AIRs, and always working, even if the TS accumulator is disconnected from the LVS or removed from the vehicle.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: LVS must not be included in the TSAC except where inherently required. Exceptions include the AIRs, TS DC/DC converters, the AMS, the IMD, the TSAL’s green light circuitry, and cooling fans.

rules.display_text: LVS must not be included in the TSAC except where inherently required. Exceptions include the AIRs, TS DC/DC converters, the AMS, the IMD, the TSAL’s green light circuitry, and cooling fans.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: Every wire used in a TSAC, regardless of whether it is part of the LVS or TS, must follow EV 4.5.2, EV 4.5.3, and EV 4.5.5, the exception being wires used in the intent of EV 5.8.11.

rules.display_text: Every wire used in a TSAC, regardless of whether it is part of the LVS or TS, must follow EV 4.5.2, EV 4.5.3, and EV 4.5.5, the exception being wires used in the intent of EV 5.8.11.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: Maintenance plugs must allow electrical separation of all TS accumulator segments, see EV 5.3.4. The separation must affect both poles of all segments including the first and last segment.

rules.display_text: Maintenance plugs must allow electrical separation of all TS accumulator segments, see EV 5.3.4. The separation must affect both poles of all segments including the first and last segment.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: Maintenance plugs must:
not require tools to separate the TS accumulator segments.
be non-conductive on surfaces that do not provide any electric connection.
be designed in a way, that it is physically impossible to electrically connect them in any way other than the design intent configuration.
be protected against accidental reconnection.
be designed such that it is clearly visible whether the connection is open or closed. Electrically controlled switches must not be used.

rules.display_text:
Maintenance plugs must:
▪ not require tools to separate the TS accumulator segments.
▪ be non-conductive on surfaces that do not provide any electric connection.
▪ be designed in a way, that it is physically impossible to electrically connect them in any way other than the design intent configuration.
▪ be protected against accidental reconnection.
▪ be designed such that it is clearly visible whether the connection is open or closed. Electrically controlled switches must not be used.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration

blocks.text: Each TS accumulator segment must be electrically insulated by the use of suitable rigid and fire retardant material, see T 1.2.1, on top of the segment to prevent arc flashes caused by inter-segment contact or by parts/tools accidentally falling into the TSAC during maintenance.

rules.display_text: Each TS accumulator segment must be electrically insulated by the use of suitable rigid and fire retardant material, see T 1.2.1, on top of the segment to prevent arc flashes caused by inter-segment contact or by parts/tools accidentally falling into the TSAC during maintenance.

rules.title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration
rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration
changelog: Reorganized section

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: All TSACs must lie fully within and be attached to the primary structure. In side view the TSACs may not exceed the height of the impact structure, see T 3.15.

rules.display_text: All TSACs must lie fully within and be attached to the primary structure. In side view the TSACs may not exceed the height of the impact structure, see T 3.15.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: The structures surrounding the TSACs must protect it from impacts, see T 3.15. Impact protection must follow T 3.16 when having bolted attachments. No part of the TSAC may be part of the primary structure.

rules.display_text: The structures surrounding the TSACs must protect it from impacts, see T 3.15. Impact protection must follow T 3.16 when having bolted attachments. No part of the TSAC may be part of the primary structure.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: All TSAC materials as well as all structural parts used to comply with EV 5.5.8 must be fire retardant, see T 1.2.1. All calculations must be conducted for an ambient temperature of 60 °C except for metallic materials and continuous fiber-reinforced laminates.

rules.display_text: All TSAC materials as well as all structural parts used to comply with EV 5.5.8 must be fire retardant, see T 1.2.1. All calculations must be conducted for an ambient temperature of 60 °C except for metallic materials and continuous fiber-reinforced laminates.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: The design of the TSAC and its contents, calculations and/or tests must be documented in the ASES. This includes materials used, drawings, images, fastener locations, section weight, cell, and section position.

rules.display_text: The design of the TSAC and its contents, calculations and/or tests must be documented in the ASES. This includes materials used, drawings, images, fastener locations, section weight, cell, and section position.
changelog: Changed segment to section

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: TSACs must be constructed of steel or aluminium, with the following requirements:
The bottom of the TSAC must be at least 1.25 mm thick if made from steel or 3.2 mm if made from aluminium.
The internal and external vertical walls, covers, and lids must be at least 0.9 mm thick if made from steel or 2.3 mm if made from aluminium.

Alternative materials are allowed with proof of equivalency per T 3.4 or for composite materials per EV 5.5.6. When alternative materials are used, test samples must be presented at Technical Inspection.

rules.display_text:
TSACs must be constructed of steel or aluminium, with the following requirements:
▪ The bottom of the TSAC must be at least 1.25 mm thick if made from steel or 3.2 mm if made from aluminium.
▪ The internal and external vertical walls, covers, and lids must be at least 0.9 mm thick if made from steel or 2.3 mm if made from aluminium.
Alternative materials are allowed with proof of equivalency per T 3.4 or for composite materials per EV 5.5.6. When alternative materials are used, test samples must be presented at Technical Inspection.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: Composite TSACs must satisfy the following requirements:
Data obtained from the laminate perimeter shear strength test and three-point bending test, see T 3.6, should be used to prove adequate strength is provided.
Each attachment point requires steel backing plates with a minimum thickness of 2 mm. Alternate materials may be used for backing plates if equivalency is approved.
The calculations and physical test results must be included in the ASES.

rules.display_text:
Composite TSACs must satisfy the following requirements:
▪ Data obtained from the laminate perimeter shear strength test and three-point bending test, see T 3.6, should be used to prove adequate strength is provided.
▪ Each attachment point requires steel backing plates with a minimum thickness of 2 mm. Alternate materials may be used for backing plates if equivalency is approved.
▪ The calculations and physical test results must be included in the ASES.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: If the TSAC is made from an electrically conductive material, the insulation barrier must be adequately protected against conductive penetrations.

rules.display_text: If the TSAC is made from an electrically conductive material, the insulation barrier must be adequately protected against conductive penetrations.
changelog: Moved from EV5.4 to EV 5.5

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: The TSAC, its mounting to the chassis, and the mounting of each cell to the TSAC must be designed to withstand the accelerations defined in T 3.3.1. All TSAC attachment points must follow EV 5.5.9. TSACs made of materials as stated in EV 5.5.5 or EV 5.5.6 may need further reinforcement to comply with this rule.T 3.2.8 applies if bonded joints are used to fulfill this rule.

rules.display_text: The TSAC, its mounting to the chassis, and the mounting of each cell to the TSAC must be designed to withstand the accelerations defined in T 3.3.1. All TSAC attachment points must follow EV 5.5.9. TSACs made of materials as stated in EV 5.5.5 or EV 5.5.6 may need further reinforcement to comply with this rule.T 3.2.8 applies if bonded joints are used to fulfill this rule.
changelog: Clarified rule

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: The TSAC must be mounted using at least 2 attachment points. T 3.16.5 does not apply to the number of attachment points. Any brackets used must be made of either 1.6 mm thick steel or 4 mm thick aluminium and must have gussets to support bending loads.

rules.display_text: The TSAC must be mounted using at least 2 attachment points. T 3.16.5 does not apply to the number of attachment points. Any brackets used must be made of either 1.6 mm thick steel or 4 mm thick aluminium and must have gussets to support bending loads.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: If any structural part of or in the TSAC is manufactured using additive processes, physical testing must verify compliance with EV 5.5.8. Test samples must be produced on the same machine with identical parameters as the final part. Calculations must account for anisotropic material properties, and all results must be documented in the ASES.

rules.display_text: If any structural part of or in the TSAC is manufactured using additive processes, physical testing must verify compliance with EV 5.5.8. Test samples must be produced on the same machine with identical parameters as the final part. Calculations must account for anisotropic material properties, and all results must be documented in the ASES.
changelog: Clarified rule

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: TS accumulator section, see EV 5.1.4, must be separated by internal vertical walls which extend upwards until the lid. Openings must follow EV 5.5.18.

rules.display_text: TS accumulator section, see EV 5.1.4, must be separated by internal vertical walls which extend upwards until the lid. Openings must follow EV 5.5.18.
changelog: Changed segment to section and phrasing of vertical walls extending up to the lid

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: Pouch cells must be fixed using one or both of the large surfaces only. Each used surface must be fixed on at least 80 %. Tabs of pouch cells must not press into the pouch. The method used for the application of pretension must be documented in the ASES. Any variation in force must be compensated for with compressible materials.

rules.display_text: Pouch cells must be fixed using one or both of the large surfaces only. Each used surface must be fixed on at least 80 %. Tabs of pouch cells must not press into the pouch. The method used for the application of pretension must be documented in the ASES. Any variation in force must be compensated for with compressible materials.
changelog: Added that design must include all states of the cell

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: Any part of the segment in the high current path, see EV 1.2.2, must not carry any mechanical loads.

rules.display_text: Any part of the segment in the high current path, see EV 1.2.2, must not carry any mechanical loads.
changelog: Extended from tabs to entire high current path in the segment

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: Mechanical stress on each cell must not exceed 0.05 MPa shear and 1.0 MPa compression, or the maximum written in the datasheet, whichever is lower, in any state of the cell. This must be calculated using 80 % of the nominal large cell surface area. Proof must be provided in the ASES.

rules.display_text: Mechanical stress on each cell must not exceed 0.05 MPa shear and 1.0 MPa compression, or the maximum written in the datasheet, whichever is lower, in any state of the cell. This must be calculated using 80 % of the nominal large cell surface area. Proof must be provided in the ASES.
changelog: Removed exception for no calculations

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: Friction-based cell mounting requires physical friction testing. Mechanically representative test cells or cell mockups can be used for friction testing.

rules.display_text: Friction-based cell mounting requires physical friction testing. Mechanically representative test cells or cell mockups can be used for friction testing.
changelog: Added consideration of states of cell

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: All fasteners used within or to mount the TSAC must comply with T 10. Fasteners within the TSAC used for non-structural parts, e.g. PCBs, do not have to follow T 10.1.2. Fasteners made of electrically non-conductive material within the TSAC used for non-structural parts do not have to follow T 10.

rules.display_text: All fasteners used within or to mount the TSAC must comply with T 10. Fasteners within the TSAC used for non-structural parts, e.g. PCBs, do not have to follow T 10.1.2. Fasteners made of electrically non-conductive material within the TSAC used for non-structural parts do not have to follow T 10.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: The AIRs and the main fuse, see EV 3.2.7, must be separated with an electrically insulating and fire retardant material, see T 1.2.1, from the TS accumulator, see EV 5.1.5. Air is not considered to be a suitable insulation material in this case.

rules.display_text: The AIRs and the main fuse, see EV 3.2.7, must be separated with an electrically insulating and fire retardant material, see T 1.2.1, from the TS accumulator, see EV 5.1.5. Air is not considered to be a suitable insulation material in this case.
changelog: Clarified rule

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: Holes, both internal and external, in the TSAC, are only allowed for the wiring harness, ventilation, cooling, or fasteners. Holes can extend to the edge of a wall. The TSAC must still be compliant with all other rules, especially the ones concerning its structural requirements. The total cutout area must be below 25 % of the area of the respective single wall. External holes must be sealed according to EV 4.5.

rules.display_text: Holes, both internal and external, in the TSAC, are only allowed for the wiring harness, ventilation, cooling, or fasteners. Holes can extend to the edge of a wall. The TSAC must still be compliant with all other rules, especially the ones concerning its structural requirements. The total cutout area must be below 25 % of the area of the respective single wall. External holes must be sealed according to EV 4.5.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: External openings in the TSAC or mounted ducts must not point toward the driver or the operator of the TS accumulator hand cart. Ducts and their mounting must be fire retardant, see T 1.2.1, and properly sealed.

rules.display_text: External openings in the TSAC or mounted ducts must not point toward the driver or the operator of the TS accumulator hand cart. Ducts and their mounting must be fire retardant, see T 1.2.1, and properly sealed.
changelog: Simplified rule

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: Any TS accumulators that may vent an explosive gas must have a ventilation system to prevent the vented gas from reaching an explosive concentration.

rules.display_text: Any TS accumulators that may vent an explosive gas must have a ventilation system to prevent the vented gas from reaching an explosive concentration.

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: Every TSAC which is completely sealed must have a pressure relief valve to prevent high pressure in the TSAC.

rules.display_text: Every TSAC which is completely sealed must have a pressure relief valve to prevent high pressure in the TSAC.
changelog: Clarified rule

rules.section_title: Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration

blocks.text: A sticker according to “ISO 7010-W012” (triangle with a black lightning bolt on a yellow background) with the triangle side length of at least 100 mm and the text “Always Energized” must be applied on every TSAC. The sticker must also contain the text “High Voltage” if the voltage is more than 60 V DC or 50 V AC RMS.

rules.display_text: A sticker according to “ISO 7010-W012” (triangle with a black lightning bolt on a yellow background) with the triangle side length of at least 100 mm and the text “Always Energized” must be applied on every TSAC. The sticker must also contain the text “High Voltage” if the voltage is more than 60 V DC or 50 V AC RMS.
changelog: Moved rule to end of chapter

blocks.text: At least two AIRs must be fitted inside each TSAC.

rules.display_text: At least two AIRs must be fitted inside each TSAC.

blocks.text: The AIRs must open both poles of the TS accumulator. If the AIRs are open, no TS voltage may be present outside of the TSAC and the vehicle side of the AIRs must be galvanically isolated from the TS accumulator side, see EV 1.2.1.

rules.display_text: The AIRs must open both poles of the TS accumulator. If the AIRs are open, no TS voltage may be present outside of the TSAC and the vehicle side of the AIRs must be galvanically isolated from the TS accumulator side, see EV 1.2.1.

blocks.text: The AIRs must be mechanical relays of a “normally open” type.

rules.display_text: The AIRs must be mechanical relays of a “normally open” type.

blocks.text: A circuit that ensures that the voltage at the vehicle side of the AIRs is pre-charged to at least 95 % of the actual TS accumulator voltage before closing the second AIR must be implemented.

rules.display_text: A circuit that ensures that the voltage at the vehicle side of the AIRs is pre-charged to at least 95 % of the actual TS accumulator voltage before closing the second AIR must be implemented.

blocks.text: The pre-charge circuit must use a mechanical, normally open relay. All pre-charge current must pass through this relay.

rules.display_text: The pre-charge circuit must use a mechanical, normally open relay. All pre-charge current must pass through this relay.

rules.title: Accumulator Management System (AMS)
changelog: Reworked cell temperature measurement requirements

blocks.text: Each TS accumulator must be monitored by an AMS whenever the LVS is active or the TS accumulator is connected to a charger.

rules.display_text: Each TS accumulator must be monitored by an AMS whenever the LVS is active or the TS accumulator is connected to a charger.

blocks.text: Every TSAC must contain its full AMS including its own and AMS exclusive SDC power stage, see EV 6.1

rules.display_text: Every TSAC must contain its full AMS including its own and AMS exclusive SDC power stage, see EV 6.1

blocks.text: The AMS must continuously measure
all cell voltages
the TS current
the temperature of thermally critical cells
for lithium-based cells: the temperature of at least 30 % of the cells equally distributed within the TSAC

rules.display_text:
The AMS must continuously measure
▪ all cell voltages
▪ the TS current
▪ the temperature of thermally critical cells
▪ for lithium-based cells: the temperature of at least 30 % of the cells equally distributed within the TSAC

blocks.text: The maximum cell temperature is 60 °C or the limit stated in the cell datasheet, whichever is lower.

rules.display_text: The maximum cell temperature is 60 °C or the limit stated in the cell datasheet, whichever is lower.

blocks.text: The sensor to measure the cell temperature must be less than 15 mm away from the cell temperature reference point, see EV 5.8.7, measured along the high current path, see EV 1.2.2.

rules.display_text: The sensor to measure the cell temperature must be less than 15 mm away from the cell temperature reference point, see EV 5.8.7, measured along the high current path, see EV 1.2.2.
changelog: Added requirement for max distance for cell temp sensor from reference point

blocks.text: The sensor must be securely mounted and have less than 0.5 mm solid non-metal material, e.g. coating, adhesive, in between the cell temperature sensor and the measuring spot.

rules.display_text: The sensor must be securely mounted and have less than 0.5 mm solid non-metal material, e.g. coating, adhesive, in between the cell temperature sensor and the measuring spot.
changelog: Added requirement for temperature sensor contact

blocks.text: The cell temperature reference point is defined as:
the point of the negative cell terminal surface that is furthest away from the positive terminal along the axis of the cell for cylindric cells.
the point where the negative cell tab exits the pouch for pouch cells.

rules.display_text:
The cell temperature reference point is defined as:
▪ the point of the negative cell terminal surface that is furthest away from the positive terminal along the axis of the cell for cylindric cells.
▪ the point where the negative cell tab exits the pouch for pouch cells.
changelog: Defined a reference point for temperature sensor placement

blocks.text: A single temperature sensor may monitor multiple cells only if the temperature sensor complies with the above stated requirements for all cells it monitors.

rules.display_text: A single temperature sensor may monitor multiple cells only if the temperature sensor complies with the above stated requirements for all cells it monitors.
changelog: Clarified rule

blocks.text: An independent cell temperature monitoring device may be provided by the officials during Accumulator Inspection and must be installed, see IN 3. The device must be placed on the warmest negative cell terminal of the TSAC and in direct contact with the terminal or less than 30 mm away from it on the busbar.

rules.display_text: An independent cell temperature monitoring device may be provided by the officials during Accumulator Inspection and must be installed, see IN 3. The device must be placed on the warmest negative cell terminal of the TSAC and in direct contact with the terminal or less than 30 mm away from it on the busbar.

blocks.text: The AMS must open the SDC, if a critical voltage, temperature, or current value according to the cell manufacturer’s datasheet or these rules persistently occurs for more than:
500 ms for voltage and current values
1 s for temperature values
The accuracy, noise, and sample rate of the measurement must be taken into account.

rules.display_text:
The AMS must open the SDC, if a critical voltage, temperature, or current value according to the cell manufacturer’s datasheet or these rules persistently occurs for more than:
▪ 500 ms for voltage and current values
▪ 1 s for temperature values
The accuracy, noise, and sample rate of the measurement must be taken into account.

blocks.text: AMS cell voltage measurement inputs, temperature measurement inputs, and supply voltage of decentralized AMS slaves may be rated below the maximum TS voltage.

rules.display_text: AMS cell voltage measurement inputs, temperature measurement inputs, and supply voltage of decentralized AMS slaves may be rated below the maximum TS voltage.

blocks.text: A red indicator light in the cockpit that is easily visible from inside and outside the cockpit even in bright sunlight and clearly marked with the lettering “AMS” must light up if and only if the AMS opens the SDC. It must stay illuminated until the error state has been manually reset, see EV 6.1.6. Signals controlling this indicator are SCS, see T 11.9.

rules.display_text: A red indicator light in the cockpit that is easily visible from inside and outside the cockpit even in bright sunlight and clearly marked with the lettering “AMS” must light up if and only if the AMS opens the SDC. It must stay illuminated until the error state has been manually reset, see EV 6.1.6. Signals controlling this indicator are SCS, see T 11.9.

blocks.text: AMS signals are System Critical Signals, see T 11.9. The loss of a measurement connection, that leads to a violation of EV 5.8.3, must result in an open SDC.

rules.display_text: AMS signals are System Critical Signals, see T 11.9. The loss of a measurement connection, that leads to a violation of EV 5.8.3, must result in an open SDC.

blocks.text: It must be possible to interrupt the measurement signal path such that at least one violation for each part of the continuous monitoring of the AMS, see EV 5.8.3, can be individually triggered on all of the segments of the accumulator during Technical Inspection.

rules.display_text: It must be possible to interrupt the measurement signal path such that at least one violation for each part of the continuous monitoring of the AMS, see EV 5.8.3, can be individually triggered on all of the segments of the accumulator during Technical Inspection.
changelog: Clarified rule

blocks.text: The AMS must be able to read and display all measured values according to EV 5.8.3 at any time in a single overview e.g. by connecting a laptop to the AMS.

rules.display_text: The AMS must be able to read and display all measured values according to EV 5.8.3 at any time in a single overview e.g. by connecting a laptop to the AMS.
changelog: Clarified rule

blocks.text: The Shutdown Circuit (SDC) directly carries the power driving the AIRs, see EV 5.6, and the pre-charge circuitry, see EV 5.7.

rules.display_text:
[Figure 21: Explanatory example schematic of the required Shutdown Circuit (SDC) — see figure on page 82]
The Shutdown Circuit (SDC) directly carries the power driving the AIRs, see EV 5.6, and the pre-charge circuitry, see EV 5.7.

blocks.text: The SDC is defined as a series connection of at least two master switches, three shutdown buttons, the BOTS, see T 6.2, the IMD, the inertia switch, see T 11.5, the BSPD, see T 11.6, all required interlocks, and the AMS. An explanatory schematic of the required SDC, excluding any possible interlock circuitry, is shown in Figure 21.

rules.display_text: The SDC is defined as a series connection of at least two master switches, three shutdown buttons, the BOTS, see T 6.2, the IMD, the inertia switch, see T 11.5, the BSPD, see T 11.6, all required interlocks, and the AMS. An explanatory schematic of the required SDC, excluding any possible interlock circuitry, is shown in Figure 21.

blocks.text: All parts of the SDC defined in EV 6.1.2 must be on the high-side connection of the AIR coils and the pre-charge circuitry.

rules.display_text: All parts of the SDC defined in EV 6.1.2 must be on the high-side connection of the AIR coils and the pre-charge circuitry.

blocks.text: The Tractive System Master Switch (TSMS), see EV 6.2, must be the last switch before the AIRs except for pre-charge circuitry and hardwired interlocks.

rules.display_text: The Tractive System Master Switch (TSMS), see EV 6.2, must be the last switch before the AIRs except for pre-charge circuitry and hardwired interlocks.

blocks.text: If the SDC is opened the TS must be shut down by opening all AIRs as well as the pre-charge relay and the voltage in the TS must drop to below 60 V DC and 50 V AC RMS in less than 5 s. All TS accumulator current flow must stop immediately. The action of opening the AIRs may be delayed by ≤250 ms to signal the action to the motor controllers and reduce the TS current before the AIRs are opened. The AIR supply must be abruptly switched off before reaching the minimum AIR supply voltage.

rules.display_text: If the SDC is opened the TS must be shut down by opening all AIRs as well as the pre-charge relay and the voltage in the TS must drop to below 60 V DC and 50 V AC RMS in less than 5 s. All TS accumulator current flow must stop immediately. The action of opening the AIRs may be delayed by ≤250 ms to signal the action to the motor controllers and reduce the TS current before the AIRs are opened. The AIR supply must be abruptly switched off before reaching the minimum AIR supply voltage.

blocks.text: If the SDC is opened by the AMS or the IMD, it has to be latched open by a non-programmable logic that can only be manually reset by a person at the vehicle who is not the driver.

rules.display_text: If the SDC is opened by the AMS or the IMD, it has to be latched open by a non-programmable logic that can only be manually reset by a person at the vehicle who is not the driver.

blocks.text: All circuits that are part of the SDC must be designed in a way, that in the de-energized/ disconnected state, they open the SDC.

rules.display_text: All circuits that are part of the SDC must be designed in a way, that in the de-energized/ disconnected state, they open the SDC.

blocks.text: It must be possible to demonstrate that all features of the SDC function correctly. This includes all interlocks.

rules.display_text: It must be possible to demonstrate that all features of the SDC function correctly. This includes all interlocks.

blocks.text: Every system that is required to or can open the SDC must have its own, non-programmable, power stage to achieve this. The respective power stages must be designed to be able to carry the SDC current, e.g. AIR inrush currents, and such that a failure cannot result in electric power being fed back into the electric SDC.

rules.display_text: Every system that is required to or can open the SDC must have its own, non-programmable, power stage to achieve this. The respective power stages must be designed to be able to carry the SDC current, e.g. AIR inrush currents, and such that a failure cannot result in electric power being fed back into the electric SDC.

blocks.text: The shutdown buttons, the BOTS, the TSMS, and all interlocks must not act through any power stage.

rules.display_text: The shutdown buttons, the BOTS, the TSMS, and all interlocks must not act through any power stage.

blocks.text: All signals influencing the SDC are SCSs, see T 11.9.

rules.display_text: All signals influencing the SDC are SCSs, see T 11.9.

blocks.text: An TSMS according to T 11.2 must be part of the SDC, see EV 6.1.2.

rules.display_text: An TSMS according to T 11.2 must be part of the SDC, see EV 6.1.2.

blocks.text: The TSMS must be fitted with a “lockout/tagout” capability to prevent accidental activation of the TS. The ESO must ensure that it is locked in the off position whenever work is done on the vehicle or no ESO is present.

rules.display_text: The TSMS must be fitted with a “lockout/tagout” capability to prevent accidental activation of the TS. The ESO must ensure that it is locked in the off position whenever work is done on the vehicle or no ESO is present.

blocks.text: The TSMS must be mounted in the middle of a completely orange circular area of ≥50 mm diameter placed on a high contrast background.

rules.display_text: The TSMS must be mounted in the middle of a completely orange circular area of ≥50 mm diameter placed on a high contrast background.

blocks.text: The TSMS must be marked with “TS” and a symbol according to “ISO 7010-W012” (triangle with a black lightning bolt on a yellow background).

rules.display_text: The TSMS must be marked with “TS” and a symbol according to “ISO 7010-W012” (triangle with a black lightning bolt on a yellow background).

blocks.text: Every vehicle must have an IMD installed in the TS system.

rules.display_text: Every vehicle must have an IMD installed in the TS system.

blocks.text: The IMD must be a Bender A-ISOMETER® iso-F1 IR155-3203, −3204, −4203, or −4204, or a Bender ISOMETER® iso165C-1, iso175, or equivalent IMD approved for automotive use. Equivalency may be approved by the officials based on the following criteria: robustness to vibration, operating temperature range, IP rating, availability of a direct output, a self-test facility, and must not be powered by the system that is monitored.

rules.display_text: The IMD must be a Bender A-ISOMETER® iso-F1 IR155-3203, −3204, −4203, or −4204, or a Bender ISOMETER® iso165C-1, iso175, or equivalent IMD approved for automotive use. Equivalency may be approved by the officials based on the following criteria: robustness to vibration, operating temperature range, IP rating, availability of a direct output, a self-test facility, and must not be powered by the system that is monitored.

blocks.text: The response value of the IMD must be set to ≥500 Ω/V, related to the maximum TS voltage.

rules.display_text: The response value of the IMD must be set to ≥500 Ω/V, related to the maximum TS voltage.

blocks.text: The response value must not be changed after Electrical Inspection.

rules.display_text: The response value must not be changed after Electrical Inspection.

blocks.text: The IMD must be connected on the vehicle side of the AIRs.

rules.display_text: The IMD must be connected on the vehicle side of the AIRs.

blocks.text: One IMD chassis ground measurement line must be connected to the grounded TSAC or the respective grounded TS enclosure of the IMD. The other chassis ground measurement line must be connected to the main hoop. Each connection must use a separate conductor, rated for at least maximum TS voltage. An open circuit in any of these ground measurement connections must result in an opened SDC.

rules.display_text: One IMD chassis ground measurement line must be connected to the grounded TSAC or the respective grounded TS enclosure of the IMD. The other chassis ground measurement line must be connected to the main hoop. Each connection must use a separate conductor, rated for at least maximum TS voltage. An open circuit in any of these ground measurement connections must result in an opened SDC.

blocks.text: In case of an insulation failure or an IMD failure, the IMD must open the SDC. This must be done without the influence of any programmable logic. See also EV 6.1.6 regarding the re-activation of the TS after an insulation fault.

rules.display_text: In case of an insulation failure or an IMD failure, the IMD must open the SDC. This must be done without the influence of any programmable logic. See also EV 6.1.6 regarding the re-activation of the TS after an insulation fault.

blocks.text: A red indicator light in the cockpit that is easily visible from inside and outside the cockpit even in bright sunlight and clearly marked with the lettering “IMD” must light up if and only if the IMD opens the SDC. It must stay illuminated until the error state has been manually reset, see EV 6.1.6. Signals controlling this indicator are SCS, see T 11.9.

blocks.text: After Technical Inspection, the only modifications allowed to the vehicle are:
Adjustment of belts, chains and clutches
Adjustment of the brake bias
Adjustment of the driver restraint system, head restraint, seat and pedal assembly
Substitution of the head restraint or seat insert for different drivers
Adjustment to engine operating parameters, e.g. fuel mixture and ignition timing
Adjustment of mirrors
Adjustment of the suspension where no part substitution, other than springs, sway bars and shims, is required
Adjustment of tire pressure
Adjustment of winglet angles, but not the position of the complete aerodynamic device in relation to the vehicle
Replenishment of fluids
Replacement of defective tires or brake pads. Replacement tires and brake pads must be identical in material/composition/size to those presented and approved at Technical Inspection.
Changing wheels and tires for “wet” or “damp” conditions as allowed in D 3.2 and D 7.6
Software calibration changes
Recharging LV batteries
Recharging TS accumulators
(De-)Coupling of actuators and sensor repositioning as allowed in T 14.7
Installing and removing protective sensor covers, if approved during Technical Inspection
Replacement of LV batteries. Replacement LV batteries must be identical and approved at Technical Inspection.
Any other modification must be either approved by or performed under the supervision of Technical Inspection officials.

rules.display_text:
After Technical Inspection, the only modifications allowed to the vehicle are:
▪ Adjustment of belts, chains and clutches
▪ Adjustment of the brake bias
▪ Adjustment of the driver restraint system, head restraint, seat and pedal assembly
▪ Substitution of the head restraint or seat insert for different drivers
▪ Adjustment to engine operating parameters, e.g. fuel mixture and ignition timing
▪ Adjustment of mirrors
▪ Adjustment of the suspension where no part substitution, other than springs, sway bars and shims, is required
▪ Adjustment of tire pressure
▪ Adjustment of winglet angles, but not the position of the complete aerodynamic device in relation to the vehicle
▪ Replenishment of fluids
▪ Replacement of defective tires or brake pads. Replacement tires and brake pads must be identical in material/composition/size to those presented and approved at Technical Inspection.
▪ Changing wheels and tires for “wet” or “damp” conditions as allowed in D 3.2 and D 7.6
▪ Software calibration changes
▪ Recharging LV batteries
▪ Recharging TS accumulators
▪ (De-)Coupling of actuators and sensor repositioning as allowed in T 14.7
▪ Installing and removing protective sensor covers, if approved during Technical Inspection
▪ Replacement of LV batteries. Replacement LV batteries must be identical and approved at Technical Inspection.
Any other modification must be either approved by or performed under the supervision of Technical Inspection officials.

blocks.text: The insulation resistance between the TS and LVS ground is measured. Vehicles are probed with a test voltage based on their maximum TS voltage according to the following table:
To pass this test, the measured insulation resistance must be at least 500 Ω/V related to the maximum TS voltage of the vehicle.

rules.display_text:
The insulation resistance between the TS and LVS ground is measured. Vehicles are probed with a test voltage based on their maximum TS voltage according to the following table:
[Table — see table on page 89]
  Maximum TS Voltage | Test Voltage
  ≤250 V | 250 V
  >250 V to ≤500 V | 500 V
  >500 V | 1000 V
To pass this test, the measured insulation resistance must be at least 500 Ω/V related to the maximum TS voltage of the vehicle.
changelog: Updated insulation test voltage to 1000 V for TS voltage above 500 V and converted requirements to tabular format

blocks.text: The IMD is tested by connecting a resistor between the TSMP, see EV 4.7 and LVS ground connector, see EV 4.7.8. The test is passed if the IMD shuts down the TS within 30 s at a fault resistance of 50 % below the response value which corresponds to 250 Ω/V.

rules.display_text: The IMD is tested by connecting a resistor between the TSMP, see EV 4.7 and LVS ground connector, see EV 4.7.8. The test is passed if the IMD shuts down the TS within 30 s at a fault resistance of 50 % below the response value which corresponds to 250 Ω/V.

blocks.text: The BSPD is tested by sending an appropriate signal that represents the current, to achieve ≤ 5 kW whilst pressing the brake pedal. This test must prove the functionality of the complete BSPD except for any commercially available current sensors. Ends of a current transducer’s auxiliary winding must be insulated.

rules.display_text: The BSPD is tested by sending an appropriate signal that represents the current, to achieve ≤ 5 kW whilst pressing the brake pedal.
