blocks.text: The Tilt Test is conducted with the tallest driver fully strapped in normal driving position.

rules.display_text: The Tilt Test is conducted with the tallest driver fully strapped in normal driving position.

blocks.text: The Tilt Test is conducted with all vehicle fluids at their maximum fill level.

rules.display_text: The Tilt Test is conducted with all vehicle fluids at their maximum fill level.

blocks.text: The vehicle is placed upon the tilt table and to an angle of 60°. There must be no fluid leaks and all wheels must remain in contact with the tilt table surface.

rules.display_text: The vehicle is placed upon the tilt table and to an angle of 60°. There must be no fluid leaks and all wheels must remain in contact with the tilt table surface.

blocks.text: All vehicles must be weighed in ready-to-race condition.

rules.display_text: All vehicles must be weighed in ready-to-race condition.

blocks.text: All fluids must be at their maximum fill level for weighing.

rules.display_text: All fluids must be at their maximum fill level for weighing.

blocks.text: Vehicles must have passed Electrical Inspection, see IN 4, to attempt the Rain Test.

rules.display_text: Vehicles must have passed Electrical Inspection, see IN 4, to attempt the Rain Test.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be in ready-to-race condition. All components and constructions used to protect the vehicle from water during the Rain Test must be used during the entire event. Any fans (if applicable) must be switched on.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must be in ready-to-race condition. All components and constructions used to protect the vehicle from water during the Rain Test must be used during the entire event. Any fans (if applicable) must be switched on.

blocks.text: The TS must be active during the Rain Test.

rules.display_text: The TS must be active during the Rain Test.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be jacked up using the jacks, see T 13.2, and all driven wheels must be removed.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must be jacked up using the jacks, see T 13.2, and all driven wheels must be removed.

blocks.text: The vehicle must not be in R2D mode, see EV 4.11.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must not be in R2D mode, see EV 4.11.

blocks.text: The test is conducted without a driver.

rules.display_text: The test is conducted without a driver.

blocks.text: Water is sprayed at the vehicle from any possible direction. The water spray is similar to a vehicle driving in rain and not a direct high-pressure stream of water.

rules.display_text: Water is sprayed at the vehicle from any possible direction. The water spray is similar to a vehicle driving in rain and not a direct high-pressure stream of water.

blocks.text: The test is passed if the IMD is not triggered and the TS is still active, see EV 4.11.1, while water is sprayed at the vehicle for 120 s and 120 s after the water spray has stopped.

rules.display_text: The test is passed if the IMD is not triggered and the TS is still active, see EV 4.11.1, while water is sprayed at the vehicle for 120 s and 120 s after the water spray has stopped.

blocks.text: The sound level is measured during a static test.

rules.display_text: The sound level is measured during a static test.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be compliant at all engine speeds up to the maximum test speed, see CV 3.2.1.

rules.display_text: The vehicle must be compliant at all engine speeds up to the maximum test speed, see CV 3.2.1.

blocks.text: Teams must bring a laptop to indicate the engine speed measured by the engine control unit.

rules.display_text: Teams must bring a laptop to indicate the engine speed measured by the engine control unit.

blocks.text: Measurements are made with a free-field microphone placed free from obstructions at the exhaust outlet level, 0.5 m from the end of the exhaust outlet, at an angle of 45° with the outlet in the horizontal plane.

rules.display_text: Measurements are made with a free-field microphone placed free from obstructions at the exhaust outlet level, 0.5 m from the end of the exhaust outlet, at an angle of 45° with the outlet in the horizontal plane.

blocks.text: Where more than one exhaust outlet is present, the test is repeated for each exhaust and the highest reading is used.

rules.display_text: Where more than one exhaust outlet is present, the test is repeated for each exhaust and the highest reading is used.

blocks.text: If the exhaust has any form of active tuning or throttling device or system, it must be compliant with the rules in all positions. Manually adjustable tuning devices must require tools to change them and must not be moved or modified after the Noise Test is passed. The position of the device must be visible to the officials and manually operable by the officials during the Noise Test.

rules.display_text: If the exhaust has any form of active tuning or throttling device or system, it must be compliant with the rules in all positions. Manually adjustable tuning devices must require tools to change them and must not be moved or modified after the Noise Test is passed. The position of the device must be visible to the officials and manually operable by the officials during the Noise Test.

blocks.text: The test is run with the gearbox in neutral. During this test the vehicle must be jacked up using the jacks, see T 13.2.

rules.display_text: The test is run with the gearbox in neutral. During this test the vehicle must be jacked up using the jacks, see T 13.2.

blocks.text: After passing the Noise Test the function of the master switch, the cockpit-mounted shutdown button and the inertia switch is tested.

rules.display_text: After passing the Noise Test the function of the master switch, the cockpit-mounted shutdown button and the inertia switch is tested.

blocks.text: After passing IN 10.1.8 the air tightness of the intake system is tested by closing off the inlet after which the engine must stall.

rules.display_text: After passing IN 10.1.8 the air tightness of the intake system is tested by closing off the inlet after which the engine must stall.

blocks.text: Lock all four wheels and stop the vehicle in a substantially straight line at the end of an acceleration run specified by the officials. All four wheels must lock before the vehicle stops; wheels may lock sequentially.

rules.display_text: Lock all four wheels and stop the vehicle in a substantially straight line at the end of an acceleration run specified by the officials. All four wheels must lock before the vehicle stops; wheels may lock sequentially.
changelog: Revised Brake Test wording

blocks.text: [CV ONLY] The vehicle must come to standstill without stalling the engine.

rules.display_text: [CV ONLY] The vehicle must come to standstill without stalling the engine.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] After accelerating, the TS must be switched off by the driver, using the cockpit-mounted shutdown button, and the driver must brake using only the mechanical brakes.

rules.display_text: [EV ONLY] After accelerating, the TS must be switched off by the driver, using the cockpit-mounted shutdown button, and the driver must brake using only the mechanical brakes.

blocks.text: After the Brake Test, the vehicle must be able to continue driving under its own power without external assistance.

rules.display_text: After the Brake Test, the vehicle must be able to continue driving under its own power without external assistance.

blocks.text: The brake light, [EV ONLY] and TSAL, illumination is checked and the officials verify if the illumination is satisfactory for external observation.

rules.display_text: The brake light, [EV ONLY] and TSAL, illumination is checked and the officials verify if the illumination is satisfactory for external observation.

provisions.text: The brake light, [EV ONLY] and TSAL, illumination is checked and the officials verify if the illumination is satisfactory for external observation.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] The R2D sound is checked and the officials verify if the sound level is satisfactory.

rules.display_text: [EV ONLY] The R2D sound is checked and the officials verify if the sound level is satisfactory.

blocks.text: During the Brake Test, tire pressure may be max. 1.0 bar above cold pressure before any dynamic discipline and must never exceed the manufacturer’s limit.

rules.display_text: During the Brake Test, tire pressure may be max. 1.0 bar above cold pressure before any dynamic discipline and must never exceed the manufacturer’s limit.

blocks.text: The EBS performance is tested dynamically and must demonstrate the performance described in T 15.4.

rules.display_text: The EBS performance is tested dynamically and must demonstrate the performance described in T 15.4.

blocks.text: The test is performed in a straight line marked with cones similar to Acceleration.

rules.display_text: The test is performed in a straight line marked with cones similar to Acceleration.

blocks.text: During the Brake Test, the vehicle must accelerate in autonomous mode up to at least 40 km/ h within 20 m. From the point where the RES is triggered, the vehicle must come to a safe stop within a maximum distance that corresponds to the Emergency Brake System Performance requirements according to T 15.4.

rules.display_text: During the Brake Test, the vehicle must accelerate in autonomous mode up to at least 40 km/ h within 20 m. From the point where the RES is triggered, the vehicle must come to a safe stop within a maximum distance that corresponds to the Emergency Brake System Performance requirements according to T 15.4.

blocks.text: In case of wet track conditions, the stopping distance is scaled by the officials dependent on the friction level of the track.

rules.display_text: In case of wet track conditions, the stopping distance is scaled by the officials dependent on the friction level of the track.

blocks.text: The EBS Test is conducted after all other elements of IN 11 have been passed.

rules.display_text: The EBS Test is conducted after all other elements of IN 11 have been passed.

blocks.text: The officials reserve the right to impound any vehicle at any time during or after any of the dynamic disciplines to check for compliance with the rules. If necessary, the vehicle remains with the officials until the violation of the rule has been discussed with the team.

rules.display_text: The officials reserve the right to impound any vehicle at any time during or after any of the dynamic disciplines to check for compliance with the rules. If necessary, the vehicle remains with the officials until the violation of the rule has been discussed with the team.

blocks.text: After Endurance and Trackdrive, the vehicle must be placed in parc fermé where no team member may access the vehicle.

rules.display_text: After Endurance and Trackdrive, the vehicle must be placed in parc fermé where no team member may access the vehicle.

blocks.text: During and after any dynamic discipline, the vehicle must be in compliance with the rules.

rules.display_text: During and after any dynamic discipline, the vehicle must be in compliance with the rules.

blocks.text: For each violation of the rules, the team receives a separate penalty as follows:
Group A: Violation of the rules without advantage for the team
Group B: Violation of the rules with advantage for the team (e.g. aerodynamics)
The penalty applies to all runs since the vehicle entered the dynamic area the last time.

rules.display_text:
For each violation of the rules, the team receives a separate penalty as follows:
▪ Group A: Violation of the rules without advantage for the team
▪ Group B: Violation of the rules with advantage for the team (e.g. aerodynamics)
[Table — see table on page 92]
   | Acceleration | Skidpad | Autocross | Endurance | Trackdrive
  Group A | 0.3 s | 0.2 s | 2 s | 30 s | 30 s
  Group B | 1 s | 0.6 s | 5 s | 2 min | 2 min
The penalty applies to all runs since the vehicle entered the dynamic area the last time.

blocks.text: Violation of the rules concerning safety or the environment (e.g. BOTS, safety harness issues, ground clearance, fluid leaks other than plain water, noise) results in DQ since entering the dynamic area.

rules.display_text: Violation of the rules concerning safety or the environment (e.g. BOTS, safety harness issues, ground clearance, fluid leaks other than plain water, noise) results in DQ since entering the dynamic area.

blocks.text: Losing a part of the vehicle on the track results in DQ for that particular run.

rules.display_text: Losing a part of the vehicle on the track results in DQ for that particular run.

blocks.text: A change in vehicle weight of more than ±5 kg compared to the official Technical Inspection weight, see IN 8, results in 20 penalty points for each kg the tolerance is exceeded by. E.g. a weight difference of ±6.2 kg results in 40 penalty points.

rules.display_text: A change in vehicle weight of more than ±5 kg compared to the official Technical Inspection weight, see IN 8, results in 20 penalty points for each kg the tolerance is exceeded by. E.g. a weight difference of ±6.2 kg results in 40 penalty points.

blocks.text: If the vehicle previously attempted any dynamic discipline in autonomous mode, see T 1.4.2, the vehicle must be able to:
enter “AS Ready”, see T 14.8.3, during Post Inspection after any dynamic discipline that was attempted in manual mode, see T 1.4.1.
fully execute the Inspection Mission, see T 14.10.2, during Post Inspection after any dynamic discipline that was attempted in autonomous mode, see T 1.4.2.
To achieve this, the vehicle may be modified according to IN 1.5.1. Violation results in DQ.

rules.display_text:
If the vehicle previously attempted any dynamic discipline in autonomous mode, see T 1.4.2, the vehicle must be able to:
▪ enter “AS Ready”, see T 14.8.3, during Post Inspection after any dynamic discipline that was attempted in manual mode, see T 1.4.1.
▪ fully execute the Inspection Mission, see T 14.10.2, during Post Inspection after any dynamic discipline that was attempted in autonomous mode, see T 1.4.2.
To achieve this, the vehicle may be modified according to IN 1.5.1. Violation results in DQ.
changelog: Relaxed requirement for inspection mission during Post Inspection

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] The vehicle must be able to enter R2D mode, see EV 4.11, for all tests requiring this mode during Post Inspection. This capability must be maintained under all circumstances for at least 15 min and without any modifications to the vehicle. Violation results in DQ.

rules.display_text: [EV ONLY] The vehicle must be able to enter R2D mode, see EV 4.11, for all tests requiring this mode during Post Inspection. This capability must be maintained under all circumstances for at least 15 min and without any modifications to the vehicle. Violation results in DQ.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] Directly after Endurance and leaving parc fermé, every team must come back to the charging area to disassemble the temperature logging device (if used by the event) from the TS accumulator, see EV 5.8.9.

rules.display_text: [EV ONLY] Directly after Endurance and leaving parc fermé, every team must come back to the charging area to disassemble the temperature logging device (if used by the event) from the TS accumulator, see EV 5.8.9.

blocks.text: Directly after the last dynamic discipline and leaving parc fermé, the data logger (if installed), see EV 4.6 or T 14.2, is disassembled from the vehicle.

rules.display_text: Directly after the last dynamic discipline and leaving parc fermé, the data logger (if installed), see EV 4.6 or T 14.2, is disassembled from the vehicle.

blocks.text: Vehicles must be presented for judging in finished condition, fully assembled, complete and ready-to-race.

rules.display_text: Vehicles must be presented for judging in finished condition, fully assembled, complete and ready-to-race.

blocks.text: The judges will not evaluate any vehicle that is presented in what they consider to be an unfinished state.

rules.display_text: The judges will not evaluate any vehicle that is presented in what they consider to be an unfinished state.

blocks.text: Vehicles may be presented for judging without having passed Technical Inspection, even if final tuning and setup is in progress.

rules.display_text: Vehicles may be presented for judging without having passed Technical Inspection, even if final tuning and setup is in progress.

blocks.text: Covers and/or parts may be removed during the judging to facilitate access and presentation of components or concepts.

rules.display_text: Covers and/or parts may be removed during the judging to facilitate access and presentation of components or concepts.

blocks.text: The objective of the BPP is to assess the team’s ability to develop, present and defend a comprehensive business model in an investment round scenario. The business model must offer a product or a service integrating the team’s specific prototype vehicle or a specific component of it. The business model must be for-profit and provide a rewarding business opportunity. Therefore, non-profit organizations are not permitted.

rules.display_text: The objective of the BPP is to assess the team’s ability to develop, present and defend a comprehensive business model in an investment round scenario. The business model must offer a product or a service integrating the team’s specific prototype vehicle or a specific component of it. The business model must be for-profit and provide a rewarding business opportunity. Therefore, non-profit organizations are not permitted.

blocks.text: The following are not eligible as components of the team’s current prototype vehicle for the creation of the business model:
Consumables and fasteners
Offcuts, scrap, or other by-products arising from the manufacturing process
Tooling or tools used in the manufacturing process
Off-vehicle infrastructure or equipment not permanently integrated into the vehicle
Test, measurement, and calibration equipment not permanently integrated into the vehicle
Personal protective equipment and driver apparel
Standalone services, data, or cloud solutions that do not rely on a team-developed on-vehicle component or software
Using, rebranding, or reselling bought parts without the team’s involvement in design, production, or further processing
Items that are not part of the team’s current prototype vehicle

rules.display_text:
The following are not eligible as components of the team’s current prototype vehicle for the creation of the business model:
▪ Consumables and fasteners
▪ Offcuts, scrap, or other by-products arising from the manufacturing process
▪ Tooling or tools used in the manufacturing process
▪ Off-vehicle infrastructure or equipment not permanently integrated into the vehicle
▪ Test, measurement, and calibration equipment not permanently integrated into the vehicle
▪ Personal protective equipment and driver apparel
▪ Standalone services, data, or cloud solutions that do not rely on a team-developed on-vehicle component or software
▪ Using, rebranding, or reselling bought parts without the team’s involvement in design, production, or further processing
▪ Items that are not part of the team’s current prototype vehicle

blocks.text: During the presentation, teams must explicitly show how they derived their proposed product or service from the team’s current prototype vehicle.

rules.display_text: During the presentation, teams must explicitly show how they derived their proposed product or service from the team’s current prototype vehicle.

blocks.text: The judges should be treated as if they were potential investors or partners for the presented business model. A team may assign the judges specific roles for their BPP, i.e. as representatives of a specific company as strategic investors. Nonetheless, these roles have to allow the judges to pose as potential investors or partners.

rules.display_text: The judges should be treated as if they were potential investors or partners for the presented business model. A team may assign the judges specific roles for their BPP, i.e. as representatives of a specific company as strategic investors. Nonetheless, these roles have to allow the judges to pose as potential investors or partners.

blocks.text: The quality of the actual prototype is not considered as part of the BPP judging, therefore S 1.1 does not apply.

rules.display_text: The quality of the actual prototype is not considered as part of the BPP judging, therefore S 1.1 does not apply.

blocks.text: Presentations are limited to a maximum of 10 min. Anything presented after the 10 min time limit is not considered for the scoring. The judges may stop any presentation exceeding 10 min.

rules.display_text: Presentations are limited to a maximum of 10 min. Anything presented after the 10 min time limit is not considered for the scoring. The judges may stop any presentation exceeding 10 min.

blocks.text: The presentation will not be interrupted by questions. Immediately following the presentation there is a question and answer session.

rules.display_text: The presentation will not be interrupted by questions. Immediately following the presentation there is a question and answer session.

blocks.text: One or more team members may present the business plan.

rules.display_text: One or more team members may present the business plan.

blocks.text: All team members participating in the BPP must be introduced to the judges at the beginning of the presentation. Only team members who were introduced at the beginning and who presented a part of the 10 min presentation may answer the judges’ questions.

rules.display_text: All team members participating in the BPP must be introduced to the judges at the beginning of the presentation. Only team members who were introduced at the beginning and who presented a part of the 10 min presentation may answer the judges’ questions.
changelog: Changed who is eligible to answer the judges’ questions

blocks.text: Handouts, prototypes, or other supporting material may be introduced at any time from the start of the presentation until the end of the Q&A. Such material is only evaluated if explicitly referenced within the presentation or Q&A. All items must be removed by the team after their presentation slot.

rules.display_text: Handouts, prototypes, or other supporting material may be introduced at any time from the start of the presentation until the end of the Q&A. Such material is only evaluated if explicitly referenced within the presentation or Q&A. All items must be removed by the team after their presentation slot.
changelog: Clarified rule

blocks.text: Before the event a specific deep dive topic, which has to be part of the 10 min presentation, is published on the competition website.

rules.display_text: Before the event a specific deep dive topic, which has to be part of the 10 min presentation, is published on the competition website.

blocks.text: To prepare the potential investors or partners for your team’s upcoming presentation, it is required that a Business Plan Executive & Financial Summary (BPEFS) is submitted before the event.

rules.display_text: To prepare the potential investors or partners for your team’s upcoming presentation, it is required that a Business Plan Executive & Financial Summary (BPEFS) is submitted before the event.

blocks.text: Further requirements regarding the BPEFS are published on the competition website on the date specified in the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: Further requirements regarding the BPEFS are published on the competition website on the date specified in the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: The BPEFS must be submitted online in PDF format via the competition website, not later than the deadline specified in the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: The BPEFS must be submitted online in PDF format via the competition website, not later than the deadline specified in the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: The BPP is evaluated on the categories specified in Table 4.

Note: All aspects of the Executive and Financial Summary are only evaluated in the “Executive & Financial Summary” category. Presented content, delivery and demonstration during the Q&A is only evaluated in the “Q&A” categories.

rules.display_text:
The BPP is evaluated on the categories specified in Table 4.
[Table 4: BPP evaluation categories — see table on page 95]
  Category | Points
  Executive & Financial Summary | 10
  Content | 20
  Finances | 15
  Deep Dive Topic | 10
  Demonstration and Structure | 15
  Delivery | 10
  Q&A – Content | 10
  Q&A – Delivery and Demonstration | 5
  General Impression | 5
  Total | 100
Note: All aspects of the Executive and Financial Summary are only evaluated in the “Executive & Financial Summary” category. Presented content, delivery and demonstration during the Q&A is only evaluated in the “Q&A” categories.
changelog: Clarified how Executive and Financial summary is scored

blocks.text: If the business model presented fails to meet any requirement from S 2.1.1 or S 2.1.2, 15 penalty points are deducted from the team’s BPP scoring.

rules.display_text: If the business model presented fails to meet any requirement from S 2.1.1 or S 2.1.2, 15 penalty points are deducted from the team’s BPP scoring.

blocks.text: The judging at the event starts with an initial judging, where all teams are judged by different judging groups.

rules.display_text: The judging at the event starts with an initial judging, where all teams are judged by different judging groups.

blocks.text: Some teams may be chosen to participate in the BPP finals to determine the BPP winner. The BPP finals are held separately from the initial judging and teams are informed about their participation during the event. The requirements of S 2.2.5 also apply to the BPP finals. During the finals, physical supporting material may be displayed or demonstrated on stage but no supporting material must be handed out to the judges.

rules.display_text: Some teams may be chosen to participate in the BPP finals to determine the BPP winner. The BPP finals are held separately from the initial judging and teams are informed about their participation during the event. The requirements of S 2.2.5 also apply to the BPP finals. During the finals, physical supporting material may be displayed or demonstrated on stage but no supporting material must be handed out to the judges.
changelog: Clarified how supporting material is handled during the finals

blocks.text: The scoring of the BPP is based on the average of the scores given by each of the judges.

rules.display_text: The scoring of the BPP is based on the average of the scores given by each of the judges.

blocks.text: The scoring for the non-finalists is calculated as follows:
BPP_SCORE = 65(Pteam Pmax )
Pteam is the score awarded to the team
Pmax is the highest score awarded to any team not participating in the finals

rules.display_text:
The scoring for the non-finalists is calculated as follows:
[Formula: BPP_SCORE = 65(Pteam Pmax )]
Pteam is the score awarded to the team
Pmax is the highest score awarded to any team not participating in the finals
changelog: Reduced maximum points for teams not participating in the finals

blocks.text: The scoring of the BPP finalists varies from 75 to 71 points and is scored immediately after the BPP finals by all judges.

rules.display_text: The scoring of the BPP finalists varies from 75 to 71 points and is scored immediately after the BPP finals by all judges.

rules.title: Cost and Manufacturing
changelog: Removed BOM of entire vehicle but kept CCBOM for selected system(s)

blocks.text: The objective of Cost and Manufacturing is to evaluate the team’s understanding of the manufacturing processes, costs and greenhouse gas emissions associated with the construction of a prototype vehicle. This includes trade off decisions between content and cost, make or buy decisions and understanding the differences between prototype and mass production.

rules.display_text: The objective of Cost and Manufacturing is to evaluate the team’s understanding of the manufacturing processes, costs and greenhouse gas emissions associated with the construction of a prototype vehicle. rules.title: Costed Carbonized Bill of Material (CCBOM)
changelog: Merged former BOM and CCBOM sections into one
Deleted rule about tires because it is no longer applicable

blocks.text: The CCBOM is a sorted list of all parts belonging to the required system(s).

rules.display_text: The CCBOM is a sorted list of all parts belonging to the required system(s).

blocks.text: The CCBOM must:
include the actual associated manufacturing processes for each part as used for the prototype vehicle. This includes the assembly of parts and sub-assemblies as well as the assembly on the vehicle.
include tooling (e.g. welding jigs, molds, patterns and dies).
include the actual costs of materials, fabrication, bought parts and assembly for each part as used for the prototype vehicle.
include the system’s carbon footprint for each part, manufacturing and assembly process of the prototype vehicle in CO2e in kg.

rules.display_text:
The CCBOM must:
▪ include the actual associated manufacturing processes for each part as used for the prototype vehicle. This includes the assembly of parts and sub-assemblies as well as the assembly on the vehicle.
▪ include tooling (e.g. welding jigs, molds, patterns and dies).
▪ include the actual costs of materials, fabrication, bought parts and assembly for each part as used for the prototype vehicle.
▪ include the system’s carbon footprint for each part, manufacturing and assembly process of the prototype vehicle in CO2e in kg.

blocks.text: The CCBOM is structured as follows:
The CCBOM is broken down into the required “system(s)”, see S 3.4.5.
Each “system” is broken down into “assemblies”, which are defined by the website tool.
Each “assembly” can optionally be broken down into “sub-assemblies”, which must be defined by the team.
Each “assembly” or “sub-assembly” is broken down into “parts”, which must be defined by the team.
Each “part” is broken down into
“materials” used (e.g. aluminium)
“processes” that describe the necessary steps for manufacturing
“fasteners” used to assemble the part (if applicable)
“tooling” required for manufacturing (if applicable)
“overhead” for additional associated costs and emissions of manufacturing and assembly of a part that are not covered by the points above

rules.display_text:
The CCBOM is structured as follows:
▪ The CCBOM is broken down into the required “system(s)”, see S 3.4.5.
▪ Each “system” is broken down into “assemblies”, which are defined by the website tool.
▪ Each “assembly” can optionally be broken down into “sub-assemblies”, which must be defined by the team.
▪ Each “assembly” or “sub-assembly” is broken down into “parts”, which must be defined by the team.
▪ Each “part” is broken down into
  ▪ “materials” used (e.g. aluminium)
  ▪ “processes” that describe the necessary steps for manufacturing
  ▪ “fasteners” used to assemble the part (if applicable)
  ▪ “tooling” required for manufacturing (if applicable)
  ▪ “overhead” for additional associated costs and emissions of manufacturing and assembly of a part that are not covered by the points above

blocks.text: The CCBOM must list all parts belonging to the required system(s) that are fitted to the prototype vehicle at any time during the event.

rules.display_text: The CCBOM must list all parts belonging to the required system(s) that are fitted to the prototype vehicle at any time during the event.

Chassis and Body

Engine and Tractive System
Grounded Low Voltage System
Miscellaneous, Fit and Finish
Steering System
Suspension System
Wheels, Wheel Bearings and Tires

rules.display_text:

blocks.text: When adding “parts” to the CCBOM, the comments section should be reviewed thoroughly. The chosen part name must clearly describe what is included. For example, if a spring is included, the “part” should not be called “damper”.

rules.display_text: When adding “parts” to the CCBOM, the comments section should be reviewed thoroughly. The chosen part name must clearly describe what is included. For example, if a spring is included, the “part” should not be called “damper”.

blocks.text: Each constituent “part” of an “assembly” must be classified as “bought” or “made”.

rules.display_text: Each constituent “part” of an “assembly” must be classified as “bought” or “made”.

blocks.text: A modified bought part is considered a made part, where the bought part acts as the material. Associated “processes”, “tooling”, “fasteners” and “overhead” (if applicable) for the modifications must be included. However, the “carbon footprint” of the bought part itself should not be considered.

rules.display_text: A modified bought part is considered a made part, where the bought part acts as the material. Associated “processes”, “tooling”, “fasteners” and “overhead” (if applicable) for the modifications must be included. However, the “carbon footprint” of the bought part itself should not be considered.

blocks.text: Only parts that can be bought from a catalog may be designated as “bought parts”.

rules.display_text: Only parts that can be bought from a catalog may be designated as “bought parts”.

blocks.text: For “bought parts”, only fasteners have to be included in the emissions calculation (if applicable). Fasteners themselves are not considered bought parts.

rules.display_text: For “bought parts”, only fasteners have to be included in the emissions calculation (if applicable). Fasteners themselves are not considered bought parts.
changelog: Removed redundant sentence

blocks.text: “Fasteners” are additional items necessary to assemble a “part” or “(sub-)assembly”.
Examples for “fasteners”: DIN-931 hexagon screws, glue, zip ties, tape used for mounting or fixing, …
Examples that are considered “parts” and not “fasteners”: Tape used for edge protection, safety wire, …

rules.display_text:
“Fasteners” are additional items necessary to assemble a “part” or “(sub-)assembly”.
▪ Examples for “fasteners”: DIN-931 hexagon screws, glue, zip ties, tape used for mounting or fixing, …
▪ Examples that are considered “parts” and not “fasteners”: Tape used for edge protection, safety wire, …

blocks.text: A self-manufactured “fastener” is considered a “part”.

rules.display_text: A self-manufactured “fastener” is considered a “part”.

blocks.text: “Tooling” is the necessary tools used for transforming the “material” into the desired shape. If production tooling is associated with processes that are specific to the part geometry, it must be included. For example the dies to stamp out a chassis bracket are tooling.

rules.display_text: “Tooling” is the necessary tools used for transforming the “material” into the desired shape. If production tooling is associated with processes that are specific to the part geometry, it must be included. For example the dies to stamp out a chassis bracket are tooling.

blocks.text: Hand or power tools must not be included.

rules.display_text: Hand or power tools must not be included.

blocks.text: “Processes” are the operations necessary to produce the “part” out of the “material” as well as the steps needed for assembly.

rules.display_text: “Processes” are the operations necessary to produce the “part” out of the “material” as well as the steps needed for assembly.

blocks.text: Only metric units must be used within the CCBOM.

rules.display_text: Only metric units must be used within the CCBOM.

blocks.text: The cost calculations must be completed as realistically as possible and exclude research, development and capital expenditures for real estate (e.g. plant or development hours of the team).

rules.display_text: The cost calculations must be completed as realistically as possible and exclude research, development and capital expenditures for real estate (e.g. plant or development hours of the team).

blocks.text: All costs must be displayed in EUR. For calculating the prices in EUR from other currencies, the team must provide the exchange rates used.

rules.display_text: All costs must be displayed in EUR. For calculating the prices in EUR from other currencies, the team must provide the exchange rates used.

blocks.text: There is no maximum cost. Receipts are not required for any items.

rules.display_text: There is no maximum cost. Receipts are not required for any items.

blocks.text: The “carbon footprint” is calculated in CO2e based on a “Cradle-to-Gate” Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of the selected “system(s)”.

rules.display_text: The “carbon footprint” is calculated in CO2e based on a “Cradle-to-Gate” Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of the selected “system(s)”.

blocks.text: The “Cradle-to-Gate” analysis includes extraction of raw materials needed, manufacturing of “made parts”, “sub-assemblies”, “assemblies” and the “system” as well as the mounting into the final prototype vehicle.

rules.display_text: The “Cradle-to-Gate” analysis includes extraction of raw materials needed, manufacturing of “made parts”, “sub-assemblies”, “assemblies” and the “system” as well as the mounting into the final prototype vehicle.

rules.display_text: Checkered Flag — the session has been completed. The driver must exit the track at the first opportunity.

blocks.text: Green Flag —

The session has started, the driver may enter the track under direction of the track marshals. In case of stalling, the vehicle can be restarted, but the driver has to await another Green Flag as the opening in traffic may have closed.
The driver is clear to re-enter the track after using the slow lane to let a faster vehicle pass.
The driver may pick up speed again after a Yellow Flag has been displayed.

rules.display_text:
Green Flag —
▪ The session has started, the driver may enter the track under direction of the track marshals. In case of stalling, the vehicle can be restarted, but the driver has to await another Green Flag as the opening in traffic may have closed.
▪ The driver is clear to re-enter the track after using the slow lane to let a faster vehicle pass.
▪ The driver may pick up speed again after a Yellow Flag has been displayed.

blocks.text: Red Flag — the driver must come to an immediate safe and controlled stop on the track and must follow track marshals’ directions.

rules.display_text: Red Flag — the driver must come to an immediate safe and controlled stop on the track and must follow track marshals’ directions.

blocks.text: Yellow Flag — danger, the driver must slow down, something has happened beyond the flag station, no overtaking unless directed by the track marshals.

rules.display_text: Yellow Flag — danger, the driver must slow down, something has happened beyond the flag station, no overtaking unless directed by the track marshals.

blocks.text: Red And Yellow Striped Flag — the track is slippery or something is on the racing surface that should not be there. The driver must be prepared for evasive maneuvers to avoid the situation.

rules.display_text: Red And Yellow Striped Flag — the track is slippery or something is on the racing surface that should not be there. The driver must be prepared for evasive maneuvers to avoid the situation.

blocks.text: After the vehicle has crossed the starting line it is prohibited to change parameters, send commands or perform any software changes by wireless communication until the vehicle has crossed the finish line. Receiving information from the vehicle via one-way-telemetry is allowed.

rules.display_text: After the vehicle has crossed the starting line it is prohibited to change parameters, send commands or perform any software changes by wireless communication until the vehicle has crossed the finish line. Receiving information from the vehicle via one-way-telemetry is allowed.

blocks.text: The only device that is allowed to send commands by wireless communication at all times is the RES described in T 14.3.

rules.display_text: The only device that is allowed to send commands by wireless communication at all times is the RES described in T 14.3.

blocks.text: During driving, the mechanical integrity of the vehicle must be maintained.

rules.display_text: During driving, the mechanical integrity of the vehicle must be maintained.

blocks.text: Vehicles must not be driven in reverse.

rules.display_text: Vehicles must not be driven in reverse.

blocks.text: The vehicle must be capable of starting and restarting without external assistance/batteries at all times.

rules.display_text: Push starts are prohibited.

blocks.text: Burnouts before and during the dynamic disciplines are prohibited.

rules.display_text: Burnouts before and during the dynamic disciplines are prohibited.

blocks.text: When driving in autonomous mode, an ASR has to be present at the race control with the RES. Additionally, a single monitoring device (laptop, tablet, …) may be brought (no complicated antenna construction or similar!).

blocks.text: If a vehicle comes to standstill for any reason, it may have up to 30 s to attempt to continue to drive. If the vehicle doesn’t restart within 30 s, it is disqualified.

rules.display_text: If a vehicle comes to standstill for any reason, it may have up to 30 s to attempt to continue to drive. If the vehicle doesn’t restart within 30 s, it is disqualified.

blocks.text: If the average speed of the first three laps in Trackdrive (after completing the third lap) is below 2.5 m/s or the average speed of any of the following laps is below 3.5 m/s, the vehicle is disqualified.

rules.title: Procedure After Completing a Driverless (DV) Dynamic Discipline

Procedure After Completing a Driverless (DV) Dynamic Discipline

blocks.text: After approval from the officials the ASR has to deactivate the vehicle using the RES.

blocks.text: A re-run may be granted in following cases:
Usage of Yellow Flag in Autocross.
Usage of Red Flag.
Usage of RES to ensure safe conditions on the track or traceable signal loss of the RES according to D 2.6.
After official’s decision due to technical or organizational issues.

blocks.text: The Skidpad track consists of two pairs of concentric circles in a figure of eight pattern.

rules.display_text: The Skidpad track consists of two pairs of concentric circles in a figure of eight pattern.

blocks.text: The centers of these circles are 18.25 m apart. The inner circles are 15.25 m in diameter and the outer circles are 21.25 m in diameter.

rules.display_text: The centers of these circles are 18.25 m apart. The inner circles are 15.25 m in diameter and the outer circles are 21.25 m in diameter.

blocks.text: 17 cones are placed around the inside of each inner circle. 13 cones are positioned around the outside of each outer circle, in the pattern shown in the Skidpad layout diagram.

rules.display_text: 17 cones are placed around the inside of each inner circle. 13 cones are positioned around the outside of each outer circle, in the pattern shown in the Skidpad layout diagram.

blocks.text: Each circle is marked with a line, outside the inner circle and inside the outer circle.

rules.display_text: Each circle is marked with a line, outside the inner circle and inside the outer circle.

blocks.text: The driving path is the 3 m wide path between the inner and outer circles. The vehicles enter and exit through gates on a 3 m wide path that is tangent to the circles where they meet.

rules.display_text: The driving path is the 3 m wide path between the inner and outer circles. The vehicles enter and exit through gates on a 3 m wide path that is tangent to the circles where they meet.

blocks.text: The line between the centers of the circles defines the start/finish line. A lap is defined as traveling around one of the circles, starting and ending at the start/finish line.

rules.display_text:
The line between the centers of the circles defines the start/finish line. A lap is defined as traveling around one of the circles, starting and ending at the start/finish line.

blocks.text: A run consists of a sequence of laps in exactly the following order. The vehicle must enter perpendicular to the figure of eight and must take one full lap on the right circle to establish the turn. The next lap must be on the right circle and is timed. Immediately following the second lap, the vehicle must enter the left circle for the third lap. The fourth lap must be on the left circle and is timed. Immediately upon finishing the fourth lap, the vehicle must exit the track perpendicular to the figure of eight and moving in the same direction as entered.

rules.display_text: A run consists of a sequence of laps in exactly the following order. The vehicle must enter perpendicular to the figure of eight and must take one full lap on the right circle to establish the turn. The next lap must be on the right circle and is timed. Immediately following the second lap, the vehicle must enter the left circle for the third lap. The fourth lap must be on the left circle and is timed. Immediately upon finishing the fourth lap, the vehicle must exit the track perpendicular to the figure of eight and moving in the same direction as entered.

blocks.text: The run time is the average time of the timed left and the timed right circle plus penalties which are added after the averaging.

rules.display_text: The run time is the average time of the timed left and the timed right circle plus penalties which are added after the averaging.

blocks.text: The Autocross track layout is a handling track built to the following guidelines:
Straights: No longer than 80 m
Slaloms: Cones in a straight line with 7.5 m to 12 m spacing
Miscellaneous: Chicanes, multiple turns, decreasing radius turns, hairpin turns, etc.
The minimum track width is 3 m
The minimum required turning diameter according to D 1.1.10 is 9 m

▪ Straights: No longer than 80 m

▪ Miscellaneous: Chicanes, multiple turns, decreasing radius turns, hairpin turns, etc.
▪ The minimum track width is 3 m
▪ The minimum required turning diameter according to D 1.1.10 is 9 m

blocks.text: Before entering the discipline, each CV’s fuel tank must be filled to the fuel level line, see CV 2.6.4, at the fueling station. During fueling, once filled to the scribe line, no shaking or tilting of the tank, the fuel system or the entire vehicle is allowed.

rules.display_text: A run consists of multiple laps driven by two different drivers.

blocks.text: The first driver drives for approximately 11 km and is then signaled into the driver change area.

rules.display_text: After the driver change specified in D 7.5, the second driver drives for an additional approximately 11 km and is signaled to exit the track after crossing the finish line.

blocks.text: Each lap of Endurance is individually timed. The corrected elapsed time is determined by subtracting the extra-long lap for the driver change from the total time and adding any penalty times.

rules.display_text: Each lap of Endurance is individually timed. The corrected elapsed time is determined by subtracting the extra-long lap for the driver change from the total time and adding any penalty times.

blocks.text: The running order for Endurance is established in a way that vehicles with similar speeds are on the track together.

rules.display_text: The running order for Endurance is established in a way that vehicles with similar speeds are on the track together.

blocks.text: During Endurance, overtaking is only permissible in the designated passing zones and under the control of the track marshals.

rules.display_text: During Endurance, overtaking is only permissible in the designated passing zones and under the control of the track marshals.

blocks.text: Passing zones have two parallel lanes, a slow lane only used by the vehicles that are being overtaken and a fast lane for the vehicles that are overtaking.

rules.display_text: Passing zones have two parallel lanes, a slow lane only used by the vehicles that are being overtaken and a fast lane for the vehicles that are overtaking.

blocks.text: Passing zones may be situated on either the left or right of the fast lane.

rules.display_text: Passing zones may be situated on either the left or right of the fast lane.

blocks.text: The passing zone procedure is as follows:
A slower leading vehicle is shown the Blue Flag and must drive into the slow lane and decelerate.
The following faster vehicle continues in the fast lane to pass the slow vehicle.
The vehicle that has been overtaken may re-enter the track when the track marshal who is in charge of that passing zone is showing the Green Flag.

rules.display_text:
The passing zone procedure is as follows:
▪ A slower leading vehicle is shown the Blue Flag and must drive into the slow lane and decelerate.
▪ The following faster vehicle continues in the fast lane to pass the slow vehicle.
▪ The vehicle that has been overtaken may re-enter the track when the track marshal who is in charge of that passing zone is showing the Green Flag.

blocks.text: The passing rules do not apply to vehicles that are stopped on track or vehicles that have spun out and are not moving. When passing a stationary vehicle, it is critical to slow down, drive cautiously and to follow the instructions from the track marshals.

rules.display_text: The passing rules do not apply to vehicles that are stopped on track or vehicles that have spun out and are not moving. When passing a stationary vehicle, it is critical to slow down, drive cautiously and to follow the instructions from the track marshals.

blocks.text: Only three team members including the drivers may enter the driver change area. They may only bring the tools required to adjust the vehicle to accommodate the second driver and/or change tires.

rules.display_text: Only three team members including the drivers may enter the driver change area. They may only bring the tools required to adjust the vehicle to accommodate the second driver and/or change tires.

perform changes to accommodate the second driver
operate the master switch(es)
change tires as per D 7.6.

rules.display_text: Wheel-to-wheel racing is prohibited.

blocks.text: If a vehicle stalls out on the track, it is allowed one lap by the vehicle that is following it (approximately one minute) to restart.

rules.display_text: If a vehicle stalls out on the track, it is allowed one lap by the vehicle that is following it (approximately one minute) to restart.

blocks.text: If a vehicle has a restart problem at the driver change or after a Red Flag, it is allowed 2 min to restart the engine or to enter R2D. The 2 min start from the time the driver first tries to restart the engine or to enter R2D. The time is added to the Endurance time.

rules.display_text: If a vehicle has a restart problem at the driver change or after a Red Flag, it is allowed 2 min to restart the engine or to enter R2D. The 2 min start from the time the driver first tries to restart the engine or to enter R2D. The time is added to the Endurance time.

blocks.text: If restarts are not accomplished within the above times, the vehicle is disqualified for the run.

rules.display_text: If restarts are not accomplished within the above times, the vehicle is disqualified for the run.

blocks.text: If a vehicle breaks down it is removed from the track and is not allowed to re-enter the track.

rules.display_text: If a vehicle breaks down it is removed from the track and is not allowed to re-enter the track.

blocks.text: Team members may be instructed by the officials to retrieve broken down vehicles. This recovery may only be carried out under the control of the officials.

rules.display_text: Team members may be instructed by the officials to retrieve broken down vehicles. This recovery may only be carried out under the control of the officials.

rules.title: Endurance Restart Procedure After Red Flag
rules.section_title: Endurance Restart Procedure After Red Flag
Endurance Restart Procedure After Red Flag

blocks.text: When the cause of the Red Flag has been rectified, all vehicles on the track are guided to the driver change area under Yellow Flag in order to receive further instructions from the officials.

rules.display_text: When the cause of the Red Flag has been rectified, all vehicles on the track are guided to the driver change area under Yellow Flag in order to receive further instructions from the officials.

rules.section_title: Endurance Restart Procedure After Red Flag

blocks.text: The lap in which the Red Flag occurred is completely ignored for Endurance and Efficiency scoring and repeated after the restart.

rules.display_text: The lap in which the Red Flag occurred is completely ignored for Endurance and Efficiency scoring and repeated after the restart.

blocks.text: Efficiency is measured during Endurance.

rules.display_text: Efficiency is measured during Endurance.

blocks.text: Only vehicles which scored minimum Pmin points in Endurance are considered for Efficiency scoring.

rules.display_text: Only vehicles which scored minimum Pmin points in Endurance are considered for Efficiency scoring.

blocks.text: [CV ONLY] Fuel pumps must be on and fuel valves must be opened during refueling.

rules.display_text: [CV ONLY] Fuel pumps must be on and fuel valves must be opened during refueling.

blocks.text: [CV ONLY] The measured fuel mass of vehicles using E85 fuel is divided by 1.45 to be comparable to the vehicles using 98 RON.

rules.display_text: [CV ONLY] The measured fuel mass of vehicles using E85 fuel is divided by 1.45 to be comparable to the vehicles using 98 RON.

blocks.text: [EV ONLY] The Endurance energy is calculated as the time integrated value of the measured voltage multiplied by the measured current logged by the data logger, see EV 4.6. Regenerated energy is multiplied by 0.9 and subtracted from the used energy.

rules.display_text: [EV ONLY] The Endurance energy is calculated as the time integrated value of the measured voltage multiplied by the measured current logged by the data logger, see EV 4.6. Regenerated energy is multiplied by 0.9 and subtracted from the used energy.

blocks.text: The Trackdrive layout is a closed loop circuit built to the following guidelines:
Straights: No longer than 80 m
Miscellaneous: Chicanes, multiple turns, decreasing radius turns, hairpin turns, etc.
The minimum track width is 3 m
The minimum required turning diameter according to D 1.1.10 is 9 m

rules.display_text:
The Trackdrive layout is a closed loop circuit built to the following guidelines:
▪ Straights: No longer than 80 m
▪ Miscellaneous: Chicanes, multiple turns, decreasing radius turns, hairpin turns, etc.
▪ The minimum track width is 3 m
▪ The minimum required turning diameter according to D 1.1.10 is 9 m

blocks.text: The length of one lap is approximately 200 m to 500 m.

rules.display_text: The length of one lap is approximately 200 m to 500 m.

blocks.text: The running order is defined by the officials, based on previous dynamic discipline results.

rules.display_text: The running order is defined by the officials, based on previous dynamic discipline results.

blocks.text: The running order is published according to the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: The running order is published according to the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: The procedure for handling the running order is defined in the Event Handbook.

rules.display_text: The procedure for handling the running order is defined in the Event Handbook.

blocks.text: A run consists of ten laps.

rules.display_text: A run consists of ten laps.

blocks.text: The vehicle is staged such that the front wheels are 6 m in front of the starting line on the track.

rules.display_text: The vehicle is staged such that the front wheels are 6 m in front of the starting line on the track.

blocks.text: After ten laps, the foremost part of the vehicle must come to a full stop within 30 m behind the finish line, all four wheels must remain within the track boundaries and the vehicle must enter the finish-state described in T 14.8.

rules.display_text: After ten laps, the foremost part of the vehicle must come to a full stop within 30 m behind the finish line, all four wheels must remain within the track boundaries and the vehicle must enter the finish-state described in T 14.8.

blocks.text: There is no last lap signal i.e. the vehicle should count laps itself.

rules.display_text: There is no last lap signal i.e. the vehicle should count laps itself.

blocks.text: Each lap of Trackdrive is individually timed. The corrected elapsed time is determined by adding any penalty times.

rules.display_text: Each lap of Trackdrive is individually timed. The corrected elapsed time is determined by adding any penalty times.

blocks.text: Points are given based on the following formula:
SCORE = (𝑃max −𝑃min)(𝑇max −𝑇team 2 ) + 𝑃min 𝑇max −𝑇min
with
𝑃max is the maximum points for the discipline according to Table 1
𝑃min is the minimum points for the discipline according to Table 9
𝑇team is the team’s best time including penalties. 𝑇team is capped to 𝑇max.
𝑇max is defined in Table 9.
𝑇min is the time of the fastest vehicle including penalties.

blocks.text: Points for Autocross are given based on the following formula:
AUTOCROSS_SCORE = 0.9𝑃max(𝑇max −𝑇team, total ) + 0.1𝑃max 𝑇max −𝑇min 𝑇team, total = min(𝑇team,1, avg(𝑇team,1, 𝑇team,2))
𝑃max is the maximum points for the discipline according to Table 1.
𝑇team,1 is the team’s autonomous mode time including penalties of run 1.
𝑇team,2 is the team’s autonomous mode time including penalties of run 2.
𝑇max is the time for driving the lap with 6 m/s.
𝑇min is the fastest autonomous mode 𝑇team, total of all teams.
For runs that are DNF or DQ or for runs with a 𝑇team,i above 𝑇max, 𝑇team,i is set to 𝑇max.

rules.display_text:
Points for Autocross are given based on the following formula:
[Formula: AUTOCROSS_SCORE = 0.9𝑃max(𝑇max −𝑇team, total ) + 0.1𝑃max 𝑇max −𝑇min 𝑇team, total = min(𝑇team,1, avg(𝑇team,1, 𝑇team,2))]
𝑃max is the maximum points for the discipline according to Table 1.
𝑇team,1 is the team’s autonomous mode time including penalties of run 1.
𝑇team,2 is the team’s autonomous mode time including penalties of run 2.
𝑇max is the time for driving the lap with 6 m/s.
𝑇min is the fastest autonomous mode 𝑇team, total of all teams.
For runs that are DNF or DQ or for runs with a 𝑇team,i above 𝑇max, 𝑇team,i is set to 𝑇max.

blocks.text: Points for Trackdrive are given based on the following formula:
TRACKDRIVE_SCORE = 0.75𝑃max( 𝑇max −1) 𝑇team
Pmax is the maximum points for the discipline according to Table 1.
Tteam is the team’s corrected elapsed time. Tteam is capped at Tmax.
Tmax is 2 times of the corrected elapsed time of the fastest vehicle.

rules.display_text:
Points for Trackdrive are given based on the following formula:

blocks.text: In deviation of D 1.1.9, an additional 2.5 % of the maximum points for the discipline according to Table 1 are given for every completed lap.

rules.display_text: In deviation of D 1.1.9, an additional 2.5 % of the maximum points for the discipline according to Table 1 are given for every completed lap.

blocks.text: Points for Efficiency are given based on the following formula:
2 EFFICIENCY_SCORE = 𝑃max(EFmax −EFteam ) EFmax −EFmin
𝑃max is the maximum points for the Efficiency according to Table 1
EFteam the team’s Efficiency Factor
EFmin the lowest Efficiency Factor of all teams which are considered for Efficiency
EFmax is defined as 2 ⋅EFmin
For runs with an EFteam above EFmax, EFteam is set to EFmax.

blocks.text: Penalties are not assessed for accident avoidance or other reasons deemed sufficient by the officials.

rules.display_text: Penalties are not assessed for accident avoidance or other reasons deemed sufficient by the officials.

blocks.text: A cone is Down or Out (DOO) if the cone has been knocked over or the entire base of the cone lies outside the box marked around the cone in its undisturbed position.

rules.display_text: A cone is Down or Out (DOO) if the cone has been knocked over or the entire base of the cone lies outside the box marked around the cone in its undisturbed position.

blocks.text: Cones that are DOO are not replaced/reset during autonomous running. There is no re-run due to cones in the driving path or disorientation due to missing cones.

rules.display_text: Cones that are DOO are not replaced/reset during autonomous running. There is no re-run due to cones in the driving path or disorientation due to missing cones.

blocks.text: The DOO penalty, see D 10.1.7, is added for each DOO including entry and exit gate cones before the start and after the finish line, that occur on that particular run.

rules.display_text: The DOO penalty, see D 10.1.7, is added for each DOO including entry and exit gate cones before the start and after the finish line, that occur on that particular run.

blocks.text: Off-Course (OC)
An OC occurs when the vehicle has all four wheels outside the track boundary as indicated by edge marking.
Missing one or more gates of a given slalom at Autocross or Endurance is counted as one OC per occurrence.
When an OC occurs, the driver must re-enter the track at the next possible point.
When re-entering the driver needs to wait for a gap and follow the instructions of the track marshals.

rules.display_text:
Off-Course (OC)
▪ An OC occurs when the vehicle has all four wheels outside the track boundary as indicated by edge marking.
▪ Missing one or more gates of a given slalom at Autocross or Endurance is counted as one OC per occurrence.
▪ When an OC occurs, the driver must re-enter the track at the next possible point.
▪ When re-entering the driver needs to wait for a gap and follow the instructions of the track marshals.

blocks.text: An Unsafe Stop (USS) is defined as not stopping within the specified area and/or not maintaining the expected orientation while stopping and/or not entering the finish-state described in T 14.8 within 30 s after stopping during autonomous running.

rules.display_text: An Unsafe Stop (USS) is defined as not stopping within the specified area and/or not maintaining the expected orientation while stopping and/or not entering the finish-state described in T 14.8 within 30 s after stopping during autonomous running.

[Table — see table on page 114]
   | Acceleration | Skidpad | Autocross | Endurance | Trackdrive
  DOO | 2 s | 0.2 s | 2 s | 2 s | 2 s
  OC | DQ | DQ | 10 s | 10 s | 10 s
  USS | DQ | DQ | DQ | n/a | −50 points

blocks.text: Failure to obey a flag: 1 min time penalty.

rules.display_text: Failure to obey a flag: 1 min time penalty.

blocks.text: Reckless or aggressive driving or “Over Driving”: Black Flag, see D 2.1.3.

rules.display_text: Reckless or aggressive driving or “Over Driving”: Black Flag, see D 2.1.3.

blocks.text: Vehicle to vehicle contact: 2 min up to DQ depending on the nature of the incident.

rules.display_text: Vehicle to vehicle contact: 2 min up to DQ depending on the nature of the incident.

blocks.text: If a vehicle is not able to start the run, within 30 s after receiving a Green Flag or go-signal, the vehicle is DQ for that run.

rules.display_text: If a vehicle is not able to start the run, within 30 s after receiving a Green Flag or go-signal, the vehicle is DQ for that run.

blocks.text: Teams that are running out-of-order as defined in the Event Handbook, are penalized by 2 min and may then run at the discretion of the officials.

rules.display_text: Teams that are running out-of-order as defined in the Event Handbook, are penalized by 2 min and may then run at the discretion of the officials.

blocks.text: Mechanical Problem: The time taken for Mechanical Inspection under a Black Flag With Orange Dot, see D 2.1.4, is considered officials’ time and is not included in the team’s total time. If the inspection reveals a mechanical integrity problem the vehicle is disqualified.

rules.display_text: Mechanical Problem: The time taken for Mechanical Inspection under a Black Flag With Orange Dot, see D 2.1.4, is considered officials’ time and is not included in the team’s total time. If the inspection reveals a mechanical integrity problem the vehicle is disqualified.

blocks.text: If it is impossible to impose a penalty by a stop under a Black Flag, e.g. not enough laps left, the officials may add an appropriate time penalty to the team’s elapsed time.

rules.display_text: If it is impossible to impose a penalty by a stop under a Black Flag, e.g. not enough laps left, the officials may add an appropriate time penalty to the team’s elapsed time.

blocks.text: A team may be disqualified if their vehicle is too slow or being driven without proper control. A vehicle is considered to be too slow if the average speed, based on lap times, for two consecutive laps is below 8 m/s in dry conditions or below 5 m/s in wet or damp conditions.

rules.display_text: A team may be disqualified if their vehicle is too slow or being driven without proper control. A vehicle is considered to be too slow if the average speed, based on lap times, for two consecutive laps is below 8 m/s in dry conditions or below 5 m/s in wet or damp conditions.

blocks.text: Any violation to the procedure of driver change, see D 7.5.3, leads to a time penalty of up to 2 min.

rules.display_text: Any violation to the procedure of driver change, see D 7.5.3, leads to a time penalty of up to 2 min.

blocks.text: All rules and penalties from IN 12 are also applicable during driver change.

rules.display_text: All rules and penalties from IN 12 are also applicable during driver change.

blocks.text: Should the fuel level change after refueling due to effects such as described in CV 2.7.1, the difference in fuel level is measured and twice the amount is added to the official fuel consumption figure.

rules.display_text: Should the fuel level change after refueling due to effects such as described in CV 2.7.1, the difference in fuel level is measured and twice the amount is added to the official fuel consumption figure.
